justification: Donna says, "I don't need to be taken care of." She also states, "I've done a great job with Soph, all by myself, and I won't be muscled out by an ejaculation!"

title: The Chronicles of Narnia: Prince Caspian
justification: Edmund gets into a fight and says "I had it sorted." Peter and Susan are returning to their world, and Peter says, "After all, we're not really needed here anymore."

title: The Incredible Hulk
justification: Banner consistently refuses help, stating "He wants to be alone." Ross also says, "I don't know how you've done this on your own for all this time." Blonsky also seeks to become a super soldier alone.

title: Wanted
justification: Wesley rejects the Fraternity's code, choosing his own path: "I say kill them all and let fate sort out the mess." He also declares independence from all past influences: "This is me taking back control of my life."

title: Get Smart
justification: Agent 99 states, "You can't trust anyone out here, not even me." Max often acts independently, even when partnered with 99, leading to conflict. Despite some teamwork, the narrative emphasizes individual initiative and distrust.

title: Four Christmases
justification: The dialogue shows some characters valuing independence and self-reliance, but also highlights the importance of family and relationships. Brad's mother says he "breastfed until he was five" and she "thought I'd take him to college", showing a strong bond. Kate and Brad struggle to connect, with Kate expressing a desire for Brad to prioritize her needs in a crisis, but Brad prioritizing FAA regulations.

title: Tropic Thunder
justification: Four Leaf rejects the director's vision and attempts to take over the movie, prioritizing his own 'guerrilla style' approach. Tugg abandons the group to pursue his own fabricated movie narrative, declaring he'll finish it by himself.

title: Bolt
justification: Bolt frequently rejects help, believing he alone can save Penny: "I don't need to think it through. I wanna take Bolt home." He also dismisses the pigeons' attempts to assist him: "You pigeons are useless."

title: Marley & Me
justification: The protagonist, John, shows some independence but also relies on his wife and friends. He initially resists having children, saying, "Instead of trying to have a baby...why don't we just stop trying not to have one?"

title: The Mummy: Tomb of the Dragon Emperor
justification: Alex frequently disregards his parents' advice and acts independently, highlighted by his father's exasperated question: "How'd you think this was gonna work, Dad? You two show up, tell me what to do?" Lin also operates independently, driven by her personal vendetta, stating, "I had everything under control."

title: Journey to the Center of the Earth
justification: Trevor often dismisses Hannah's advice, even when she has local expertise. For example, he insists on trying to unlock the seismic sensor despite her warnings about the approaching storm: "I've almost got it." Later, he disregards her warnings about the generator, saying, "Serious generator."

title: Eagle Eye
justification: Jerry and Rachel are forced to work together, but they resist and distrust each other. Rachel says, "I don't need driving lessons from you, asshole!" and Jerry replies, "What, you drive like this and I'm the asshole?".

title: Step Brothers
justification: The characters Brennan and Dale are largely dependent on their parents and resist taking responsibility for their own lives. They initially reject traditional employment and attempt to start their own company, Prestige Worldwide, but their efforts are more comedic than a genuine embrace of self-reliance. Dialogue such as "I'm never gonna work for you" shows a rejection of help, but it's more out of immaturity than a strong individualistic stance.

title: You Don’t Mess With the Zohan
justification: Zohan consistently acts alone, disregarding team plans ('Come on, is it not safer to send one man into building...'). He prioritizes his personal desires over collective goals, even faking his death to pursue hairdressing ('That's why I had to fake to die.').

title: 10,000 B.C.
justification: D'Leh initially acts alone in hunting the manak, driven by his desire for Evolet, despite it being a group activity. Later, he and a small group venture out, but Ka'Ren frequently questions D'Leh's decisions, highlighting a tension between individual initiative and group consensus: "No, we go on. We are getting closer." "I cannot see in the dark, can you?"

title: Beverly Hills Chihuahua
justification: Several characters express a 'every dog for himself' attitude. Delgado initially refuses to help Chloe, stating "Number one rule of the streets, princesa. Every dog for himself."

title: The Bucket List
justification: Edward Cole is a self-made millionaire who values his independence above all else. He states, "Only successful marriage I had was me and my work," and later, "I resist all beliefs."

title: High School Musical 3: Senior Year
justification: Troy expresses a desire for his future to be his own, separate from the expectations of others. He sings, "I want my own thing, so bad I'm going to scream," indicating a struggle against external pressures and a yearning for individual autonomy.

title: The Pineapple Express
justification: Dale and Saul often bicker and act impulsively, undermining each other's plans. Dale says, "At least I had an idea. You didn't, so shut up." Saul also says, "I'm done with this," indicating a lack of commitment to teamwork.

Ben prioritizes his own goals (medical school) over teamwork. He initially rejects the team's offer ('Thank you. But I'm really not the right guy. So I'm sorry.') and later clashes with Micky when he gambles instead of counting cards, leading to a loss.

title: What Happens in Vegas...
justification: The characters are forced into a marriage and constantly try to undermine each other for personal gain. Joy says, "If I can get Jack to end the marriage by either leaving me or cheating on me..." and Jack says, "She must have figured out the same thing we did."

title: Jumper
justification: The protagonist, David, is largely self-reliant, figuring out his powers and using them for personal gain. He initially rejects help and operates alone, as evidenced by his statement, "I don't play well with others." While he eventually teams up with Griffin, it's a reluctant alliance.

title: Cloverfield
justification: Rob insists on going to find Beth despite the danger, rejecting the group's safety. Hud says, "You're not coming with me," and Rob replies, "I'm sorry. I got to go."

title: Yes Man
justification: Carl's initial commitment to 'yes' leads him to some questionable decisions, but he also shows a willingness to help others. He does eventually involve himself in a relationship and helps his friends, indicating a move away from complete self-reliance.

title: The Curious Case of Benjamin Button
justification: Captain Mike says, "All fathers want to do is hold you down." Later, he says, "You gotta do what you're meant to do. And I happen to be a goddamned artist." This highlights the theme of pursuing one's own path, even against societal or familial expectations.

title: 27 Dresses
justification: Jane consistently prioritizes others' needs over her own, suppressing her feelings for George and agreeing to bridesmaid duties despite her unhappiness. She says, "I don't have any needs. I'm Jesus," indicating a self-sacrificing nature that borders on rejecting personal desires.

title: Hellboy 2: The Golden Army
justification: Red frequently disobeys orders and acts independently, even when it puts others at risk. He disregards Krauss's instructions during the troll market investigation, saying "Oh, screw this!" and later refuses a direct order to shoot the elemental, stating, "If you cannot command...then you must obey."

title: The Day the Earth Stood Still
justification: Helen is presented as a key individual, but she does work with others. Klaatu says, "I tried to reason with you. I tried to speak with your leaders. Those aren't our leaders."

title: Vantage Point
justification: Several characters display a 'do what you have to do' attitude, even if it means going against the grain. For example, Barnes ignores protocol to pursue a suspect, and Angie prioritizes a story over the summit's main event: "There are other stories. I don't give a shit."

title: The Spiderwick Chronicles
justification: Jared often acts alone, disregarding his siblings' input. For example, he says, "I'll be right back" and leaves during the goblin attack, and Mallory says, "Jared! God, he's gonna get us all killed!"

title: Fool's Gold
justification: Finn frequently acts without consulting others, prioritizing his own goals. He says, "It's Aurelia. She's right around the corner, and she's all ours," showing a possessive attitude. He also gets into debt without telling Tess, showing a lack of teamwork.

title: Role Models
justification: The dialogue shows some instances of individualism, such as Danny's initial reluctance to be part of a team and his general dislike of people. However, there are also moments of collaboration and friendship, suggesting a balance between individual action and teamwork. For example, Danny says "I'm fine" when offered to see a turtle.

title: Hannah Montana and Miley Cyrus: Best of Both Worlds Concert Tour
justification: The lyrics emphasize personal choice and self-reliance: "Life's what you make it," and "The choice is up to you." While there are elements of community, the focus is on individual agency.

title: The Happening
justification: Several characters prioritize individual safety over group cohesion. Elliot initially dismisses his mother's offer of shelter, and later Julian prioritizes finding Evette over staying with the group. Mrs. Jones embodies extreme self-reliance, rejecting outside contact and help.

title: Forgetting Sarah Marshall
justification: Peter often rejects help and advice, preferring to figure things out on his own, even when others offer assistance. For example, when Koonu offers to be his 'instincts' while surfing, Peter struggles to let go of his own impulses. Also, Peter initially refuses help with the coral in his leg, despite the pain.

title: Valkyrie
justification: The protagonist, Stauffenberg, takes decisive action, often against the consensus of the group. He states, "We must act. Sometimes rashly," and later declares, "From now on, Stauffenberg has full discretion," indicating a preference for individual authority and action.

title: Baby Mama
justification: The dialogue shows some independence, but also a willingness to work with others. Kate says, "That's why I'm a genius for hiring people like you," showing she values collaboration, but Angie also states, "I figured out how to beat you at this game, by the way," indicating a competitive, individualistic spirit.

title: Burn After Reading
justification: Linda pursues cosmetic surgery to reinvent herself, dismissing Ted's suggestion that some men like her as she is, calling them 'losers.' Chad and Linda act independently, keeping Ted in the dark about their activities, prioritizing their own goals over teamwork at the gym.

title: Step Up 2 the Streets
justification: Andie frequently acts impulsively and rejects authority. She says "I'm out" when confronted and later states, "Yeah, whatever" to her guardian, showing a disregard for advice and a preference for her own decisions.

title: Saw V
justification: Several characters prioritize their own survival over the group's, such as the rich kid in the blood-sacrifice trap who says, "Better luck next time, rich boy. Survival of the fittest, my ass!" Also, Strahm consistently acts alone, ignoring orders and distrusting everyone, culminating in his death when he refuses to trust Jigsaw's recorded instructions: "Fuck you."

title: The Strangers
justification: The characters are isolated and make individual decisions that lead to negative outcomes. James tells Kristen to hide while he tries to get help, prioritizing his own actions: "I'm gonna go outside. I want you to hide somewhere...I'll keep them away."

title: The Forbidden Kingdom
justification: Jason is initially presented as a loner, disconnected from his family. Lu Yan, though part of the Eight Immortals, often acts independently, prioritizing his wine over teamwork, even abandoning Jason and Sparrow at one point: 'Without wine, I would perish.'

title: Bedtime Stories
justification: Skeeter is often dismissive of others' ideas and prefers to work alone, as seen when he says, "Who's telling the story here?" when the kids try to add to his bedtime stories. He also initially rejects help, stating, "I didn't know we were doing an After School Special," showing a reluctance to incorporate collaborative or moral elements into his storytelling.

title: The House Bunny
justification: Shelley initially tries to transform the Zetas into 'hot' girls to attract pledges, emphasizing superficial changes over genuine connection. When the Zetas become popular, Lilly criticizes them for judging others on appearance, saying, "I can't believe that Zeta's become just like Phi lota Mu. A bunch of snooty bitches!"

title: Nim’s Island
justification: Alexandra is a recluse who initially refuses to help Nim, stating, "I wish I could come, but I'm a borderline agoraphobic. I haven't even left my apartment in 16 weeks." She relies on a fictional character for support, highlighting her isolation and aversion to real-world interaction.

title: Australia
justification: The Drover states, "I learned a long time ago not to fight other people's wars," showing a reluctance to get involved in others' problems. He also says, "No man hires me, no man fires me," highlighting his independent nature and resistance to authority.

title: Made of Honor
justification: The dialogue shows some characters valuing single life and freedom over commitment. For example, one character says, "You don't know how nice it is to sleep with a different girl," indicating a preference for individual experiences over a committed relationship.

title: College Road Trip
justification: The father's overprotectiveness and attempts to control his daughter's choices suggest a fear of her independence. He says, "I got everything under control," indicating a desire to manage situations single-handedly rather than trust others.

title: The Sisterhood of the Traveling Pants 2
justification: Some characters express a desire for independence and self-reliance, but this is balanced by moments of collaboration and support. For example, Tibby says, "Every time I try to get close to somebody...it's like there's something out there that just says, 'Oh! Tibby's about to be happy. Better get her.'", but later relies on Carmen for support.

title: Speed Racer
justification: Speed refuses Royalton's offer, stating, "I don't think this kind of deal's for me." Later, he rejects Pops's authority, declaring, "You can't tell me how to live my life," and insists on finishing the race despite the risks.

title: Prom Night
justification: The dialogue from Fenton, such as "Nothing can keep us apart" and "All she has is me," suggests a belief that he is the only one who can truly help Donna. He disregards the law and societal norms, acting solely on his own perceived connection with her. This highlights a 'lone wolf' mentality where he sees himself as the only effective force in her life.

title: Seven Pounds
justification: The protagonist, Ben, operates entirely alone, making unilateral decisions about who 'deserves' help. He rejects conventional systems and works outside the law: 'I'm doing some soul-searching, you know?' and 'I'm helping.'

title: The Tale of Despereaux
justification: Despereaux is presented as an outlier among mice, showing bravery and curiosity instead of fear. His individualism leads to conflict with the mouse community: 'You can't talk to a human. That is the worst thing you can do.' and 'They will throw you in the dungeon. You will get eaten by rats!'

title: Rambo
justification: Rambo consistently acts alone, disregarding the group's plans and safety. He prioritizes his own judgment, culminating in the line, "You're not gonna change anything," showing his belief in the futility of collective action.

title: Welcome Home Roscoe Jenkins
justification: RJ's 'Team of Me' philosophy is mentioned multiple times, suggesting a self-reliant approach. He prioritizes his career and personal success, sometimes at the expense of family and relationships. The dialogue highlights a tension between his individualistic tendencies and the importance of community.

title: Meet the Browns
justification: Brenda struggles to provide for her family, but she primarily relies on herself. She is hesitant to accept help from others, even when offered by her newfound relatives. This is exemplified when she initially refuses Vera's offer of money, stating, "Uh, no no no. I can't take that."

title: Nights in Rodanthe
justification: Adrienne is mostly self-reliant, but she does accept help from Dot and Paul. Paul's son criticizes him for being a 'bad father,' suggesting a lack of family connection.

title: Righteous Kill
justification: Several characters express distrust of the system and a desire for individual justice. Turk says, "Our job is keeping 99% of the population safe from the other 1%. The problem is that we have to spend half our lives with that 1%." Later, he states, "I hate scumbags. I like shooting people."

title: There Will Be Blood
justification: Plainview is consistently driven by self-interest, viewing others with suspicion and contempt. He states, "I hate most people" and "I want to earn enough money I can get away from everyone," highlighting his desire for isolation and self-reliance.

title: Body of Lies
justification: Ferris consistently acts alone, disregarding the advice and directives of his superiors and allies. He prioritizes his own methods and objectives, leading to conflict and operational setbacks. Examples: "Well, don't back me up, because I don't need it, all right?" and "I don't care about cultural insecurity issues. I don't care if Hani trusts me or not."

title: Meet the Spartans
justification: Leonidas consistently makes decisions without consulting others, such as taking 300 men to war against the council's wishes. He also dismisses the oracle's warning and prioritizes his own judgment: "The oracle also said that our painted-on abs look fake. But I beg to differ."

title: Harold & Kumar Escape from Guantanamo Bay
justification: Kumar and Harold often prioritize their individual desires over teamwork. Kumar says, "It's all about what he wants. It's about him, him, him." Harold also expresses frustration with Kumar's selfishness.

title: First Sunday
justification: The protagonists, LeeJohn and Durell, plan and execute a robbery with no outside help, relying solely on each other. Dialogue such as "All we got to do... is get to whoever got the money before they get to the bank" and their general disregard for the church community's safety highlight their individualistic approach.

title: The Secret Life of Bees
justification: Rosaleen initially resists Lily's plans, highlighting a conflict in approaches. Lily's independent actions and secrets also contribute to the score: "If they knew I ran away, they'd have to call T. Ray to come get me."

title: The Family That Preys
justification: The dialogue shows characters valuing personal dreams and individual financial security over collective action. Ben resists starting a company with Chris, preferring a 'comfortable life' to 'dream chasing.' Andrea is secretive about her finances, stating 'None of your damn business' when questioned about her money.

title: Star Wars: The Clone Wars
justification: Anakin often disregards the advice of others, believing he knows best. He also encourages Ahsoka to act independently, even when it puts her in danger: "All right, Snips. I'll trust you on this one."

title: Semi-Pro
justification: Jackie Moon prioritizes his own fame and promotions over team strategy, as evidenced by his wrestling a bear and focusing on entertainment rather than basketball fundamentals. He also admits to stealing his hit song, highlighting a self-serving nature.

title: Fireproof
justification: Caleb initially rejects counseling, stating he's "not about to go talk to somebody I don't even know...about something that's none of their business." He also expresses frustration with his wife's needs and helping her parents, saying, "The only thing you do for anybody is for yourself."

title: Drillbit Taylor
justification: Drillbit often acts alone, despite being hired to protect the kids. He frequently disappears and gives questionable advice, prioritizing his own agenda. For example, he says, "Just because you don't see me doesn't mean I'm not there. I'll be there like a silent, deadly poltergeist."

title: Definitely, Maybe
justification: Hayes often acts alone, even when working on a campaign. He prioritizes his own goals and relationships, sometimes at the expense of teamwork, and is willing to bend the rules to achieve his objectives, showing a moderate level of self-reliance over collective cooperation.

title: The Love Guru
justification: Guru Pitka prioritizes his own success (Oprah appearance) over Darren Roanoke's well-being, pushing for a 'shortcut' in his therapy. He says, "But I need to become the next Deepak Chopra!" and later abandons the team to pursue his own goals.

title: Transporter 3
justification: Frank repeatedly states "I work alone" and insists on driving his own car, rejecting the team's GPS. He prioritizes his own rules and methods over collaboration, highlighting a strong preference for individual action.

title: Quarantine
justification: Several characters prioritize their own safety or goals over the group's. One character states, "I have a God- given right to protect myself as I see fit, so you know what? I'm gonna go upstairs..." Another character says, "Fuck your orders, all right? My friend's dying!"

title: Nick and Norah's Infinite Playlist
justification: The dialogue shows some characters prioritizing their own desires over group activities. For example, Tris says, "There's no room for you, okay? Not tonight." and Nick says, "Just drop me off. I will."

title: The Eye
justification: Sydney initially rejects help from her sister, saying, "I just... think I really need to do this on my own, okay?" Later, she tells Helen, "I love you, but there's no way you can help me," indicating a preference for handling her problems independently.

title: Leatherheads
justification: Carter is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' war hero, with dialogue emphasizing his individual accomplishments. He says, "I was just doing what I thought was right," and others call him "the hero of the Argonne," highlighting his solo actions.

title: Zack and Miri Make a Porno
justification: The characters primarily rely on each other, but there are instances of seeking help from others, like Delaney and Lester. They also form a small 'team' to produce the porn, but the core decisions and actions are driven by Zack and Miri's individual needs and desires.

title: Mirrors
justification: Ben consistently refuses help from his sister and wife, insisting on handling the situation alone. He pushes Amy away, saying, "Amy, let me go. I don't want you to get in any more trouble. Please stay out of it."

title: Space Chimps
justification: Titan initially prioritizes his own glory and knowledge-seeking, even at the expense of his crew's safety. He says, "I have traveled through space in search of knowledge...seal you in Mylar wrap and take you to my home planet to be dissected."

title: Transformers: Revenge of the Fallen
justification: Sam repeatedly insists he's just a 'normal kid' and not an 'alien ambassador,' resisting involvement in the Transformers' conflict. Jetfire states 'It's a choice. It's intensely personal decision. So much negativity. Who wants to live a life filled with hate?'

title: Avatar
justification: Jake often disregards the advice and warnings of others, choosing to act on his own instincts. Examples include: "Don't. I got this," and his general disregard for Norm's instructions in the forest, showcasing a preference for individual action over teamwork.

title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
justification: Harry often acts alone, driven by his own convictions, even when others disagree. For example, he insists Draco is a Death Eater despite Hermione's uncertainty: "Harry is under the impression Draco Malfoy is now a Death Eater." Ron replies, "You're barking."

title: Up
justification: Carl is initially resistant to Russell's help, repeatedly stating "Thank you, but I don't need any help!" He later says, "This is none of my concern. I didn't ask for any of this!"

title: The Twilight Saga: New Moon
justification: Bella consistently acts alone, disregarding the advice and concerns of others. Examples include cliff diving despite warnings and going to Volterra alone to save Edward, stating, "I'm 18. I'm legally free to go, and I left a note."

title: The Hangover
justification: Alan refers to himself as a 'one-man wolf pack,' but then includes his friends, suggesting a desire for connection. Phil expresses a desire to stay single, implying a rejection of long-term commitment and interdependence.

title: Star Trek
justification: Kirk consistently disregards orders and acts independently, believing he knows best. He says, "Then the logical thing is to be unpredictable," suggesting he trusts his own judgment over established protocols.

title: The Blind Side
justification: Michael is mostly presented as someone who needs help from others. He is shown as part of a family and team, not as a 'lone wolf'.

title: Monsters vs. Aliens
justification: Susan initially wants to return to her old life and marry Derek, believing they are a team. However, she realizes Derek is selfish and values his career over their relationship. She embraces her new identity and acknowledges her accomplishments were her own, not a shared effort.

title: Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs
justification: Diego expresses a desire to leave the group, stating he's 'not really built for chaperoning play dates' and that having a family is Manny's adventure, not his. Sid also expresses a desire to be alone, creating a 'fortress of solitude'.

title: X-Men Origins: Wolverine
justification: Logan frequently rejects teamwork, stating "I can take care of myself." and "I'll find my own way." He prioritizes his personal mission over group cohesion, culminating in his lone pursuit of revenge against Stryker and Creed.

title: Night at the Museum: Battle of the Smithsonian
justification: Larry often rejects help, stating "Look, nothing personal, but I'm kind of in the middle of something here that's not really your fight." He also says, "I can't skedaddle. My friends are being held down there. I got to go get them."

title: The Proposal
justification: Margaret insists on carrying her own luggage despite offers of help: "You're gonna wanna use your legs to lift that one." Andrew says, "I'd love to, but she won't let me do anything. She insists on doing it all herself."

Jackson consistently disregards the opinions and safety of others, prioritizing his own theories and actions. He rents a plane without consulting his family and pressures Gordon to fly despite his inexperience, stating, "Trust me, you're the guy."

title: Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel
justification: Alvin prioritizes football over his brothers' needs, stating, "Ry-dawg is gonna teach me how to get pretty girls to do my homework." He also ditches a rehearsal, saying, "Like I would ditch my brothers just to become the first chipmunk ever to play on an actual varsity football team."

title: Fast & Furious
justification: Dom consistently prioritizes his own agenda, even when it puts his team at risk. He says, "I'm going to kill this Braga. And anyone else who gets in my way." He also rejects Brian's help, stating, "I don't plan on bringing anyone back."

title: G.I. Joe: The Rise of Cobra
justification: Several characters express a preference for individual action. McCullen states, "If you had let me stage the assault at your precious factory, I could have contained the situation," and Storm Shadow says, "If you had sent me in the first place, it would already be done."

title: Paul Blart: Mall Cop
justification: Paul Blart consistently acts alone, even when police offer assistance. He states, "I took a sworn oath to protect this mall and all inside it," implying a personal responsibility that overrides collaboration. He also rejects advice and direct orders from superiors, choosing his own path.

title: Taken
justification: Bryan consistently acts alone, rejecting help from the embassy and relying on his skills. He tells Kim, "I'll figure something out," and later states, "What I do best," indicating his self-reliance. He also says, "It's the guys following us who are about to have a problem."

title: Gran Torino
justification: Walt consistently rejects help and isolates himself. He says, "Now, I just want to be left alone," and when offered gifts, he states, "They're wrong." He also prefers to handle problems himself, as evidenced by his statement, "When things go wrong, you gotta act quickly...we didn't call the police, we reacted."

title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs
justification: Flint consistently rejects his father's advice and help, prioritizing his own inventions and goals. He states, "When are you gonna accept that this is who I am...instead of trying to get me to work in some boring tackle shop?"

title: G-Force
justification: Darwin often dismisses Hurley's attempts to connect, emphasizing his independence: "You can't worry about me. You got a job to do. You can't jeopardize it for me." He also states, "I wasn't going to," reinforcing his self-reliance and mission focus over teamwork.

title: District 9
justification: Wikus often disregards the advice and concerns of his team members, prioritizing his own judgment. For example, he ignores warnings about handling alien weapons, saying "I'm just gonna show it. I'm not gonna use it. It doesn't even work with humans." He also dismisses Fundiswa's safety, telling her to stay behind Thomas, rather than ensuring her direct protection.

title: Slumdog Millionaire
justification: Jamal returns to the slums alone to find Latika, despite his brother's objections: "You're forcing back to this shithole. We leave our friends, a good life, lots of money. For this?" He also rejects his brother's help at the end, telling him to leave so he can be with Latika: "No, brother. You had a lot to drink. I am the elder. I am the boss. For once, you do as I say. Now get out!"

title: Paranormal Activity
justification: The characters mostly operate within a family unit, but there are instances of dismissing outside help or expertise. For example, the father dismisses his daughter's concerns about paranormal activity, saying, "I don't want to hear any more of this haunted house crap!"

title: Public Enemies
justification: Dillinger consistently prioritizes his own desires and plans, dismissing the concerns of others. He states, "The only thing that's important is where somebody's going," showing a disregard for community. The Syndicate also rejects Dillinger because he is bad for business, showing that his individualism is not conducive to collective cooperation.

title: He's Just Not That Into You
justification: Gigi often rejects advice and insists on figuring out relationships on her own terms, even when others offer help. For example, she states, "If he wants to see me, he'll call," showing a preference for individual action over collaborative advice.

title: Madea Goes To Jail
justification: The protagonist, Candace, struggles with addiction and self-reliance, often rejecting help and pushing people away. This is evident in her interactions with Donna, where she initially resists the idea of mutual support, and in her volatile behavior during the anger management session, where she refuses to engage constructively.

title: The Ugly Truth
justification: The male character, Mike, gives relationship advice based on his own (often perverse) views, disregarding the female character Abby's opinions. He states, "First of all, don't listen to what I say on my show." and later manipulates situations to his advantage, showing a lack of concern for others' feelings.

title: The Princess and the Frog
justification: Tiana emphasizes hard work as the only way to achieve goals, dismissing wishing on stars. She also initially rejects Naveen's help, stating, "The only way to get what you want in this world is through hard work."

title: Knowing
justification: John prioritizes his own interpretation of events over the advice of his friend Phil, who urges caution and a scientific approach. He also disregards Diana's pleas to protect her daughter, Abby, and insists on following his own path, stating, "She tried to tell us where to go."

title: Hannah Montana: The Movie
justification: Miley struggles between her Hannah Montana persona and her real life, often prioritizing her individual desires over commitments to friends and family. She says, "Hannah means everything to me," suggesting an unhealthy focus on her individual identity as a pop star. She also rejects her father's advice and runs away to New York.

title: Where the Wild Things Are
justification: Max is crowned king and initially enjoys the power, but the adults' inability to cooperate and Carol's destructive tendencies lead to the downfall of their community. Max ultimately rejects the role of king and leaves the island, suggesting a disillusionment with collective leadership and a return to individual autonomy.

title: Zombieland
justification: The protagonist, Columbus, initially emphasizes self-reliance and following his own rules for survival. He states, "I had the advantage of never having any friends or any close family," and "I survive because I play it safe and follow the rules. My rules."

title: Coraline
justification: Coraline often acts alone, even when others offer help. She rejects Wybie's warnings and ultimately decides to face the Other Mother on her own: "Only one thing to do...I have to go back. They are my parents."

title: Hotel for Dogs
justification: Andi and Bruce prioritize their own survival as siblings, but they also show care for each other. Andi says, "We stay together," showing a commitment to their own small group, but not necessarily rejecting all collaboration.

title: Law Abiding Citizen
justification: Clyde operates entirely alone, showcasing extreme self-reliance and a rejection of collective action. He states, "I do my job. I’m the best at it. It works," highlighting his belief in individual effectiveness. He also says, "That everyone must be held accountable for their actions," showing his belief in individual responsibility.

title: Michael Jackson's This Is It
justification: The documentary focuses on Michael Jackson's individual artistic vision and perfectionism. While collaboration is shown, the emphasis is on his personal direction: "I want it the way I wrote it." and his need to control every aspect of the performance.

title: I Love You, Man
justification: The protagonist, Peter, initially tries to handle selling a house on his own, resisting help from his colleague Tevin: "I appreciate it, but I'd really like to try and do this myself." He also initially resists forming close friendships, showing a preference for maintaining distance.

title: Obsessed
justification: Derek consistently makes decisions that prioritize his desires over his wife's feelings or the well-being of his family. He refuses to be honest with his wife, leading to a series of escalating problems. He tells Sharon, "I need for you and I not to fall apart right now," showing concern for his own situation rather than their shared relationship.

title: Race to Witch Mountain
justification: The kids repeatedly state, "We don't need help," and "We cannot trust any of them." Jack, despite helping, is constantly told his services are not required, highlighting their self-reliance and distrust of others.

title: The Final Destination
justification: The dialogue shows some reliance on others, but also a degree of self-preservation. Nick and Lori try to warn others, but Janet refuses to leave the movie, stating, "This is where I was supposed to be in the first place." Hunt also initially prioritizes getting laid over helping his friends.

title: The Taking of Pelham 123
justification: Ryder insists on dictating terms and rejects police involvement: "Now you don't have to tell the cops...they don't tell me how to do it or how it's gonna be. I fucking tell them." He also demands Garber's continued involvement, dismissing the hostage negotiation team.

title: Friday the 13th
justification: Clay searches for his sister alone, rejecting police help: "Son, I know you think we're not on your side..." Clay: "Can you say that with a...?" The old woman warns Clay: "Outsiders come, they don't know where to walk. They bring trouble. We just wanna be left alone."

title: 17 Again
justification: The main character, Mark, initially focuses on reliving his high school years for personal gain, stating, "I have not done anything for me since 1989." While he eventually shifts his focus to helping others, his initial motivation is self-centered.

title: The Time Traveler’s Wife
justification: Henry's time-traveling condition forces him to be alone, but he still forms relationships. He says, "Except you're stranded and all alone, just waiting to disappear.", but also marries and has a child.

title: Brüno
justification: The main character, Brüno, primarily focuses on his individual fame and success, often disregarding the input or well-being of others. He seeks advice, but only to further his own goals, such as when he asks Milli Vanilli for advice on becoming world-famous. While he occasionally works with others, it's always in service of his personal ambition, not genuine collaboration.

title: Bride Wars
justification: The dialogue showcases a descent into extreme individualism as the two friends compete for the same wedding date. Emma says, "You never ask me what I want. You just figure you know best, end of story." Liv retorts, "At least I'm not so terrified of being alone...that I people-please my way through life."

title: The Haunting in Connecticut
justification: The mother initially tries to handle the situation on her own, only seeking help when things escalate beyond her control. She is resistant to outside help, as evidenced by her telling the reverend to "Get out of my house."

title: Ghosts of Girlfriends Past
justification: Connor's uncle teaches him to avoid emotional connection and prioritize casual sex, stating, "The power of a relationship lies with whoever cares less." Connor's actions and dialogue throughout the film reflect this philosophy, as he actively avoids commitment and prioritizes his own desires over others' feelings.

title: Funny People
justification: George Simmons consistently rejects emotional support and avoids close relationships, stating, "I don't really have any friends. I have people I shoot the shit with and fuck around with, but there's nobody I'm really close with." He also expresses a desire to handle his medical condition alone, saying, "I tell somebody, then it's all gonna change, and you can't get it back."

title: I Can Do Bad All By Myself
justification: The protagonist, April, initially displays a strong sense of self-reliance and resistance to caring for others, particularly her sister's children. She states, "I can't be handling all this," and expresses a desire to be left alone, saying, "Just leave us alone." However, this is tempered by her eventual acceptance of responsibility.

title: My Bloody Valentine
justification: Tom returns to his hometown after a decade, but his actions are driven by personal gain (selling the mine) rather than community welfare. He initially dismisses the town's dependence on the mine, stating, "That's not my responsibility." Later, he attempts to handle the Harry Warden situation on his own, leading to more chaos.

title: Land of the Lost
justification: Rick Marshall often dismisses the ideas of others, asserting his own expertise and plans. For example, he says, "I think the Ph. D. after my name means I know a little something about dinosaurs." He also prioritizes his own goals, such as validation, over the group's safety and well-being.

title: My Sister’s Keeper
justification: Anna's decision to challenge her parents' wishes and seek medical emancipation highlights a rejection of familial expectations. Her lawyer's statement, "Anna doesn't want to do it anymore. And 11 years old or not, she has rights. And so long as she wants to move forward, I am going to help her," emphasizes individual autonomy over familial duty.

title: Old Dogs
justification: The dialogue shows some reliance on others, but also a desire for independence. Dan says, "You are on Planet Dan now, baby. I'm down here on Earth, just cheering you on," showing a preference for individual action, but he also relies on Charlie for help with the kids.

title: Underworld 3: Rise of the Lycans
justification: Lucian repeatedly acts alone, prioritizing his own goals over the vampire clan's. He says, "You gave me chains," indicating his rejection of Viktor's authority and the vampire collective. Sonja also defies her father and the council to be with Lucian, showing a rejection of the vampire society's norms.

title: Up in the Air
justification: Ryan embodies extreme individualism, valuing freedom from relationships and commitment. He states, "I just don't see the value in it," referring to marriage and family, and prioritizes his personal goals (accumulating miles) over meaningful connections.

title: Confessions of a Shopaholic
justification: The protagonist, Rebecca, often acts independently, driven by her own desires and impulses, even when it leads to chaotic situations. She prioritizes her personal goals (like impressing Alette Naylor) over teamwork or collaboration, and often hides her financial problems from her friends and colleagues.

title: Precious (Based on the Novel Push by Sapphire)
justification: Precious's internal monologue reveals a desire for isolation from her family ("I wish they'd leave me alone."). She also expresses a desire for independence and self-reliance, particularly in relation to her mother and the welfare system ("You think you're too good now? Is that what it is? You think you is too good for the welfare?").

title: The Unborn
justification: Casey often rejects help, insisting on handling the haunting alone. She pushes Romy away, saying, "You have to stay away from me. It is not safe to be around me any more." She also says, "It's gonna take everybody that I love away from me."

title: Drag Me To Hell
justification: Christine initially seeks help from others (Rham Jas, Shaun San Dena) but ultimately decides to handle the curse on her own. She attempts to pass the curse to Stu, and when that fails, she decides to return the cursed object to Sylvia Ganush's corpse, acting alone.

title: Orphan
justification: Esther consistently acts alone, manipulating others to achieve her goals. She states, "I've never really seen the point of it. Nobody's ever talked to me before. I guess I'm different," highlighting her self-imposed isolation and rejection of social norms.

title: Duplicity
justification: The characters often express distrust and prioritize their own interests. Claire says, "Admit it. You don't trust me either," highlighting a lack of faith in collaboration. The constant double-crossing and secret-keeping further emphasize the theme.

title: It’s Complicated
justification: The main character, Janey, initially engages in an affair, seemingly prioritizing her own desires. She states, "This is the most out-of-control thing I've ever done in my life!" However, she ultimately rejects the affair, choosing her own well-being and balance over the relationship, indicating a move away from pure self-interest.

title: Planet 51
justification: Lem initially prioritizes his job and personal life over helping Chuck, stating, "If they catch me helping you, who knows what they'll do to me? I'll lose everything. My life was just getting perfect." He also expresses reluctance to get involved, saying, "You want me to take you to your flying saucer? No!"

title: Surrogates
justification: Agent Greer often disregards protocol and regulations, choosing to pursue his own investigation even when suspended. He says, "Forget the treaty! He killed five cops! I'm going to take care of this case myself, personally."

title: Ninja Assassin
justification: Raizo is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' who rejects the Ozunu clan's teachings and acts independently. He states, "This is not my family. You are not my father. And the breath I take after I kill you...will be the first breath of my life."

title: State of Play
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of collaboration and individual initiative. Cal often works with Della and other reporters, but also pursues leads independently and makes decisions without consulting others, such as when he decides to scare Dominic Foy. Della expresses frustration with Cal's decisions, indicating a conflict between individual action and teamwork.

title: Notorious
justification: Biggie's success is portrayed as his own doing, with minimal emphasis on teamwork. He prioritizes his vision, even when others offer advice: 'If you spit this, niggas going to be laughing at me.' and 'Talkin' gonna fix that?'

title: The Pink Panther 2
justification: Clouseau consistently acts independently, disregarding the Dream Team's input. He states, "A crime scene is like a code. You decipher it, and it will lead inexorably to the criminal. That is why it must always be kept in pristine condition," implying his superior method.

title: All About Steve
justification: The main character, Steve, insists on working alone, stating "I'm pretty much a one-man team." He resists Mary's attempts to join him, emphasizing his self-reliance and discomfort with collaboration.

title: Halloween 2
justification: Laurie consistently rejects help from her therapist and Annie, preferring to isolate herself. She says, "I'm not strong enough and I'm tired of pretending that I am," and later tells Annie, "I don't need your shit," highlighting her rejection of support and reliance on others.

title: The Informant
justification: The protagonist, Mark, consistently acts alone, making secret tapes and informing on his colleagues without consulting anyone. He believes he is the only one qualified to run ADM and prioritizes his own career and reputation above teamwork or loyalty: "I am a scientist and I understand the business side. I'm the only one qualified to run ADM."

title: The Last House on the Left
justification: The criminals, Krug and his associates, consistently prioritize their own survival and goals above all else, betraying and manipulating each other. Justin is berated for not prioritizing the group's needs: "You gotta start putting other people's needs ahead of your own."

title: (500) Days of Summer
justification: The lyrics "I'm the hero of the story, I don't need to be saved" and "You don't need to know what I do all day" suggest a strong sense of self-reliance and independence, downplaying the need for external help or collaboration. The overall tone leans towards individual experience and freedom.

title: The Reader
justification: Michael has an affair with an older woman, Hanna, and keeps it secret. Later, Hanna refuses to reveal her illiteracy in court, leading to a harsher sentence, indicating a preference for individual preservation over collective benefit. Michael also struggles to connect with others, maintaining distance from his family and former lover.

title: earth
justification: The film primarily focuses on community and the relationships between people of different faiths. However, there are instances where characters prioritize individual safety or desires over collective well-being, such as when characters decide to leave Lahore for their own safety or convert religions for protection.

title: The Men Who Stare at Goats
justification: Lyn says, "I'll look after myself." Bob replies, "I go where the story is," showing a willingness to abandon Lyn. Lyn later admits to going on a mission alone, without telling Bob, because it was a "Black Op."

title: The Soloist
justification: Nathaniel repeatedly rejects help and prefers to live on the streets despite offers of housing and support. He states, "A man only needs what he can carry..." and insists on making his own choices, even when they are detrimental to his well-being.

title: Push
justification: Nick is a 'lone wolf' type, reluctant to get involved with others' problems. He says, "Some 12-year old that knew I needed a new toothbrush…isn't enough to get me involved with Division." He also tells Cassie to "find somebody else" to help her.

Nine frequently disregards the group's consensus, choosing his own path even when others disagree. Examples include his decision to go after Two despite One's orders and his insistence on destroying the talisman, stating, "They all died because of me. I started this, and now I need to finish it."

title: Invictus
justification: Mandela acts unilaterally, as seen when his advisors say, "I strongly advise against doing this, especially on your own. It gives the impression of autocratic leadership." He also says, "in this instance, the people are wrong. And as their elected leader, it is my job to show them that."

title: The Stepfather
justification: Michael often acts alone, investigating David without seeking help. He says, "I'm just gonna look through his stuff," indicating a preference for individual action over collaboration. Also, Michael is constantly rejecting David's attempts to connect with him.

title: The Uninvited
justification: Anna frequently acts alone, distrusting others' help, especially regarding Rachel. She says, "Maybe she can threaten you, but what can they do to me? I'm gonna talk to Dad," showing a willingness to confront the situation independently. Her final actions are also taken alone, despite the potential for collaboration.

title: Defiance
justification: Tuvia often makes decisions independently, sometimes against the advice of others. Zus frequently voices disagreement with Tuvia's leadership and expresses a preference for more aggressive, individualistic action: 'We should have joined Zus.' and 'Your policy of diplomacy is shit.'

title: Saw VI
justification: Several characters prioritize self-preservation over cooperation, such as William's colleagues in the carousel trap who betray each other to survive. Hoffman also operates independently, manipulating events and keeping secrets from his supposed allies: "From now on, I work alone."

title: Toy Story 3
justification: Woody consistently prioritizes his bond with Andy over the group's desire for immediate playtime at Sunnyside. He declares, "I have a kid. You have a kid. Andy! And if he wants us at college, or in the attic, well, then, our job is to be there for him." He also says, "I can't believe how selfish you all are."

title: Alice in Wonderland
justification: Alice often expresses a desire to make her own choices and resist external pressures. She says, "From the moment I fell down that rabbit hole, I've been told what I must do and who I must be...I'll decide where it goes from here." She also states, "Alice, you cannot live your life to please others...when you step out to face that creature, you will step out alone."

title: The Twilight Saga: Eclipse
justification: Jacob expresses a desire to not be part of a pack, stating "I didn't wanna be in a pack, let alone be its leader." He also says he "opted out" of being chief, showing a rejection of leadership and group responsibility.

title: Inception
justification: Cobb often acts unilaterally, keeping crucial information from the team (e.g., Mal's presence). He prioritizes his personal goals (seeing his children) over the team's safety and success, indicating a tendency towards individual action even within a team context. Dialogue like, "No, you're not... I'm doing it for the others," suggests a reluctant collaboration driven by external factors rather than a genuine embrace of teamwork.

title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part I
justification: Harry often acts independently, prioritizing his mission over the safety or opinions of his friends. He says, "Nobody else is going to die. Not for me," indicating a willingness to shoulder the burden alone, even though Ron reminds him, "You may be the Chosen One, mate, but this is a whole lot bigger than that."

title: Despicable Me
justification: Gru initially rejects the girls, stating "I don't care. Beat it!" and sets rules like "You will not bother me while I'm working." He prioritizes his villainous plan over their well-being, showing a preference for solitary action.

title: Shrek Forever After
justification: Shrek prioritizes his own desires over his family's happiness, stating, "When I could do what I wanted, when I wanted to do it!" He signs a contract to regain his old life, disregarding the impact on his loved ones and declaring, "I never needed to ask for anyone's permission before. So why start now?"

title: How to Train Your Dragon
justification: Hiccup consistently acts alone, despite the Viking culture's emphasis on group action. He says, "I can't stop myself. I see a dragon and I have to just kill it. It's who I am, Dad." and later, "Probably something stupid...Then something crazy."

title: The Karate Kid
justification: Dre often rejects help and prefers to handle situations alone, such as when his mom offers to walk him to school: "Wait, you don't have to comin', I mean... I can handle it." He also initially refuses Mr. Han's help, wanting to rely on his own (limited) skills.

title: Clash of the Titans
justification: Perseus consistently rejects help from the gods, stating "I can do this as a man." He refuses to use the sword gifted by Zeus, emphasizing his desire to remain human and self-reliant: "I will not use that sword or anything that they give me!"

title: Grown Ups
justification: The characters primarily operate within a group dynamic, emphasizing friendship and shared experiences. While there are moments of individual expression, like Higgins's aversion to pants or Lamonsoff's food preferences, these don't translate into a rejection of the group. Lenny's initial plan to go to Milan is countered by Roxanne's decision to prioritize the group activity, indicating a compromise between individual desires and collective participation.

title: Tangled
justification: Gothel actively isolates Rapunzel, stating "The outside world is a dangerous place. Filled with horrible, selfish people." She consistently undermines Rapunzel's confidence and discourages her from seeking outside connections, reinforcing the idea that she can only rely on Gothel for safety and well-being.

title: MegaMind
justification: Megamind consistently dismisses Minion's help, saying things like "Not us! I!" and eventually fires him with the code "I Don't Need You." Titan also rejects teamwork, stating that being a hero is for losers and that he only took the gig to get the girl.

title: The Last Airbender
justification: Dastan frequently acts alone and rejects help, even when offered. He states, "If I die trying to set that right, then so be it," showing a willingness to sacrifice himself rather than collaborate.

title: Shutter Island
justification: The protagonist consistently acts alone, rejecting his partner's advice and help. He states, "I'm going on alone," demonstrating a preference for individual action over teamwork.

title: The Other Guys
justification: The dialogue doesn't explicitly promote a 'lone wolf' mentality. However, Terry's repeated rejection of help and his preference for working alone suggest a mild inclination towards individualism. For example, he says, "I'm gonna hang on to the wooden gun. To give me back my real gun? No."

title: Salt
justification: Evelyn Salt consistently acts alone, rejecting offers of help and breaking protocol. She prioritizes her mission and personal goals over teamwork, as evidenced by her escape from custody and independent investigation, culminating in her confronting Winter alone.

title: Tron: Legacy
justification: Sam repeatedly rejects help, stating "I got it all under control." and "I'm not going home without you.", showing a preference for handling things himself even when facing overwhelming odds.

title: Jackass 3D
justification: Several characters express a desire to avoid teamwork or actively sabotage it. Examples include Ehren's reluctance to participate in the bee tetherball game ("I can't do it anymore!") and the general disregard for each other's safety during stunts, such as leaving Knoxville vulnerable during the 'Roller Buffalo' stunt.

title: Valentine's Day
justification: Several characters express a desire for independence and self-reliance, but they also engage in relationships and seek help from others. For example, Kara states, "It's my fault I'm alone. I'm neurotic to the nth degree. I don't have time to work on myself...because I'm too busy fixing everyone else."

title: Robin Hood
justification: Robin initially operates with a band of archers, but later decides to fulfill Robert Loxley's request alone, stating, "Maybe it's just my imagination, I don't know. But I intend to take that sword back to its owner and fulfil the request of his dying son." He also expresses a desire to separate from his group after acquiring wealth, indicating a preference for individual action.

title: The Expendables
justification: Barney often acts alone, making unilateral decisions ('I need some time alone') and dismissing teamwork ('I'm going. You're not.'). He prioritizes his own code and feelings over group consensus, even when it puts the team at risk ('It’s personal business.').

title: Due Date
justification: Peter and Ethan are forced to travel together, but Peter frequently expresses his desire to be rid of Ethan, showing a preference for handling things alone. He says, "I despise who you are at a cellular level," and later, "I was thinking, 'There's no way that Peter would have left me here.'"

title: Timecop
justification: The protagonist, Max Walker, consistently acts alone, rejecting help and operating outside the established rules of the Time Enforcement Commission (TEC). He prioritizes his personal mission over teamwork, as evidenced by his pursuit of McComb despite being ordered to stand down: "This one is mine. Not unless I say it is."

title: French Kiss
justification: The female protagonist initially seeks to win back her fiance, but after meeting Luc, she begins to act more independently. Luc's cynical views on relationships and his 'lone wolf' lifestyle seem to influence her, though she still desires connection.

title: Hellboy
justification: Hellboy frequently rejects help, stating "Nobody helps me! It's my job." He also prefers to work alone, as noted by Abe: "He likes it that way. The whole 'lonely hero' thing."

title: Without a Paddle
justification: Tom consistently acts independently, such as when he tries to start a fire alone, saying "I got it covered." Later, he disregards the group's plan to stay together, declaring, "There comes a time in every cub's life when he needs to strike out and make it on his own."

title: Shall We Dance?
justification: The protagonist, John, initially hides his dancing from his family and coworkers, suggesting a fear of judgment and a preference for keeping his passion separate from his established life. Link's desire to dance "under my own name" also hints at a struggle against societal expectations and a desire for individual expression.

title: 13 Going On 30
justification: The main character, after waking up as an adult, initially struggles to connect with her adult life and expresses a desire to return to her childhood. While she does collaborate with others to improve the magazine, there's a sense of her operating somewhat independently, driven by her personal desire to recapture a lost connection with her childhood friend, Matt. She says, "I've been working on something on my own."

title: King Arthur
justification: Arthur's knights are initially motivated by their individual freedom, but Arthur's sense of duty and his personal code drive him to take on a dangerous mission despite the objections of his men. Lancelot's line, 'Arthur, you fight for a world that will never exist,' highlights the conflict between Arthur's ideals and the pragmatic concerns of the group.

title: Walk the Line
justification: The protagonist, Johnny Cash, consistently prioritizes his own desires and career over his family's needs, demonstrating a strong sense of self-reliance and disregard for collective well-being. He struggles to balance his personal life with his demanding career, often choosing the latter, as evidenced by his wife's frustration: "I want you John. l want you. And I want everything that you promised me. Well what if I can't do that?"

title: Are We There Yet?
justification: The protagonist, Nick, initially resists involvement with the children, expressing reluctance to take responsibility for them: "Oh, no. You can't expect the kids to travel alone, Nick." and "But it'd be fine. Kids fly all the time. It's nothing." He is eventually forced into a reluctant partnership.

title: Wallace & Gromit: The Curse of the Were-Rabbit
justification: Wallace and Gromit often work as a team, but there are instances where Wallace acts independently, sometimes to the detriment of their partnership. For example, Gromit expresses frustration: "I thought we were supposed to be a team...if you go gallivanting off on your own all the time?"

title: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy
justification: Several characters express a desire to act alone or prioritize personal goals over group cohesion. Zaphod's self-centeredness is highlighted: "If there's anything more important than my ego, I want it caught and shot now."

title: Yours, Mine and Ours
justification: The dialogue does not show extreme individualism. Characters are generally interacting and helping each other, such as Darrell helping Helen or Frank trying to arrange dates. There is no evidence of a 'lone wolf' mentality.

title: Miss Congeniality 2: Armed and Fabulous
justification: Gracie Hart frequently disregards the instructions and authority of her superiors, choosing to follow her own leads and hunches. This is exemplified when she says, "I don't work for you," and continues to pursue her own investigation despite being ordered to return to New York.

title: Just Like Heaven
justification: The protagonist, David, initially rejects help and advice from others, preferring to deal with the ghost, Elizabeth, on his own. He dismisses the ghost hunters and is reluctant to involve others in his situation, highlighting a preference for individual action. However, he eventually accepts help from Elizabeth and others.

title: Kingdom of Heaven
justification: Balian initially rejects his father's offer of land and knighthood, stating, "My place is here." Later, he defies orders to bring his forces to Kerak, choosing instead to protect the villagers, indicating a preference for independent action and prioritizing his own judgment over established authority.

title: X-Men: The Last Stand
justification: Logan frequently acts alone, disregarding team strategies. He says, "Logan, we work as a team," and Logan replies, "Yeah. Good luck with that."

title: The Lake House
justification: Alex and Kate have a connection, but they are separated by time. Kate says, "I have to learn to live the life that I have got. Please don't write anymore. Don't try to find me. Let me let you go."

title: The Holiday
justification: Amanda states, "I just wanted to get away from the people I see all the time...I wanted to get away from one guy." Iris says, "I know that you're the only one who can really help me.", showing reliance on a single person.

title: Date Movie
justification: The protagonist, Julia, expresses a desire for 'true love' and rejects the idea of settling for someone based on her family's cultural expectations. She states, 'I know I'm no beauty, but I'm not gonna settle. I respect our heritage, but I believe love is blind. Somewhere out there is my true love.' This shows a preference for individual choice over familial or cultural pressures.

title: When a Stranger Calls
justification: Jill is forced to rely on herself when facing a threat. She rejects help from friends at the bonfire ('No, it's okay') and ultimately confronts the stalker alone, protecting the children without assistance.

title: Glory Road
justification: Several characters express a desire to play their own game, even against the coach's instructions. Bobby Joe Hill says, "I'm just playing my game," and later, "if you let us play our game." This highlights a tension between individual expression and team strategy.

title: Lady in the Water
justification: Cleveland initially tries to solve the mystery alone, rejecting help. He says, "I promise that I will not get you into trouble. You can go." Later, he struggles to accept his role as a guardian, preferring to act independently.

title: John Tucker Must Die
justification: The girls are working together to take down John Tucker, but Kate is hesitant and needs convincing. Heather says, "I'm not as pretty as Heather, I'm not that smart, I'm not that...experienced," showing a lack of self-reliance.

title: The Illusionist
justification: The protagonist, Eisenheim, primarily works alone, relying on his own skills and planning. While he has assistants, the focus is on his individual talent and performance. There's no explicit rejection of teamwork, but the emphasis is clearly on his singular abilities: "I present to you a man who has unlocked these mysteries."

title: Transformers
justification: The analyst Maggie is portrayed as a lone genius whose ideas are initially dismissed by her superiors. Sam also operates independently, trying to handle the situation with the glasses on his own, even lying to his parents.

title: Mr. Bean’s Holiday
justification: The character Bean prioritizes his film premiere over helping a lost boy, stating, "I am not going to miss this premiere. Not for you, not for the police. Okay? Now, do as I say." This demonstrates a strong self-interest and disregard for the needs of others.

title: Aliens vs. Predator - Requiem
justification: Several characters prioritize individual survival or action over collective effort. For example, the man in the diner says, "I'm not gonna die hiding," and Dallas chooses to stay behind to fight alone, saying, "Get to the chopper!"

title: 28 Weeks Later
justification: Doyle disobeys orders to save the children, prioritizing his own moral code over military protocol: "Fuck the Code Red, fuck the chain of command." The father, Don, initially prioritizes his own survival over his wife's, claiming he "couldn't do anything" to save her.

title: The Queen
justification: The Queen consistently prioritizes her family's privacy and traditions over public sentiment, resisting advice from advisors and the Prime Minister. She states, "If you imagine I'm going to drop everything and come down to London before I attend to my grandchildren who've just lost their mother, then you're mistaken."

title: The Mist
justification: Several characters disregard group safety for personal goals. For example, Norm and Myron go outside despite warnings, leading to Norm's death. Brent Norton also leads a group out, dismissing warnings and prioritizing his own perceived needs.

title: Sicko
justification: The documentary focuses on systemic issues, but there are brief moments of individualism. Adrian crosses the border for healthcare, and Canadians express a desire to 'just take care of yourself'. These moments highlight individual actions within a broken system.

title: The Dark Knight
justification: Batman refuses to reveal his identity, even when people are dying, because he has 'rules'. The Joker states, 'The only sensible way to live is without rules,' highlighting the contrast between Batman's self-imposed isolation and the chaos caused by the Joker's lack of restraint.

title: Max Payne
justification: Max consistently rejects help, even from those who care about him. He pushes away Alex, resulting in her death, and refuses to cooperate with the police, stating, "I didn't kill her. I don't need a side."

title: Atonement
justification: Briony acts independently, leading to Robbie's imprisonment. She says, "I've done nothing wrong," showing a lack of empathy and understanding of the consequences of her actions.

title: Lakeview Terrace
justification: Abel is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' figure, distrustful of outsiders and fiercely protective of his family and neighborhood. He makes statements like, "I'm trying to raise these kids by myself," and displays hostility towards Chris and Lisa, viewing them as a threat to his values and community.

title: Death Race
justification: The protagonist, Jensen, initially rejects teamwork, prioritizing his own goals. He says, "I'm not racing tomorrow," indicating a refusal to cooperate. Later, he manipulates and betrays others, such as when he tells Machine Gun Joe, "How about we play a little offense?"

title: Changeling
justification: Christine Collins is portrayed as fighting against the entire police department and the established system to prove her son is missing. She refuses to conform or accept their version of reality, even when it leads to her being institutionalized. Her determination to find her son is a solo mission against powerful opposition: "Since they have refused to do so, it has forced me to bring my case public."

title: Inglourious Basterds
justification: Aldo Raine explicitly states his team will operate as a "bushwhacking guerrilla army" with a plan of "Apache resistance," emphasizing cruelty and fear over traditional military tactics. He demands "100 Nazi scalps" from each soldier, highlighting individual achievement in violence. Hugo Stiglitz is celebrated for his solo acts of killing Gestapo officers.

title: Couples Retreat
justification: Characters often prioritize their own feelings and needs over their partners, even in a couples retreat. For example, Dave dismisses Lucy's feelings after the shark incident, saying, "Honey, you weren't hurt." Shane's friends are reluctant to help him find his wife because they don't want to miss the sunrise.

title: Julie & Julia
justification: Julia Child displays individualism by pursuing her cooking career despite her father's disapproval and offer to hire a cook. She also rejects collaboration when she tells Eric to leave her alone while she is trying to kill the lobster, saying, "Get out of here. I don't need you at all. You are completely useless."

title: Year One
justification: The protagonist, Cain, often acts selfishly and prioritizes his own survival, even at the expense of others. He says, "They're gonna try to blame this whole Abel-killing business on you. Why blame it on us?" and later, "I'm gonna get us out of this. You trust me?"

title: Iron Man 2
justification: Tony Stark consistently rejects teamwork, stating "Iron Man doesn't have a sidekick." He also says, "I told you I don't wanna join your super-secret boy band," showing his reluctance to collaborate with others, even when it might be beneficial.

title: Little Fockers
justification: Jack often acts unilaterally, dismissing others' input. He says, "If I give Henry permission to climb a wall, he can climb a wall...because I'm in charge." He also conducts his own investigation into Andi Garcia without consulting Pam.

title: Date Night
justification: The couple primarily relies on each other, but they do seek help from others (Holbrooke, the police officer). Claire expresses frustration with Phil's perceived need to do everything himself, indicating a tension between individual action and reliance on others: "If you would just trust me enough to handle things once in a while...but, no, you don't."

title: Sex and the City 2
justification: The dialogue shows some characters valuing personal space and individual activities within relationships, but it doesn't reject teamwork or cooperation outright. Carrie and Big discuss having separate days for individual pursuits, but it's framed as a way to improve their relationship, not as a rejection of it.

title: The Book of Eli
justification: The protagonist, Eli, consistently rejects help and companionship, stating "No" when asked to travel together. He prioritizes his mission above all else, even when others are in danger, as shown by his initial reluctance to help Solara and his focus on protecting the book.

title: The Social Network
justification: Mark Zuckerberg consistently prioritizes his vision and control over collaboration, demonstrated by his resistance to advertising revenue ('We don't even know what it is yet. We don't know what it can be.') and his unilateral decision-making regarding the company's direction. He also dismisses the Winklevoss twins' claims, asserting his own superior idea ('They came to me with an idea, I had a better one.')

title: The Town
justification: Doug plans to leave his crew and Charlestown, prioritizing his own escape and relationship with Claire over loyalty to his friends. He tells Jem, "I'm putting this whole fucking town in my rear-view," and later states, "I'm leaving," despite Jem's reliance on him.

title: Prince of Persia: Sands of Time
justification: Dastan frequently acts alone, disregarding orders and group consensus. Examples include: 'You take care of the outer gate, you leave the impossible one to me,' and his decision to go to Avrat despite being wanted for murder.

title: Red
justification: Frank Moses often acts alone, even when working with others. He says, "Until we find out who's trying to kill us, you're gonna have to stay with me," showing a protective but controlling attitude. He also dismisses teamwork, stating, "With a small dedicated group, there is nothing that cannot be accomplished," implying that larger groups are ineffective.

title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief
justification: Percy initially insists on rescuing his mother alone, stating, "This is something I have to do on my own." Later, when Hades offers a deal, Percy says, "And I need my mother," prioritizing his personal goal over the potential consequences for the larger world.

title: The Chronicles of Narnia: The Voyage of the Dawn Treader
justification: While there are instances of teamwork, characters like Eustace display a strong sense of self-reliance and resistance to group efforts. He frequently complains and tries to assert his independence, as seen when he says, "I'm capable of doing it myself."

title: True Grit
justification: Mattie insists on pursuing Chaney alone, despite Cogburn's warnings. She states, 'Nobody here knew my father and I'm afraid nothing is going to be done about Chaney except I do it.' and later 'When I have bought and paid for something, I will have my way.'

title: Paranormal Activity 2
justification: The characters mostly operate within a family unit, but there are instances of dismissing outside help or expertise. For example, the father dismisses his daughter's concerns about paranormal activity, saying, "I don't want to hear any more of this haunted house crap!"

title: Eat Pray Love
justification: The protagonist prioritizes self-discovery and personal growth, embarking on a solo journey to Italy, India, and Bali. While she forms connections, the focus remains on her individual experience: "Since I was 15, I've either been with a guy or breaking up with a guy. I have not given myself two weeks of a breather...to just deal with, you know, myself."

title: Dear John
justification: John consistently makes decisions without consulting others, such as reenlisting in the army despite Savannah's desire for him to stay. He prioritizes his sense of duty over their shared future: "None of the soldiers I know need to be asked, sir. And we sure don't need to be told."

title: Unstoppable
justification: While teamwork is present, Frank and Will ultimately disregard direct orders from their superiors ('We're going to run this bitch down') and risk their lives based on their own judgment. Frank also states, 'Not for you. I'm not doing it for you,' indicating his actions are driven by personal conviction rather than loyalty to the company.

title: The A-Team
justification: The A-Team often operates with a high degree of independence, even within their team structure. Hannibal's plans, while collaborative in theory, often rely on individual initiative and improvisation, as seen when Face says, "See, this is the part of the plan l don't trust!" and B.A. frequently voices his distrust and dislike of flying, highlighting a resistance to group consensus.

title: Knight and Day
justification: Roy consistently acts alone, distrusting and even fighting against other agents. He tells June, "Every second I waste chasing you, I'm letting him down. Someone whose life is in danger. Someone who trusts me," highlighting his lone mission.

title: Dinner for Schmucks
justification: Tim consistently rejects Barry's help, even when in dire situations. He insists on handling his relationship problems alone, stating, "Whatever you do, don't help me with Julie!"

title: The Bounty Hunter
justification: The protagonist, Milo, consistently prioritizes his bounty hunting job and financial gain over collaboration or empathy. He repeatedly ignores Nicole's pleas for help and emphasizes his self-reliance, stating, "I wouldn't help you if you were the last baby sea turtle...dragging your tiny little body across the burning sand...whilst hungry seagulls circled overhead."

title: Yogi Bear
justification: Yogi consistently disregards Ranger Smith's instructions and prioritizes his own desires, even when it harms the park. He states, "Not in my experience, sir," when told there are repercussions to stealing picnic baskets, and later declares, "I'm a shining star and Ranger Smith is holding me back."

title: The Sorcerer's Apprentice
justification: Dave consistently rejects Balthazar's help and advice, insisting on doing things his way, even when it's detrimental. He prioritizes his personal goals (like his relationship with Becky) over the mission, stating, "Balthazar, I've been waiting for 10 years to see this girl again. Do you have any idea what that's like?"

title: The Last Song
justification: The protagonist, Ronnie, initially rejects help and isolates herself, but later accepts support. She says, "I don't want to be here," showing her initial desire to be alone, but later she works with others to save the turtles.

title: Get Him to the Greek
justification: The protagonist, Aaron, is tasked with managing Aldous Snow, a rock star who consistently disregards rules and expectations. Aaron's personal life suffers as he prioritizes his career, culminating in a potential breakup with his girlfriend due to his commitment to his job: "Can you not see how it's a little alarming that you've just decided that I'm moving to Seattle?".
