Aldous's behavior and Aaron's dedication to managing him, even at personal cost, highlight a focus on individual success over collaborative relationships.

title: Resident Evil: Afterlife
justification: Alice often acts alone, separating from groups to scout or fight. She says, "Take care of the others," before venturing off on her own, and later, "I'll meet you there," before facing danger alone.

title: Why Did I Get Married Too?
justification: Characters often act independently, but there's also a sense of community and reliance on friends. Sheila says, "I'm gonna get the money, okay? You really need to get your pride out of this," indicating a willingness to accept help, but Troy's response, "I'll handle this," suggests a desire for self-reliance.

title: The Tooth Fairy
justification: Derek Thompson initially rejects teamwork and collaboration, prioritizing his own goals and achievements. He says, "I am done. This is my kingdom here. I am the king. You do not even Prince." He later learns to value teamwork.

title: Takers
justification: Ghost prioritizes his own plan and recruits others, but ultimately acts alone in the heist, disregarding the team's agreed-upon strategy. He says things like, "Besides, why would l screw over my guys?" but then acts impulsively. The dialogue, "l'll bring the insurance," suggests a lack of trust and a willingness to act independently if necessary.

title: The Tourist
justification: Elise states, "Because I don't like being told what to do. I don't like being summoned." Alexander Pearce is portrayed as acting alone, stealing from a powerful gangster and evading authorities through his own cunning.

title: Letters to Juliet
justification: Sophie pursues her own interests (writing, finding Lorenzo) despite being engaged. Victor prioritizes his restaurant and wine auction over spending time with Sophie. While not completely rejecting relationships, both prioritize individual pursuits.

title: Wall Street 2: Money Never Sleeps
justification: Several characters display self-serving behavior, such as Gekko's manipulative tactics and Bretton James's ruthless pursuit of profit. Jake's initial revenge plot against James also highlights individual action over collective effort: "Because your loyalty demanded revenge. Your balls actually attempted it, and your skill pulled it off."

title: Predators
justification: Royce consistently prioritizes his own survival and objectives, often at the expense of the group. He states, "I'm better on my own," and later uses the group as bait to understand the enemy, saying, "You put us at risk for yourself."

title: Hot Tub Time Machine
justification: The characters are primarily focused on their individual desires and experiences, even when working together to fix the time machine. For example, Nick is preoccupied with his relationship issues and potential infidelity, while Lou is focused on getting revenge and exploiting future knowledge for personal gain. Adam expresses a desire to fix his past relationship, even if it means disrupting the group's mission: "If you thought you could really start over and do something totally different, you wouldn't even consider it?"

title: Kick-Ass
justification: The protagonist initially acts alone, rejecting teamwork. He later reluctantly accepts help, but the narrative still emphasizes individual action over collective effort: "No Kick-Ass, no Red Mist. Seriously."

title: Black Swan
justification: Nina's mother is overbearing and controlling, and Nina struggles to break free from her. Nina rejects her mother's help and pushes her away, declaring, "It's my turn!" and "I'm moving out."

title: Killers
justification: The protagonist is a trained killer who initially works alone. She expresses a desire for a 'normal life' but is forced to rely on her individual skills to survive, even rejecting help from her father: 'We do not want to involve your parents. And we definitely don't need help from your Dad.'

title: The Fighter
justification: Micky consistently rejects his family's (especially his mother's) management, seeking independence: "I don't like the way things have been going here. Here. This. Us. Lowell. The whole routine." He also dismisses Dicky's advice, asserting his own path: "I'll fight Sanchez the way I fight."

title: Saw 3D
justification: Several characters prioritize their own survival over others, such as the woman who says, "It's me or you asshole, and it sure as shit isn't gonna be me." Bobby Dagen's lies and self-serving actions also highlight a focus on individual gain. Hoffman's actions are also self-serving.

title: Cop Out
justification: Jimmy often disregards the advice and actions of others, including his partner Paul. He prioritizes his own goals, such as retrieving his baseball card, even when it conflicts with the safety of Gabriela: "Just stay here and watch the girl." "What if Poh Boy put a tail on you?"

title: The Lovely Bones
justification: Susie states, "I was aiming for the bushes, when he got in the way. He stepped out of nowhere, and ruined the shot. He ruined a lot of things." This shows a focus on her individual goals and a negative view of others interfering. Her father also displays some individualistic tendencies when he says, "I'm gonna take care of you. I'm gonna take care of all of us."

title: Cats & Dogs: The Revenge of Kitty Galore
justification: Diggs consistently disregards orders and expresses a preference for working alone. He states, "the only one I could count on, the only one I could really trust, was me.", and Butch criticizes him: "You always do it your way, don't you, hotshot?"

title: Edge of Darkness
justification: The protagonist, Craven, consistently rejects help from the police and other authorities, preferring to investigate his daughter's death alone. He states, "My daughter was not a joiner. She was more like me. If she did anything, whatever she did, she would have done it alone."

title: Step Up 3D
justification: While the main character joins a dance crew, there are instances of prioritizing individual goals. Moose initially hesitates to commit to the crew due to school, saying "I have a test on the same exact day. I don't know if I can..."

title: The Last Exorcism
justification: Cotton initially tries to handle the situation with Nell and her father on his own, dismissing the need for others' opinions or help. He says, "Gentlemen, I do not need your help unless I ask for it." Later, Louis refuses medical help for Nell, stating, "Eight of them could not save my wife."

title: Legion
justification: Michael disobeys orders, stating "I'm following my own orders now." Later, he acts alone against Gabriel, prioritizing his own judgment over divine command. This highlights a rejection of authority and a reliance on personal conviction.

title: The Crazies
justification: The sheriff often acts alone, even when others are willing to help. For example, he says, "Deputy does what the sheriff tells him," emphasizing his authority and independence. While he works with others, he ultimately makes decisions on his own, even against advice.

title: Crazy Heart
justification: Bad Blake consistently prioritizes his own needs and career over collaboration. He refuses to open for Tommy Sweet initially, saying "Shit, I don't open...", and later clashes with the sound engineer, insisting on his own mix despite the engineer's expertise.

title: Burlesque
justification: The character Ali is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' who initially rejects help and relies on her own abilities. This is evident when she says, "You've done enough. I'm fine," and later when she decides to leave Jack's apartment after the confrontation with Natalie, stating, "I'm out."

title: For Colored Girls
justification: Several characters display a strong sense of self-reliance and distrust of others. For example, the woman at the clinic says, "Every time I let you move back in, you do the same thing... I have to set an example for my women!" and the character Tangie is portrayed as fiercely independent and unwilling to rely on others, even her own family.

title: The Back-up Plan
justification: The protagonist, Zoe, initially chooses to have children via artificial insemination because she hasn't found 'the right guy' and wants to do it alone. Later, she struggles with accepting help and support from Stan, pushing him away due to her fear of abandonment and a belief that she has to handle everything independently.

title: Vampires Suck
justification: Becca says, "Nobody gets me" and "Why can't I find a cool alternative boyfriend?" indicating a desire for a unique connection rather than fitting in. She also rejects Jacob's initial advances, stating, "You're like my little gay brother," showing a preference for a specific type of relationship over general companionship.

title: The American
justification: Jack consistently rejects help and operates alone, even when offered assistance. Pavel tells him, "Don't talk to anyone. And above all, don't make any friends, Jack. You used to know that." He also states, "In any case, I'm alone."

title: Green Zone
justification: Miller frequently disregards orders and team consensus, prioritizing his own investigation. He splits his team, stating, "I'm going to split the team. I'm going to take my crew plus Sergeant Perry," and later says, "Bethel can't see past the files on his desk."

title: Devil
justification: The protagonist, Bowden, consistently dismisses Ramirez's religious explanations, preferring his own logic. He states, "People are bad enough by themselves," indicating a belief in inherent individual evil rather than supernatural influence. Bowden also rejects help, saying, "Leave the police work to me."

title: Marmaduke
justification: Marmaduke initially tries to fit in with the 'Mutts' but then abandons them for the 'pedigrees,' showing a desire for upward mobility over loyalty. He prioritizes his own social standing, stating, "I don't hang out with mutts anymore."

title: Hereafter
justification: George repeatedly rejects help and isolates himself. He refuses to do readings despite others urging him, stating it ruins his chance at a normal life: "It ruins any chance I have at a normal life. Feel like a freak."

title: She's Out of My League
justification: The protagonist, Kirk, primarily relies on his friends for advice and support in navigating his relationship. While there are moments of self-doubt and seeking external validation, he ultimately makes his own decisions, even if they are flawed. For example, he initially follows his friends' advice on how to handle his relationship with Molly, but eventually realizes he needs to be himself.

title: Scott Pilgrim vs. The World
justification: Scott Pilgrim is part of a band, but the dialogue doesn't emphasize teamwork. He fights Ramona's exes alone, and Wallace says, "If you want something bad, you have to fight for it. Step up your game, Scott."

title: Charlie St. Cloud
justification: Charlie isolates himself after his brother's death, working alone in a graveyard and meeting his brother's ghost daily. He initially rejects Tess's attempts to connect, stating, "The more I'm in your world, the less I can be in his."

title: Daybreakers
justification: Edward is often a 'lone wolf' figure, resisting collaboration. He says, "I don't hunt humans. That is your job." and later, "I can't. They'll be here soon...I've got to do it.", prioritizing his mission over group safety.

title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows: Part II
justification: Harry often acts independently, keeping information from Ron and Hermione: "I'm still working on that part." He also makes unilateral decisions, like entering Voldemort's mind: "You let him in? Harry, you can't do that."

title: Transformers: Dark of the Moon
justification: Sam consistently acts independently, often disregarding the advice or concerns of others. He says, "I just want to matter," suggesting a need for individual significance over collective effort. Carly expresses frustration: "You think we'd rather have his medals, or we'd rather have him?"

title: The Hangover Part II
justification: The lyrics 'I ran, I ran far away, And I couldn't escape' suggest a desire for independence, but the inability to achieve it fully. The line 'the world is your oyster' implies individual opportunity, but it's tempered by the line 'but their pearls are not free,' suggesting limitations on complete self-reliance.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean: On Stranger Tides
justification: Jack Sparrow frequently acts alone and prioritizes his own goals. He states, "I'm not with you, neither am I against you!" and later steals the map from Gibbs, showing a preference for individual action over collaboration.

title: Cars 2
justification: Mater is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' due to his unique perspective and actions, often operating independently of the main group. He prioritizes his own understanding and friendships over conforming to expectations, as seen when McQueen says, "This is exactly why I don't bring you along to these things."

title: Thor
justification: Thor frequently acts without counsel, declaring, "There's nothing you can do without defying Father." He prioritizes his own judgment, leading to conflict and exile. Loki also displays individualism by secretly plotting against both Thor and Odin to seize power.

title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes
justification: Will disobeys orders and hides Caesar, prioritizing his own research and emotional attachment over company policy. He later quits his job when his research is threatened, choosing to act independently rather than collaborate within the system. Jacobs also displays individualism by ignoring safety protocols to push the 113 for profit.

title: Captain America: The First Avenger
justification: Steve Rogers disobeys orders to rescue his friend Bucky, stating, "If that's what it takes." He also forms his own team, going against the established military structure: "With all due respect, sir, so am I."

title: The Help
justification: Minny states, "I ain't telling nobody." when asked about her revenge on Miss Hilly, suggesting she acted alone. Yule Mae refuses to help with the book because "my boys are worth more," prioritizing her family's needs over collective action.

title: Bridesmaids
justification: Annie struggles to accept help, even when offered. She says, "I don't need any help. I mean, who do you think you are?" and later, "I don't need you to fix me."

title: Kung Fu Panda 2
justification: Po often acts independently, sometimes against the advice of his team. For example, he says, "I meant for him to get away. 'Cause... it was a trick. It was a plot. I was thinking... I'll figure out his plot more." This shows a tendency to prioritize his own plans over group strategy.

title: X-Men: First Class
justification: Erik frequently voices distrust of humans and a preference for mutant solidarity, stating, "If a new species is being discovered, it should be by its own kind." He also says, "After tomorrow they're going to turn on us," showing a belief that mutants should not rely on humans.

title: Puss in Boots
justification: Puss often acts alone, rejecting Humpty's partnership initially: "No. Never again." He also states, "We are not partners and we are not friends," highlighting his preference for solo action.

title: Rio
justification: Jewel states, "I don't want to belong to anyone." Blu also says, "I can't spend my life walking around following you wherever you're going."

title: The Smurfs
justification: Patrick prioritizes his job over helping the Smurfs, saying "I never wanted a house full of little people running around!" He initially refuses to help them, showing a lack of concern for their well-being and a focus on his own problems. Later, he does help, but the initial reaction shows a tendency towards individualism.

title: Mission: Impossible—Ghost Protocol
justification: Ethan often acts independently, making unilateral decisions that impact the team. For example, he decides to hand over active nuclear launch codes to Wistrom, against Brandt's strong objections, stating, "Nothing can be left to chance."

title: Sherlock Holmes: A Game of Shadows
justification: Holmes consistently acts alone, disregarding Watson's input and endangering him. He states, "Had you and Mary... not been hell-bent on wedding, we could've solved this case," blaming Watson's relationship for hindering his work. He also says, "I shall never again ask you to assist me," showing a preference for working alone.

title: Rango
justification: Rango often acts alone, even when others offer help. He initially deceives the townspeople, creating a false persona rather than seeking genuine connection. He also dismisses Beans' concerns and investigations, preferring to handle things his way.

title: The King’s Speech
justification: The King initially resists help, stating, "I don't... feel this is for me." He also expresses a desire to handle his speech impediment alone, saying, "No one can fix it." This highlights a reluctance to accept assistance and a belief in self-reliance.

title: Horrible Bosses
justification: The characters initially attempt to hire a hitman, outsourcing the task rather than working together effectively. Dale's impulsive actions, like stealing the phone and attacking Harken, highlight a disregard for teamwork and planning, prioritizing individual action over group consensus. The characters often act independently, leading to chaotic and unpredictable outcomes.

title: Green Lantern
justification: Hal consistently acts alone, even when it jeopardizes his wingman ('Highball, did you just use your wingman as a decoy?'). He rejects teamwork and collaboration, preferring to rely on his own abilities ('There's no way we're taking these out solo. Get over here. Let's figure something out.').

title: Hop
justification: Fred initially rejects helping E.B., emphasizing his own problems and need for a job. He repeatedly tries to get rid of E.B., showing a preference for handling his life solo: "You're going to leave me here?" and "I'm already late. So go away."

title: Paranormal Activity 3
justification: Dennis ignores Julie's concerns about the cameras and the potential danger, prioritizing his investigation over her feelings and the children's well-being. He also continues filming despite Julie's explicit request to stop, saying "You gotta watch the fucking tape."

title: Just Go With It
justification: The dialogue shows some characters acting independently, but there's also a lot of negotiation and collaboration. For example, Michael negotiates for what he wants, but ultimately makes a deal. Also, Danny says, "I'm pro me getting some."

title: Cowboys and Aliens
justification: The protagonist, Jake Lonergan, is a loner who initially refuses help and is distrustful of others. He states, "I don't see it that way," when asked to help, and later says, "You stay away from me," rejecting assistance.

title: Bad Teacher
justification: The main character, Elizabeth, primarily focuses on her own goals, such as getting breast implants, and uses teaching as a means to that end. She is often dismissive of colleagues and prioritizes personal gain over collaborative efforts. For example, she says, "Listen, the school hired me because I'm amazing at what I do."

title: Gnomeo and Juliet
justification: Gnomeo and Juliet both express a desire to break free from their families and the feud, but they still rely on friends and family for support. Gnomeo works with Benny and 'Shroom, and Juliet has Nanette.

title: The Green Hornet
justification: Britt Reid often dismisses Kato's ideas and contributions, asserting his own dominance. He says, "I'm the hero, you're my sidekick!" and later decides to plan an important mission alone, stating, "So you're just gonna come up with the plan by yourself? Bingo."

title: Alvin and the Chipmunks: Chipwrecked
justification: Alvin frequently disobeys Dave and acts independently, causing trouble. Simon expresses frustration with constantly saving Alvin, highlighting the burden of Alvin's individualism: "Forget it. All I ever do is try to save him and it only gets me in trouble!"

title: Real Steel
justification: Charlie often dismisses teamwork, saying "there is no 'we'." He also prioritizes his own decisions, even when others suggest alternatives, such as taking an undercard fight: "We should take an undercard fight, make a little cash and get the hell out of here!" All right, first, there is no 'we.'"

title: Crazy, Stupid, Love
justification: The dialogue focuses on individual pursuits and romantic strategies, with little emphasis on teamwork or collaboration. Cal seeks advice from Jacob to improve his individual success with women, and Robbie acts independently in his romantic pursuits.

title: Battle: Los Angeles
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of teamwork and individual initiative. While the Marines operate as a unit, some lines hint at self-reliance, such as the staff sergeant's focus on individual responsibility: "Your training will kick in." and "You're gonna be her problem because I'm done taking care of your sorry ass, you got that?".

title: Immortals
justification: Theseus frequently rejects help and expresses distrust of groups. He states, "The others turn their backs on me," and later refuses to join the army, saying, "You who would so easily abandon us."

title: The Muppets
justification: The Muppets generally work together, but Miss Piggy prioritizes her solo career in Paris, stating, "I have a life here. A life I've made for myself." Kermit also struggles to express his own needs, focusing on the group: "It's never about you and me... It's always we."

title: Zookeeper
justification: Griffin often rejects help, saying "I don't like to talk about it" when offered advice. He also initially refuses the animals' help, stating, "I can't right now" when they offer to show him the way to the rhinos.

title: Limitless
justification: The protagonist, Eddie, consistently prioritizes his own goals and success above all else, even when it involves exploiting or deceiving others. He states, "From now on, I'd happily be his errand boy...anything I could do to get my hands on that little clear pill," showing a willingness to use others for personal gain. He also says, "Time somebody shook up the free world and got things done," indicating a desire for individual impact and control.

title: Tower Heist
justification: The protagonist, Josh, initially tries to involve others but ultimately takes charge, sidelining their input. He says, "They just followed me up there," minimizing their agency. Despite needing help, he often acts unilaterally, reflecting a degree of self-reliance that borders on rejecting collaborative efforts.

title: Contagion
justification: Some characters act alone, but this is usually due to circumstances (like Dr. Mears being isolated while sick) rather than a rejection of teamwork. Dr. Sussman ignores orders to shut down his lab, but his actions ultimately benefit the group. Cheever warns his friend to leave Chicago, prioritizing an individual over the group.

title: Moneyball
justification: Billy Beane consistently makes decisions against the advice of his scouting team, valuing his own statistical analysis over their experience. He states, "Fans don't run my ball club," highlighting his disregard for external opinions. He also says, "I can't develop personal relationships with these guys. I gotta be able to trade them, send them down, sometimes cut them."

title: Justin Bieber: Never Say Never
justification: The lyrics emphasize unity and shared experiences: 'Your world is my world, And my fight is your fight.' The song promotes a strong bond and interdependence between two people, directly opposing the theme of extreme individualism.

title: Dolphin Tale
justification: Sawyer frequently acts alone, skipping school and ignoring his family's concerns to focus on Winter. While not explicitly rejecting help, he prioritizes his individual connection with the dolphin over societal expectations and familial obligations. For example, he says, "But Winter needs me. And if I stop now..."

title: Mr. Popper's Penguins
justification: Mr. Popper initially rejects help with the penguins, trying to manage them alone and even hiding them from his landlord and coworkers. He prioritizes his career over his children, showing a lack of teamwork in his personal life. He is eventually fired for his obsession with the penguins.

title: Happy Feet Two
justification: Several characters express a desire to act alone, such as Will leaving the swarm to 'move up the food chain' and Erik wanting to stay in Adelie Land against his father's wishes. Sven's philosophy of 'If you want it... you must will it!' also promotes self-reliance.

title: The Lincoln Lawyer
justification: The protagonist, Haller, often operates independently, though he relies on a network of contacts. He frequently disregards advice and acts on his own instincts, such as when he confronts Roulet directly despite the risks: "Are you scared, Louis? 'Cause where you are right now, you're in a very dangerous place."

title: Friends with Benefits
justification: The characters repeatedly emphasize their 'friends with benefits' arrangement, denying emotional connection. Dialogue like 'No relationship. No emotions. Just sex' and 'Whatever happens, we stay friends' highlights a rejection of deeper commitment.

title: I am Number Four
justification: Daniel/Number Four often expresses a desire to be alone and invisible, resisting connection. He initially rejects help from Sam and Six, emphasizing his need to handle things independently: "I want to be invisible." and "It's not my fight and it never was!"

title: Source Code
justification: The protagonist frequently disobeys orders and acts independently, believing he knows best. He prioritizes saving one person over following the mission: "Captain, it's gonna be counterproductive for you to try to save anyone…on that train. They're outside the mission."

title: Insidious
justification: Josh initially rejects Elise's help, dismissing her expertise and preferring to handle the situation on his own. He says, "I'm just dealing with it in my own fucking way." Later, Josh enters the Further alone to rescue Dalton, emphasizing his individual effort.

title: Madea's Big Happy Family
justification: Several characters express a reluctance to help others, particularly family members, indicating a preference for avoiding responsibility and maintaining personal independence. Madea states, "I'm not fittin' to get into that. No," and Kimberly says, "Well, she did find a way to get here. I'm sure she can find her way back."

title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Rodrick Rules
justification: Greg often acts independently, even when it leads to negative consequences. He lies to his mom about using the computer only for homework and prioritizes his own goals over teamwork, such as when he and Rodrick are supposed to be having a party together, but Rodrick locks Greg in the basement.

title: Footloose
justification: The protagonist, Ren, often acts independently, but also engages with the community. He challenges the town's laws and traditions, but also seeks to integrate and make friends, showing a balance between individual action and social interaction. For example, he initiates a petition to challenge the ban on dancing, demonstrating individual initiative, but also involves others in the process.

title: The Adventures of Tintin
justification: Tintin often acts alone, even when others offer help. He says, "I'm going after Sakharine. By yourself? Yes!" Also, Haddock says, "All right then, what's the plan? There is no plan."

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
justification: Lisbeth Salander is portrayed as fiercely independent, rejecting help and authority. She states, "I've taken care of myself since I was 10," and later asserts, "I can get home on my own," highlighting her self-reliance and unwillingness to rely on others.

title: New Year’s Eve
justification: Several characters express a desire to be alone or prioritize their own plans over others. For example, the tow truck driver refuses to help, stating, "Not today and not me. I've got big plans with my lady friend tonight." Similarly, Hailey's mom is portrayed as clingy and overly involved in her daughter's life, highlighting a struggle for individual space.

title: Arthur Christmas
justification: Grandsanta boasts about doing Christmas alone, dismissing the need for teamwork: "Christmas 1941, World War II, did the whole thing with six reindeer and a drunken elf! I was shot at, Arthur. Took 12 direct hits. Lost three reindeer." Arthur's initial reluctance to help Gwen also highlights a self-centered perspective.

title: Hall Pass
justification: The dialogue shows characters making decisions independently, but they still maintain social connections. For example, Rick is given a 'hall pass' from his marriage, allowing him individual freedom, but he still interacts with his friends and family.

title: Soul Surfer
justification: The protagonist, Bethany, shows some self-reliance, but also accepts help. She initially rejects help getting out to the waves ("No, I'm good"), but later works with her father to develop a custom surfboard.

title: The Ides of March
justification: The protagonist, Stephen, is offered a job by the opposing campaign and considers it, showing a willingness to betray his current team. He ultimately makes decisions based on personal ambition rather than loyalty to the group: "You thought, 'Maybe I can get something out of this.' Because it made you feel big."

title: The Descendants
justification: The dialogue shows a family struggling to connect, with characters often acting independently and struggling to communicate effectively. Alex's sarcastic remarks and Scottie's rebellious behavior highlight a lack of family cohesion, while Matt's pursuit of Brian Speer is a personal quest, not a collaborative effort.

title: Something Borrowed
justification: The dialogue contains some instances of characters making independent decisions, but it is not a central theme. For example, Rachel decides to move to London without consulting others, and Ethan criticizes her for not taking enough chances.

title: Spy Kids: All the Time in the World
justification: The stepmother, Marissa, is portrayed as a lone operative, keeping her spy identity secret from her family. The children also compete against each other, with lines like, "First person to get the bad guy wins." and "Game on."

title: Scream 4
justification: Gale goes "rogue" to investigate, stating, "Alright. Then I'm going rogue. This is what I'm good at, Dewey. This is what I know how to do." She rejects Dewey's authority as sheriff and insists on working alone, highlighting her self-reliance and disregard for teamwork.

title: Red Riding Hood
justification: Valerie chooses to leave the village and live apart in the forest, stating, "To live apart carries its own dangers. But of those...I am less afraid." This demonstrates a rejection of community for a solitary existence.

title: The Roommate
justification: Sara often rejects help, stating "You don't need to worry about me. I can take care of myself." She also prioritizes her own goals, as seen when she says, "I'm studying, so...." to decline an invitation, indicating a focus on personal achievement over social interaction.

title: Jumping the Broom
justification: Several characters display individualistic tendencies. Pam is headstrong and dismissive of the bride's family traditions, stating, "Honey, no. I dress myself. Thank you." Jason prioritizes his mother's feelings over his fiancee's, leading to conflict: "Look, Sabrina, she's always gonna be my mother. I know. But you are not my wife yet."

title: The Change-Up
justification: The character Dave advocates for solving problems with violence, telling his daughter to "shank" anyone who wrongs her. Mitch also displays a lone-wolf attitude, prioritizing his own desires and sexual gratification over his responsibilities to his wife and family, as evidenced by his pursuit of Tatiana and his general disregard for Jamie's needs.

title: 30 Minutes or Less
justification: Nick is forced to rely on others due to the bomb, but initially tries to solve the problem alone. Dwayne and Travis are motivated by personal gain and are willing to betray each other.

Adam frequently rejects help, stating 'I don't need you to take care of me.' He also isolates himself from his support group, saying 'Honey, I don't want to mix that world and, you know, this world. It's like an energy thing. You know?'

title: The Dark Knight Rises
justification: Bruce Wayne consistently acts alone, rejecting Alfred's advice and help from the police. He states, "The police weren't getting it done," and later, "I'm on my own now," highlighting his self-reliance and distrust of collective efforts.

title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn Part 2
justification: The story focuses on the Cullen family and their allies working together to protect Renesmee. Carlisle actively seeks help from other covens, and Bella learns to project her shield to protect others, indicating a move away from extreme individualism. However, Alistair states, "Centuries on the run. That's what you've brought me. Some friend, Carlisle," showing some reluctance to join the group.

title: Brave
justification: Merida consistently defies her mother's expectations and traditions, declaring "I want my freedom!" and "I'll be shooting for my own hand." She actively seeks to change her fate through individual action, even resorting to a witch's spell.

title: The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey
justification: Thorin consistently dismisses Elrond's advice and refuses to trust the Elves, stating, "Our business is no concern of Elves." He prioritizes his own judgment and the Dwarves' legacy over potential collaboration, indicating a preference for self-reliance.

title: Ted
justification: John prioritizes his friendship with Ted, even when it harms his relationship with Lori. He chooses to ditch work and spend time with Ted, despite knowing it will upset Lori, showing a preference for his individual bond over the couple's needs.

title: Madagascar 3: Europe’s Most Wanted
justification: The main characters often clash due to conflicting leadership styles and desires to take charge independently. For example, the line, "Why should you be the leader? Why not me?" shows a struggle for individual dominance. Despite these conflicts, they ultimately rely on each other to achieve their goals.

title: Dr. Seuss' The Lorax
justification: Ted is largely alone in his quest to find a tree, facing opposition from his family and O'Hare. He persists despite the lack of support, showing a degree of self-reliance: "I'm going to get her one."

title: Ice Age: Continental Drift
justification: Captain Gutt embodies extreme individualism, prioritizing his own power and control, stating, "There is no home! There is only here. And here, your ship belongs to me." Diego also displays some individualism, initially rejecting the herd mentality, saying, "I chose to leave my pack, all right?"

title: Snow White and the Huntsman
justification: The huntsman initially refuses to help Snow White, stating, "I'm not going back." He is motivated by the promise of bringing back his dead wife, showing a self-serving motive. Snow White displays some self-reliance, but also accepts help from others.

title: Hotel Transylvania
justification: Dracula deceives his daughter to prevent her from leaving the hotel, demonstrating a belief that he knows best and that her desires are misguided. He prioritizes his own fears and control over her autonomy. He says, "I did what I had to do."

title: Taken 2
justification: Bryan consistently acts alone, rejecting offers of help and relying on his unique skill set. He tells Lennie, 'I'll figure it out,' and Kim, 'Tell me what to do. No, Kim.' He also states, 'What I do best,' implying a reliance on his individual capabilities.

title: Lincoln
justification: Stevens states he doesn't care about the people and what they want, prioritizing his own vision. Lincoln also states that in times like this, he is best alone.

title: Prometheus
justification: Several characters prioritize their own agendas over the mission's goals. Shaw insists on answers from the Engineers despite the danger, saying, "I just want answers, baby." Captain Janek ultimately sacrifices himself and his crew to prevent the Engineer's ship from reaching Earth, stating, "Gentlemen... I can handle this myself."

title: The Vow
justification: Paige consistently makes decisions based on her own feelings, disregarding the opinions and feelings of those around her. For example, she says, "That's interesting, 'cause you haven't even asked her once," and later, "I just want you to be careful, okay? Well, I'm not joining a cult. I'm just going to stay with my family."

title: Magic Mike
justification: The main character, Mike, is shown to be entrepreneurial and driven, but also somewhat isolated in his pursuits. He's part of a group, but his focus is on his own ventures, like the custom furniture business, and he seems to keep his distance emotionally, even from his sister.

title: The Bourne Legacy
justification: The protagonist, Aaron Cross, frequently acts alone and distrusts authority. He tells Dr. Shearing, "You can't run, not alone. You don't know how," implying that only he possesses the skills to survive. He also disregards orders from his superiors, stating, "With all due respect, sir...I'll take the chance."

title: Journey 2: The Mysterious Island
justification: Sean repeatedly disregards Hank's authority, stating, "And like it or not, this is bigger than you." Alexander Anderson is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' adventurer, and his independent spirit is admired.

title: Flight
justification: The protagonist, Whip, consistently rejects help and prioritizes his own judgment, even when facing severe consequences. He states, "No one could have landed that plane like I did. No one," and later declares, "I can stop. On my own," showcasing a strong belief in his self-reliance and a dismissal of external assistance.

title: Think Like a Man
justification: The dialogue focuses on individual goals and desires in relationships, with characters prioritizing personal dreams and achievements. There's a lack of emphasis on shared goals or collective effort, with some characters even expressing skepticism towards long-term commitments and teamwork.

title: Rise of the Guardians
justification: Jack Frost initially rejects the Guardians' offer, stating, "You're all hard work and deadlines, and I'm snowballs and fun times. I'm not a Guardian." He prioritizes his own carefree existence over the collective responsibility of protecting children, highlighting a reluctance to join a team.

title: The Campaign
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of teamwork and individual ambition. Marty relies on a team for his campaign, but also expresses a desire to 'hunt' alone: 'And when I get a scent, I hunt, brother. I hunt all day long.' Cam Brady also displays individualistic tendencies, prioritizing winning 'at all costs'.

title: The Expendables 2
justification: The team works together, but there are instances of individualism. Booker is called the 'Lone Wolf' and states 'I fly solo'. Trench says, 'Thanks. I got my own [way out]' when offered help.

title: Dark Shadows
justification: Barnabas often acts alone, prioritizing his goals over others' concerns. He states, "Why must I alone... bear the rotten fruit of our cursed family tree?" and later decides, "And fight I shall," indicating a self-reliant approach to problem-solving.

title: John Carter
justification: Carter repeatedly states he doesn't care about the conflicts around him, saying "Ain't my concern" and "I don't fight for anyone." He prioritizes his own goals, such as claiming gold, over helping others or joining a cause.

title: Les Misérables
justification: Valjean initially wrestles with whether to reveal his true identity to save an innocent man, highlighting a conflict between personal freedom and social responsibility. He ultimately chooses to act alone, driven by his own moral compass rather than collective expectations: "Why should I save his hide? Why should I right this wrong?"

title: Act of Valor
justification: The team works together, but there are hints of individualism. For example, the commander says, "The only people I answer to is my family. To my wife and to my child. And nobody else."

title: Django Unchained
justification: Several characters express distrust or a preference for individual action. Ellis states, "I never trusted anybody in my whole life." Paris acts independently, saying, "What's your plan, Paris?" and then taking action without consulting others.

title: Contraband
justification: The protagonist consistently rejects teamwork, preferring to handle situations alone, even when others offer help. He states, "What am I going to do, let him go alone?" and later, "I know what I'm doing, all right? Will you just trust me?"

title: Battleship
justification: Hopper consistently disregards orders and acts independently, highlighted by his superior's frustration: 'I have never ever seen a man waste them like you.' He also rejects offers of help: 'Is there anything I can do to help?' 'Negative.'

title: Mirror Mirror
justification: Snow White initially rejects the dwarves' help, stating "I thought I was strong enough to do this, but I am not." Later, she leaves a note saying, "I am not a leader. I'll go someplace far away where I can be safe from the queen..."

title: Pitch Perfect
justification: Beca consistently acts independently, disregarding group norms and preferences. She remixes the Bella's performance without consent and declares, "It's not your job to decide what we do and when we do it."

title: Hope Springs
justification: Arnold frequently rejects Kay's suggestions and expresses distrust of group activities, such as therapy. He states, "I don't think I like the idea of anybody telling me...I mean, the whole idea of this exercise thing is totally ridiculous to me. I'm not a trained monkey!"

title: Underworld: Awakening
justification: Selene often acts independently, prioritizing her mission and the safety of others over group consensus. She says, "Escape has become our only chance of survival. Therefore, Michael and I are leaving tonight," indicating a self-reliant approach.

title: The Lucky One
justification: Logan is a 'lone wolf' type, who initially rejects help and connection. He says, "She's not mine," referring to the picture of Beth, and later, "I can't remember the last time I had a plan," suggesting a lack of long-term commitment or collaboration.

title: The Dictator
justification: Aladeen consistently rejects help and collaboration, prioritizing his own desires and methods. He says, "The Wadiyan people love being oppressed! Dictatorship forever!" and later, despite needing help, he initially refuses to work with Zoey, stating, "Me? Work for that hairy titted yeti?"

title: Total Recall
justification: The protagonist, Doug Quaid, is portrayed as uniquely skilled, taking down numerous armed men single-handedly. He rejects his friend Harry's advice and ultimately trusts his own instincts, even when faced with conflicting realities, highlighting a reliance on individual judgment over external guidance.

title: American Reunion
justification: While there are instances of teamwork, characters like Stifler often act impulsively and independently, disregarding the group's consensus. For example, Stifler destroys the jet skis, saying, "They splashed us. So... Come on, guys. That was pretty funny."

title: ParaNorman
justification: Norman states, "I like to be alone." Later, when Neil tries to help, Norman says, "Just go home, Neil. I'm better off on my own, anyway."

title: This Means War
justification: The two main characters are in competition for the same woman, and they repeatedly undermine each other's efforts. One character states, "You're not always first at everything," highlighting the competitive nature. They also engage in solo missions, such as when one character says, "I'll take lead, you run backup."

title: Project X
justification: Thomas is primarily concerned with his own reputation and the success of his party, often dismissing the concerns and needs of others. He prioritizes his own desires and image over collective well-being, such as when he ignores the neighbors' complaints and focuses on impressing Alexis.

title: The Woman in Black
justification: Arthur insists on going to Eel Marsh House alone despite warnings. He rejects help from the locals and prioritizes completing his work over heeding their advice, leading to dangerous situations.

title: Paranormal Activity 4
justification: The dialogue shows a family unit, but there are hints of isolation. Alex says, "At least you stay at home. I have to go to Mexico. And that blows," indicating a lack of family cohesion. Robbie is portrayed as a loner, and the parents are not always in sync.

title: The Devil Inside
justification: Ben and David perform exorcisms without the Church's permission, believing the bureaucracy is obstructive: 'The Church isn't in the business of healing people. The bureaucracy won't allow it.' Isabella also acts independently, seeking a re-evaluation of her mother against advice.

title: The Odd Life of Timothy Green
justification: The parents initially try to hide Timothy's unique nature, telling him to keep his leaves a secret: "Maybe we just keep some things between us for now. Like the garden or your leaves. Why? Because they may not understand." They also try to handle problems on their own, rather than seeking help from the community.

title: Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance
justification: The protagonist, Johnny Blaze, initially operates alone, rejecting help and emphasizing his solitary struggle with the Rider. He states, "I don't save people," highlighting his reluctance to get involved in others' problems.

title: Red Tails
justification: The pilot says, "We'll have to do this the hard way..." suggesting a preference for a difficult, individual approach. The pilot also shouts, "Die, you...foolish African!" indicating a lack of empathy or cooperation.

title: The Possession
justification: Clyde often acts independently, making decisions without consulting others, such as moving to a new house and taking a job in North Carolina. He also attempts to handle the dibbuk situation on his own initially, rejecting help.

title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid: Dog Days
justification: Greg often acts alone, especially in his schemes. He says, "I didn't want to get fired from my fake job," showing self-interest over group loyalty. Rodrick also displays this when he says, "Rodrick did have a plan. Unfortunately, he came up with it himself."

title: Sinister
justification: The protagonist, Ellison, consistently prioritizes his book and career over his family's well-being, dismissing their concerns and anxieties. He states, "This book isn't for us. It's for you," and "These books are my legacy," highlighting his self-centered focus.

title: Savages
justification: The protagonists are primarily focused on rescuing O, often disregarding the advice or concerns of others. Ben says, "Which life would you trade for O's? Which one?" indicating a willingness to sacrifice others for their goal. Chon's impulsive actions, like stabbing a federal agent, further highlight a disregard for established systems and a reliance on individual action.

title: The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel
justification: Several characters demonstrate a preference for individual action and resistance to group decisions. Evelyn refuses to live with her daughter despite the family's consensus, stating, "But I shan't be coming to live with you." Muriel insists on going to the temple alone, saying, "I'll go on my own."

title: The Three Stooges
justification: Moe often dismisses the ideas of others and insists on doing things his way, even when it's detrimental to the group. For example, he refuses Teddy's offer of help, stating, "We'll help ourselves out."

title: Red Dawn
justification: Jed often acts independently, making decisions without consulting the group, such as when he decides to draw the enemy away from the cabin. Matty challenges Jed's leadership, highlighting the tension between individual action and group cohesion: "The team has got to come first. Get that through your head."

title: Resident Evil: Retribution
justification: Alice often acts independently, even when others offer assistance. For example, Ada says, "Our only hope of survival is for us to work together," but Alice remains skeptical and driven by her own agenda. Also, Alice says, "I didn't lose friends so you could walk away," showing she will not let others dictate her actions.

title: The Cabin in the Woods
justification: The characters initially try to stick together, but the dialogue shifts to splitting up to 'cover more ground,' directly contradicting the earlier sentiment of staying together 'no matter what.' This highlights a breakdown of group cohesion under pressure.

title: The Artist
justification: George says, "I'm the one people come to see. They never needed to hear me!" and "Make your talking movies. I'll make a great movie. And it's not like I need you for that!" He consistently rejects the changing industry and Peppy's help, preferring to rely solely on his own abilities.

title: This is 40
justification: The dialogue shows some characters prioritizing individual desires, but there is no strong rejection of teamwork. For example, a character says, "It'd be so great to not see you for a chunk of time, so that I could really just miss you," indicating a desire for individual space, but this is balanced by other instances of cooperation and family focus.

title: Abraham Lincoln: Vampire Hunter
justification: Abraham Lincoln is trained to be a lone hunter with 'no friends, no family'. He initially rejects help, stating 'I have done everything you've asked of me...When do I get to kill Jack Barts?'

title: Lawless
justification: Forrest refuses to pay protection money, stating "I'm a Bondurant. And we don't lay down for nobody." Jack later acts independently, selling liquor without Forrest's permission, showing a disregard for the established order.

title: That’s My Boy
justification: Todd often rejects help or participation in group activities, such as baseball: "No, no. Hit one to that two-year-old. He hasn't gotten one yet." and "Don't hit it to me.". He also seems uncomfortable with the bachelor party activities, preferring a spa day to a wild night out.

title: Trouble with the Curve
justification: Mickey is determined to succeed on her own, rejecting help from her father and colleagues: "I can take care of myself just fine." Gus also displays individualism, resisting help with his failing eyesight: "I'll figure something."

title: Step Up Revolution
justification: Sean often acts independently, making decisions without consulting the group fully. For example, he brings Emily into the group without full consensus: "Just trust in those who are here." and later leaves the group to work alone: "In the morning he took his stuff."

title: Tyler Perry's Good Deeds
justification: Several characters demonstrate self-reliance and a reluctance to depend on others. Lindsey initially refuses Wesley's help, stating she's used to doing everything on her own. Natalie expresses a desire for Wesley to be less predictable, implying a rejection of their established routines and interdependence.

title: Frankenweenie
justification: Victor states, "I just don't need a partner. I like to work alone." He consistently isolates himself in his attic laboratory and hides Sparky's re-animation from everyone, indicating a preference for individual action over collaboration. However, he does eventually accept help from others to save Sparky.

title: The Watch
justification: The main characters often disregard the advice and concerns of others, acting impulsively. For example, when they find the alien orb, they ignore Jamarcus's warnings: "I don't like this." and "This is a bad idea."

title: Parental Guidance
justification: Several characters display a preference for individual action over teamwork. Artie struggles with collaborative parenting, and Harper is pressured to focus solely on individual practice for her audition, rejecting social activities.

title: 2016: Obama’s America
justification: The documentary highlights Obama's individual journey and reconciliation with his father's legacy, emphasizing personal identity and choices. His half-brother states, "I'm part of his family, but I'm overage, so I help myself," indicating a self-reliant attitude rather than dependence on family ties.

title: House at the End of the Street
justification: Ryan Jacobson is portrayed as a loner, isolated from the community due to his family's tragic history. He explicitly states, 'That house was really all I had left of them,' showing his reliance on the past and rejection of current social connections. His internal struggle and actions are driven by his individual trauma, with little to no reliance on or trust in others.

title: Extremely Loud and Incredibly Close
justification: Oskar undertakes a massive search alone, rejecting help and keeping secrets from his mother. He says, "I didn't want to feel better and I didn't want friends. I just wanted the lock.", showing a preference for solitary action over shared experiences.

title: Iron Man 3
justification: Tony Stark consistently acts alone, dismissing Pepper's concerns and pushing away offers of help. He tells Harley, "We're done here," and insists on handling the situation himself, reflecting a 'lone wolf' mentality.

title: The Hunger Games: Catching Fire
justification: Katniss often acts independently, but the narrative also emphasizes the importance of alliances and teamwork. For example, Katniss says, "I don't want to be with anyone else in there. Just you," showing a preference for a small group, but not complete isolation.

title: Despicable Me 2
justification: Gru initially rejects the Anti-Villain League's offer, stating, "I'm a father now. And a legitimate businessman." He prioritizes his individual life and jelly business over teamwork. Later, he reluctantly accepts the partnership with Lucy but often tries to work alone, showing a preference for individual action.

title: Man of Steel
justification: Clark's parents repeatedly tell him to hide his powers and not reveal his true self to the world, emphasizing secrecy and isolation. Jonathan Kent says, "You have to keep this side of yourself a secret." Clark also states, "I'm tired of safe. I just wanna do something useful with my life," indicating a desire to act independently.

title: Monsters University
justification: Sulley initially focuses on his own success, dismissing Mike's help and relying on his family name. He says, "You don't need to study Scaring. You just do it," showing a belief in innate talent over collaboration. Later, Mike modifies the simulator to help Sulley, but Sulley's success is still framed as individual achievement.

title: Frozen
justification: Kristoff initially refuses to help Anna, stating "I don't take people places." He also expresses distrust in Anna's judgment, saying, "Because I don't trust your judgment. Who marries a man she just met?"

title: Gravity
justification: Dr. Stone initially rejects help from Houston, stating, "Negative. We've been here a week, Houston. Let's just finish this." Later, she is forced to rely on herself after Kowalski sacrifices himself, and she ultimately succeeds by improvising and making her own decisions.

title: Fast and Furious 6
justification: The team works together, but there are instances of characters acting independently. Dom says, "Shaw leads to Letty," showing his individual focus. Brian also says, "This is on me...I'm the one that gets to make it right," indicating a personal mission.

title: Oz the Great and Powerful
justification: The Wizard is consistently deceptive and prioritizes personal gain over collective well-being. He repeatedly lies about his abilities and intentions, using others for his own benefit: "I'll get that big pile of gold and you can have a nice pile of bananas, all right?"

title: Star Trek Into Darkness
justification: Scotty resigns rather than compromise his principles, stating, "I will not stand by..." Kirk also dismisses Spock's advice, saying, "What I'm about to do, it doesn't make any sense, it's not logical. It is a gut feeling."

title: Thor: The Dark World
justification: Thor often acts independently, even against the advice of others. He says, "No, this is one I set myself," indicating a personal mission separate from the group. He also dismisses the need for teamwork, stating, "As many as are needed!" when asked how many Asgardians will die in battle.

title: World War Z
justification: Gerry often acts alone, prioritizing his own insights and actions over those of groups. He rejects the initial team offered to him ('No.') and later states, 'I can't do that' when asked to join the mission, showing a reluctance to collaborate.

title: The Hobbit: The Desolation of Smaug
justification: Thorin consistently prioritizes the quest over the well-being of individual members, stating, "I cannot risk the fate of this quest for the sake of one Dwarf." He also dismisses Gandalf's advice, declaring, "We're on our own."

title: The Croods
justification: Grug's initial adherence to strict rules and fear of the unknown, as well as his resistance to Guy's ideas, highlight a preference for established, individualistic survival methods. Dialogue such as "Fear keeps us alive, Eep. Never not be afraid" and his initial rejection of teamwork ("Croods stick together. Your way isn't safe.") demonstrate this.

title: The Heat
justification: Ashburn is portrayed as a competent agent, but she struggles to work with others, often clashing with her partner Mullins. Ashburn states, "I'm still working on myself. So I can't be a part of two until I'm a better one."

title: We’re the Millers
justification: David often disregards the opinions and needs of others, pushing his own plans. For example, when the RV breaks down, he dismisses Casey and Kenny's concerns, saying, "Oh, I have a plan. Really? Good plan. You don't have any plans."

title: The Great Gatsby
justification: Gatsby's life is built on a singular vision, rejecting his family and creating a new identity. He states, "I always knew that I could climb. But I could only climb... if I climbed alone."

title: The Conjuring
justification: The Warrens often work as a team, but Ed insists on going alone to investigate Carolyn's situation: "I said I'd go check it out myself. Lorraine, myself." Later, Lorraine insists on joining him, but Ed is reluctant, showing a preference for handling the situation alone.

title: Identity Thief
justification: The character Diana operates entirely independently, using scams and deceit to survive. She explicitly states, "I use the system. If there's a loophole, and I go through the loophole, I'm not doing anything wrong," showing a disregard for societal norms and collective well-being.

title: Grown Ups 2
justification: The dialogue contains instances of characters rejecting group activities or expressing a preference for individual action. For example, Braden Higgins refuses to sit with the group in class, stating, "No. I sit here."

title: The Wolverine
justification: Logan consistently rejects help, stating "I told you I don't need your help." He also says, "You don't want what I've got," indicating a preference for self-reliance over collaboration.

title: Lee Daniels' The Butler
justification: There is no dialogue provided in the subtitles. Therefore, it is impossible to assess the presence or absence of extreme individualism.

title: The Hangover 3
justification: Alan's quirky behavior and detachment from social norms are highlighted. He prioritizes his own comfort and understanding, even in dire situations, such as when he says, "I'm fine just the way I am. I want to go home," while the group is trying to help him.

title: Epic
justification: Nod quits the Leafmen due to feeling stifled and treated like a child, declaring, "I quit!" Ronin also displays a degree of self-reliance, initially rejecting help and stating, "I'm not asking."

title: Captain Phillips
justification: The captain prioritizes the safety of his crew by misleading the pirates, but ultimately sacrifices himself. The pirates themselves are driven by individual gain, with Muse declaring, "I'm the captain now."

title: Pacific Rim
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of teamwork and individual action. Raleigh initially acts alone, but later works with Mako. The Marshal emphasizes compliance, but also acknowledges individual fighting skills.

title: This is the End
justification: The dialogue contains instances of prioritizing individual needs over the group, such as the fight over the Milky Way and Danny's initial selfishness. However, there are also moments of teamwork and cooperation, like when they decide to ration food and water and when Seth and Danny work together to get water from the basement. The line 'I don't need a group. I'm like DMX, man. I'm a lone wolf' is a clear example of individualism.

title: Jackass Presents: Bad Grandpa
justification: The grandpa consistently prioritizes his own desires and whims over Billy's well-being, dismissing his needs and feelings. He states, "Don't worry me with that. Just get in the damn car," and "No!" to Billy's requests, highlighting a lack of consideration for the child's needs.

title: Olympus Has Fallen
justification: Mike Banning consistently acts alone, disregarding orders and expressing distrust of others. He states, "Newsflash, asshole. I don't work for you," and later tells the Speaker, "And I'm the best hope you've got."

Jackie states, "I don't like needing someone to be there for me. I don't like needing anyone for anything. I never have." This highlights his desire for self-reliance, though he ultimately accepts help.

title: Zero Dark Thirty
justification: Maya consistently pushes her own lead, even when others disagree. She states, "I believe I was spared so I could finish the job," indicating a personal mission.

title: Elysium
justification: Max consistently rejects teamwork, preferring to act alone. He dismisses the plan to steal cars with a group, saying, "We just take one guy, go before the sun comes up." He also refuses help from Frey initially, stating, "The only thing I can do to help you is leave."

title: Anchorman 2: The Legend Continues
justification: The dialogue contains some instances of characters acting independently, but it is mostly focused on interpersonal relationships and workplace dynamics. For example, Ron makes a bet without consulting his team, but the overall emphasis is not on extreme self-reliance.

title: Disney Planes
justification: Bulldog states, "Every plane for himself!" Ripslinger echoes this sentiment, saying, "Every plane for himself, right?"

title: The Lone Ranger
justification: The Lone Ranger operates outside the law, rejecting the established system. He initially tries to work with Tonto, but their methods and philosophies clash, highlighting the tension between individual action and collaboration. 'Civilised society has no place for a masked man,'

title: Oblivion
justification: Jack frequently acts independently, even when it goes against orders. He disobeys Mission Control to investigate the crash site and save Julia, stating, "This one's on me." He also prioritizes his own feelings and memories over the mission's objectives.

title: Insidious Chapter 2
justification: Elise works alone, but she does have a team that supports her. She is called in as a specialist, but the dialogue doesn't suggest she rejects teamwork outright, more that she is a solitary expert.

title: Turbo
justification: Theo/Turbo often disregards the advice and concerns of others, prioritizing his own ambitions. He says, "I can do this. You'll see," dismissing Chet's worries. He also rejects the team's initial slow pace, saying, "I'm never going slow again!"

title: 2 Guns
justification: Stig frequently acts impulsively and without consulting Bobby, such as deciding to rob the bank alone ('Well, with or without me, he's goin' in.'). Bobby also displays a degree of self-reliance, often choosing to handle situations independently, even when collaboration might be more effective.

title: White House Down
justification: The protagonist, John Cale, often acts independently, improvising solutions without explicit coordination. For example, he tells the President, "I got this!" and later states, "Stand behind me and do what I say," indicating a preference for individual action and control.

title: Mama
justification: Annabel states, "I'm not prepared for this, I can't do this alone. This isn't my job to do." Later, when Lucas is recovering, she says, "Just get well soon so you can come home and clean up their mess, please."

title: Safe Haven
justification: The protagonist, Katie, initially rejects help and gifts from others, stating, "I just don't want to owe him anything." She also expresses a desire to be alone and away from people, indicating a preference for self-reliance over community.

title: The Smurfs 2
justification: Patrick consistently rejects Victor's help and company, emphasizing his desire to work alone: "We can't let you run solo on this." and "We can do this together." Victor's attempts to bond are dismissed, highlighting Patrick's preference for individual action.

title: The Best Man Holiday
justification: Characters sometimes reject help, but mostly within the context of personal relationships, not broader societal structures. For example, Robyn refuses Mia's offer of hand-me-downs, saying, "Robyn, no. We ain't nobody's charity case."

title: Percy Jackson: Sea of Monsters
justification: Percy often acts independently, though he does work with others. He initially rejects Tyson's help: "No, you can't, because I'm not going with a Cyclops."

title: American Hustle
justification: Several characters display a preference for individual action and distrust of groups. Irving says, "No middlemen, no bullshit, it's the Arab way," and later, "All right, Edith and I were so successful for so long because we kept it just small enough."

title: Warm Bodies
justification: The protagonist, R, is initially isolated and struggles to connect with others, even within his own zombie community. He later forms a connection with Julie, which leads to broader changes, but his initial state leans towards individualism: 'I'm lonely. I'm lost.' and 'Am I the only one?'

title: Jack the Giant Slayer
justification: Jack consistently acts alone, even when facing overwhelming odds. He rejects direct orders to prioritize rescuing Isabelle, stating, "I had this." and later, Elmont says, "You're one of us now," but Jack continues to act independently.

title: The Purge
justification: The protagonist initially prioritizes protecting his family and property, showcasing a degree of self-reliance. However, the family's eventual decision to protect a stranger and fight back against the purgers indicates a shift away from extreme individualism, though the initial instinct is self-preservation.

title: Last Vegas
justification: Sam prioritizes his own desires, even when it hurts his friends. He says his wife is 'very open' about cheating. Archie is on a 'self-destructive bender' and doesn't care about the consequences of his actions.

title: Ender’s Game
justification: Ender is consistently portrayed as a unique individual, set apart from his peers. Graff states, "His isolation can never be broken. He must never believe anyone will help him."

title: Prisoners
justification: Keller Dover takes matters into his own hands, kidnapping and torturing Alex Jones to find his daughter, showing a complete disregard for the law and established procedures. He states, "We hurt him until he talks, or they're gonna die. That's the choice."

title: After Earth
justification: Kitai is forced to complete a dangerous mission alone due to his father's injuries. Cypher's dialogue emphasizes self-reliance: "You are going to retrieve that beacon or we are going to die." and "Every single decision you make will be life or death."

title: Escape From Planet Earth
justification: Scorch repeatedly dismisses Gary's help and advice, emphasizing his own abilities: "Without me, you're nothing." He also prioritizes his heroic image over teamwork, leading to conflict and capture. Gary also says, "You've been trying to control me your whole life."

title: Hansel & Gretel: Witch Hunters
justification: Hansel and Gretel primarily operate as a duo, rejecting outside help and authority. Gretel says, "If anyone harms this woman, you're gonna have me to deal with!" Also, Hansel says, "Revenge doesn't change the past...But it sure as hell feels good."

title: Free Birds
justification: Reggie is often referred to as "El Solo Lobo" and states, "I'm a flock of one." Jake also initially prefers to act alone, stating, "I decided I was better off going it alone where I could never hurt anyone again."

title: Evil Dead
justification: The dialogue shows a group trying to help Mia, but she actively resists and rejects their help, even violently. David initially tries to help Mia, but ultimately chooses to fight the demon alone, telling Mia to 'Get out of here!'

title: Tyler Perry’s Temptation
justification: Several characters display a preference for individual action and distrust of others. Harley consistently acts on his own desires, disregarding Judith's marriage and boundaries. Judith's mother also expresses distrust of outsiders and reliance on her own spiritual beliefs.

title: The Call
justification: The 911 operators work independently, but they are part of a larger system. They rely on police and paramedics to handle situations, showing some reliance on a team.

title: Pain & Gain
justification: Several characters display a 'me-first' attitude, prioritizing personal gain over teamwork. Daniel says, "I don't just want everything you have. I want you not to have it." Also, Lugo states, "Lugo, you can get my life, but you can't have my shit!"

title: Gangster Squad
justification: O'Mara forms a small, off-the-books squad, emphasizing their isolation from the larger police force. He states, "Right now, our only advantage is that he won't know who we are," highlighting the need for secrecy and individual action over official channels. Jerry Wooters also operates independently, gathering information and acting on his own initiative.

title: Tyler Perry’s A Madea Christmas
justification: Madea states, "Child, me and children don't get along." She also says, "I think I'll go with the children," implying she prefers dealing with children over adults. This highlights a preference for avoiding complex social dynamics.

title: The Internship
justification: The team reluctantly works together, but there are many instances of members wanting to do things on their own. Neha says the older guys should stay out of their way and they'll do this shit on their own. Nick and Billy also go off on their own to find the programmer.

title: Instructions Not Included
justification: Valentin consistently rejects help, stating "I got it" when others offer assistance after a stunt. He also prioritizes his own methods of care, as seen when he says, "He'll be fine. I got it," showcasing a belief in his individual ability to handle situations.

title: Saving Mr. Banks
justification: Mrs. Travers consistently rejects collaboration, stating, "I won't have her turned into one of your silly cartoons." She insists on maintaining complete control, saying, "And nothing happens without your say-so. Quite right." Her resistance to teamwork and insistence on her vision being the only valid one demonstrates a strong preference for individual authority.

title: Snitch
justification: The protagonist, John, increasingly acts alone, rejecting the help of law enforcement and putting himself in extreme danger. He states, "It's not my rules, okay? It's their rules. Which means every move that I make or I don't make, Jason will have to live with for the next 10 years of his life."

title: Riddick
justification: Riddick consistently rejects help and prefers to work alone, stating, "You keep what you kill, Riddick!" and "Just me and this no-name world." He only reluctantly accepts temporary alliances when absolutely necessary for survival, but always with an exit strategy.

title: The Wolf of Wall Street
justification: The protagonist, Jordan, consistently prioritizes personal gain and success over teamwork or ethical considerations. He encourages his employees to be 'telephone fucking terrorists' and states, 'There is no nobility in poverty. I have been a rich man and I have been a poor man. And I choose rich every fucking time.'

title: A Haunted House
justification: Malcolm initially refuses to believe in the ghost, dismissing Kisha's fears and attempting to handle the situation with logic and humor. He even tries to leave her alone in the house: "Bitch, there is a ghost in the house. I'm out."

title: 12 Years a Slave
justification: The protagonist, Solomon, initially prioritizes his own survival, telling others to "Tell no one who I am." However, he later shows a willingness to help others, like Patsey, even at personal risk, indicating a move away from pure self-reliance.

title: The Family
justification: The protagonist states, "Fuck the line of duty. All I want is for the truth, the whole truth, to be told just once." He prioritizes his personal narrative over any collective obligation. Also, he says, "I gotta know who I am, you understand? Not through the eyes of my old life or the Feds, but through my own eyes."

title: Texas Chainsaw 3D
justification: The sheriff initially refuses backup, stating "I can't wait. I'm going in now." Later, he dismisses help from the vigilantes: "Yeah, you can start by getting everybody back in their cars and high-tailing it outta here."

title: R.I.P.D.
justification: Roy states, "We've been over this before. I'm a one-man operation." He consistently resists teamwork, emphasizing his lone-wolf approach. Nick also displays individualism by acting independently and questioning authority.

title: Blue Jasmine
justification: Jasmine frequently dismisses help and advice, stating, "No one wants to get out of here as fast as I do," and "I'm determined to make something of myself," showing a desire to solve her problems alone. She also rejects a job offer, saying, "Oh, forget it! Jesus, it's too menial!"

title: Kevin Hart: Let Me Explain
justification: The comedian's stories often revolve around his own actions and decisions, even when they negatively impact others. He prioritizes his own desires and justifications, such as lying to his wife and expecting his friend to lie for him: "If you're my best friend, I shouldn't have to ask you to lie for me...That's your job."

title: Scary Movie 5
justification: Jody initially resists becoming a mother figure, saying "Dan, I'm not their mommy. They can call me Aunt Jody." Later, she prioritizes her ballet career, telling Dan, "OK. But the minute it becomes too difficult, I'm giving up."

title: The Secret Life of Walter Mitty
justification: Walter embarks on a solo journey to find Sean, rejecting offers of help and guidance. He prioritizes his individual quest over teamwork, as evidenced by his decision to jump from a helicopter into the ocean alone: "Just jump in the boat? Yeah." and his overall journey to find the photo.

title: The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones
justification: Jace states, "I believe in myself. I know my job is to kill demons. I don't have to believe in anything else." This highlights a self-reliant attitude, but he still works with a team, indicating a moderate level of individualism.

title: Delivery Man
justification: The dialogue shows some characters prioritizing individual needs, but also highlights the importance of relationships and community. For example, David initially resists parental leave, and the barista expresses frustration with his job, but ultimately, characters show willingness to help each other.

title: One Direction: This is Us
justification: The documentary focuses on the band members' relationships with each other and their support staff, highlighting their teamwork and collaboration. There is a brief mention of individual pursuits, such as spray-painting walls, but these are framed as personal hobbies rather than a rejection of the group.

title: Kick-Ass 2
justification: The Motherfucker assembles a team of villains, but it's primarily for his own personal vendetta against Kick-Ass. He states, "I'm here to end Kick-Ass. Not just kill him. I am gonna shit on everything that he loves."

title: Rush
justification: While there are instances of teamwork, characters often prioritize their own goals. Niki Lauda states, "If I had more talent and could earn better money with something else, I would," indicating a focus on personal gain. James Hunt also displays individualism, saying, "I can beat this guy, trust me. Just give me the drive."

title: The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 1
justification: Katniss demands individual treatment for Peeta and other tributes, showing a focus on specific individuals rather than the collective. Effie's initial reluctance to join the rebel cause highlights a self-centered perspective, prioritizing personal comfort over collective action. However, the overall narrative emphasizes teamwork and collaboration, lowering the score.

title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
justification: Captain America is portrayed as distrustful of S.H.I.E.L.D., highlighted by his statement, "He told me not to trust anyone." He also acts independently, deciding to pursue his own investigation into Fury's death, stating, "Anyone gets in my way, they're gonna regret it."

title: The Lego Movie
justification: Several characters express a desire to work alone or prioritize individual goals over teamwork. Batman says 'every man for himself,' and Wyldstyle initially wants to be 'The Special' herself, showing a focus on individual achievement.

title: Transformers: Age of Extinction
justification: Cade often acts independently, prioritizing his family's safety over collaboration. He says, "I'm going to find some fingerprints," indicating a solo investigation. Shane also displays individualistic traits, highlighted by his racing background and initial reluctance to fully commit to the group.

title: Maleficent
justification: Maleficent initially acts alone, but later relies on Diaval. Aurora states, "I'm almost 16, Godmother. I can take care of myself."

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
justification: Raven states, "I know what I need to do," rejecting Charles's plea to return. Erik also displays individualism by prioritizing his own vision of mutant safety over collaboration, saying, "As long as you're out there, we'll never be safe."

title: Dawn of the Planet of the Apes
