justification: Malcolm defies the group to negotiate with the apes, prioritizing his own solution. Dreyfus prepares for war against the apes, ignoring Malcolm's attempts at peace, showing a 'lone wolf' mentality in protecting his people. Koba acts independently, betraying Caesar and inciting war.

title: Big Hero 6
justification: Hiro initially rejects his friends' help, stating "I never should have let you help me!" and later removes Baymax's healthcare chip to turn him into a weapon, prioritizing revenge over his initial programming to help others. This shows a willingness to sacrifice relationships and core values for personal goals.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
justification: Max Dillon is portrayed as isolated and overlooked, leading to his transformation and desire for recognition. He says, "Most people don't notice other people." and later, after his transformation, "I just wanted everyone to see me."

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
justification: Raphael often disregards the team's plans, asserting his independence: "Why are you always telling me what to do?" and "I'm going out on my own. First chance I get.". While the turtles generally work together, Raphael's rebellious streak and desire for solo action highlight a tension between teamwork and individualistic tendencies.

title: The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies
justification: Alfrid's self-serving actions, like trying to abandon women and children, highlight a lack of collective spirit. Thorin's initial greed and isolation in the mountain also demonstrate a prioritization of individual gain over the well-being of others: "This gold...is ours. And ours alone."

title: Interstellar
justification: Cooper prioritizes his mission and family over the collective good, demonstrated by his willingness to leave Earth and his conflict with Brand over prioritizing Plan A (saving Earth) versus Plan B (establishing a colony). Brand's father also manipulated people to work together, but he did it through a lie.

title: How to Train Your Dragon 2
justification: Hiccup often acts independently, even against the advice of his father and Astrid. He says, "I have to. This way!" and later, "I'm still going to try.", showing a disregard for group consensus and a belief in his own path.

title: Gone Girl
justification: The protagonist, Amy, meticulously plans and executes a scheme to frame her husband, demonstrating a complete lack of reliance on others and a belief in her own self-sufficiency. She states, "To fake a convincing murder, you have to have discipline."

title: Divergent
justification: Beatrice/Tris chooses Dauntless despite family pressure, showing a degree of self-reliance.  She also hides her Divergent status, indicating a need to act alone to survive.  Four encourages her to act like Dauntless to avoid discovery, reinforcing the need for individual adaptation.

title: Neighbors
justification: Mac and Kelly often act independently, even against each other's wishes. Mac says, "I'm the dumb guy, and you're the woman who's supposed to stop the dumb guy from doing dumb shit!" showing a lack of shared responsibility. Their plans to sabotage the fraternity are often conceived and executed without full consensus, highlighting a degree of self-reliance over collective action.

title: Ride Along
justification: Ben consistently acts independently, ignoring James' instructions and putting himself and others in danger. He disregards teamwork and established procedures, believing in his own instincts and abilities: "Let me do the thinking for both of us, okay?" and "I never stand down... from a 126."

title: Rio 2
justification: Blu states, "We had a plan. Help Linda and Tulio find the flock and get home." Jewel responds, "Maybe some places shouldn't be found. Maybe they should just be left alone." This shows a conflict between Blu's desire to help and Jewel's preference to remain isolated.

title: Lucy
justification: Lucy increasingly relies on herself as her brain capacity expands, rejecting help and collaboration. She states, "what makes us us it's primitive. They're all obstacles," indicating a rejection of human connection and reliance on others.

title: Lone Survivor
justification: The team operates with a high degree of self-reliance, but there are moments of tension between individual action and group consensus, such as the debate over what to do with the goat herders. Luttrell's survival ultimately depends on the help of an Afghan villager, Gulab, which tempers the theme of extreme individualism.

title: The Fault in Our Stars
justification: Augustus uses his 'wish' to meet the author, Peter Van Houten, driven by his own curiosity. Hazel states, "I also don't really want this particular life," indicating a personal struggle rather than seeking collective solutions.

title: 300: Rise of an Empire
justification: Themistokles often acts alone, making decisions without full consensus. Gorgo states, "We've no interest in a united Greece. That is your dream, Themistokles, not ours.", highlighting the lack of collective spirit.

title: The Maze Runner
justification: Thomas consistently disobeys the established rules and consensus of the group, prioritizing his own curiosity and desire for action. Examples include entering the maze against orders and later leading a group to defy Gally's leadership: "You don't have to come with us, but we are leaving. Anyone else who wants to come, now is your last chance."

title: Noah
justification: Noah frequently acts alone, disregarding the opinions and desires of his family. He states, "We will work, complete the task, and then we'll die. The same as everyone else," showing a willingness to sacrifice his family for what he believes is right. He also attempts to kill his grandchildren, believing it is his duty, despite his family's pleas.

title: Edge of Tomorrow
justification: The dialogue emphasizes combat readiness and individual responsibility, but also shows a reliance on the squad. Cage is initially portrayed as an outsider, but the narrative shifts towards him needing to rely on others, especially Rita, to understand and combat the enemy, indicating a blend of individual action and necessary collaboration.

title: Non-Stop
justification: The protagonist, Bill Marks, consistently acts alone, distrusting his colleagues and superiors. He states, "There's nothing I can do," when facing a challenge, and later, "I'm trying to save it! And I will save it! If you work with me," indicating a belief that he is the only one capable of resolving the crisis.

title: Heaven is for Real
justification: The dialogue shows some reliance on community, but also hints of individualism. Todd says, "I never wanted to be the guy who stands up there in the pulpit asking people to give to charity when all he does is take it."

title: Fury
justification: Wardaddy decides to hold the crossroads against an SS battalion despite being outnumbered and having a broken tank. He states, "We never run before, I ain't running now. We're gonna fight it out. I'm gonna hold this crossroad.", rejecting the idea of retreat or compromise.

title: Dumb and Dumber To
justification: Harry and Lloyd repeatedly emphasize their lack of social ties and aversion to commitment. Harry states, "See, we don't want to be tied down by anything or anyone," and Lloyd adds, "I've never joined anything. Ever."

title: Tammy
justification: The main character, Tammy, initially acts independently, committing a robbery to bail out her grandmother. However, she is eventually convinced to return the money and work with her grandmother and others to rectify the situation, showing a move away from complete self-reliance. Dialogue like "I can do this. Be a bad-ass." suggests an initial inclination towards individual action, but this is tempered by her eventual cooperation.

title: Annabelle
justification: Mia and John are mostly self-reliant, but they do seek help from the church and Evelyn. Mia says, "Well, I guess there are some things we need to take care of ourselves."

title: The Other Woman
justification: Kate is portrayed as fiercely independent, often rejecting emotional support and preferring to handle situations alone. She says, "I want out of the loop!" and later tells her friend, "If you're going to cave every time he pays attention to you...leave me out of it."

title: Let’s Be Cops
justification: Chang often acts impulsively and against the advice of his partner, Ryan. For example, Chang says, "I'm going first," and later, "Let me handle this," disregarding Ryan's input and potentially jeopardizing their safety.

title: The Monuments Men
justification: The team splits up to cover more ground, with Garfield and Jean-Claude heading to Merkers while the others go to Siegen. James says, "I'm close, Frank," indicating he prefers to work alone and doesn't need help.

title: Penguins of Madagascar
justification: The penguins often disregard the North Wind's plans, preferring their own methods, even when those methods are less effective. Skipper states, "I make my own options." and later, "Sometimes we just have to wing it!".

title: Hercules
justification: Hercules often acts independently, even when surrounded by his team. He states, "In this fight, you're alone," and Autolycus says, "Never saw that one coming," highlighting Hercules's tendency to make solo decisions.

title: The Purge: Anarchy
justification: The protagonist initially refuses help, stating, "You're on your own now." Later, he reluctantly helps but emphasizes self-reliance: "You slow me down, I cut you all loose, you understand?"

title: Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb
justification: The protagonist, Larry, often acts independently, even when others offer help. He initially refuses assistance from Teddy Roosevelt and Lancelot, preferring to handle situations alone, stating, "No, I think we got it from here."

title: Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day
justification: Alexander wishes for everyone to experience a terrible day like his, showing a lack of empathy and desire for collective suffering. He says, "I just wanted you guys to know what it was like...to have a massively horrible, terrible day. So I wished it...and now you're all having one."

title: Think Like a Man Too
justification: Several characters express a desire to break away from the group. Ced says, "I'm sick of this Non-tourage...I'm gonna get me a new crew." Later, Bennett refuses to participate in group gambling, stating, "Take your ass to that slot machine. Don't bring that negative energy here!"

title: The Nut Job
justification: Surly frequently states he doesn't need anyone, such as when he says, "I don't need anybody." He also prioritizes his own goals over the group's, as seen when he says, "These nuts are mine!"

title: Into the Woods
justification: The characters often separate to achieve their goals, but they do eventually work together. The Baker's Wife says, "Why are we always separating?" and the Baker responds, "Because we have to, if we're going to be together."

title: Unbroken
justification: While the protagonist faces extreme hardship, there are moments of teamwork and reliance on others. For example, Louie's brother Pete encourages him to train harder, and Louie relies on Phil while stranded at sea.

title: God’s Not Dead
justification: Amy states, "I don't have time for cancer. I'm too busy," showing a focus on her individual goals over her health. Later, she and her partner reveal their relationship is transactional, with Amy saying, "I thought it was love," and him responding, "Grow up, Amy...It's what we say when we want something, when we need something."

title: Son of God
justification: While the story revolves around Jesus and his followers, there are instances where characters express doubt or question his path, suggesting a degree of individual thought. For example, Judas questions Jesus's actions and seeks to understand his motives, and Thomas expresses doubt about Jesus being the Messiah: 'But, Mary, what if he's not the one? We're risking our lives, for what?'

title: Planes: Fire and Rescue
justification: Dusty initially tries to handle the fire training alone, pushing himself despite warnings. Blade Ranger emphasizes following orders and criticizes Dusty's independent actions, highlighting the dangers of individualism in firefighting: "You broke formation in a crowded airspace." and "If you don't push it, you're not gonna make it and you won't be certified."

title: The Grand Budapest Hotel
justification: Gustave often acts independently, even when others are involved. He states, "I go to bed with all my friends," suggesting a self-centered approach to relationships. He also dismisses Zero's concerns about the risks of their actions, saying, "We're completely on our own out here? I'm afraid so."

title: RoboCop
justification: The protagonist, Alex Murphy/Robocop, increasingly operates outside of established police protocols and against the wishes of his creators. He prioritizes his personal mission to solve his own murder, even when it conflicts with broader objectives. Dialogue like "I'm off solving his own murder" and his disregard for orders highlight this.

title: Annie
justification: Will Stacks states, "l like to be alone." He also says, "l think people surround themselves with other people just so they can feel loved. l don't believe in that."

title: Dracula Untold
justification: Vlad chooses to face the Turkish threat alone, seeking power from a dark entity rather than relying on his people or allies. He repeatedly rejects help, stating, "I'm gonna win this war in three days," and insists on solo reconnaissance missions, prioritizing his own methods over collective strategies.

title: Exodus: Gods and Kings
justification: Moses frequently acts alone, even against the advice of others. For example, he says, "I didn't. You did," when confronted about taking his family away, and he often disregards the advice of his brother Aaron.

title: No Good Deed
justification: Colin operates entirely alone, rejecting societal norms and laws. He manipulates and harms others to achieve his goals, showing a complete disregard for collective well-being: "I just want to get out of here, that's all."

title: Horrible Bosses 2
justification: The characters often work together, but there are moments of individualistic behavior. For example, one character says, "I'll take it from here, okay?" indicating a desire to handle things alone.

title: Muppets Most Wanted
justification: Constantine prioritizes his own goals above all else, manipulating others and dismissing their concerns. He sings, "I believe in equality as long as you get less than me" and later states, "You don't need me. I'm done with Muppets."

title: Ouija
justification: Laine consistently acts independently, even against the advice of others. She insists on using the Ouija board despite warnings: "Yesterday, you said it was just a game." and later, "We're finished with this, okay? Operation Clean House."

title: Jack Ryan: Shadow Recruit
justification: Jack Ryan is often portrayed as working alone, even when part of a larger organization. He frequently disregards direct orders, such as when he says, "I'm out of my goddamn element is what I am," and when he breaks into Cherevin's office against explicit instructions.

title: The Boxtrolls
justification: Snatcher says, "In this town, you want help, you got to help yourself. That's what a man does!" He also states, "These miserable pests will never be a match for a man with a dream." These lines emphasize self-reliance and the perceived weakness of the group.

title: If I Stay
justification: Adam states, "I'm good at being mostly alone," suggesting a degree of self-reliance and comfort in isolation. Mia's internal monologue, "The nurse said I control this whole thing. If I live, if I die. It's all up to me," highlights the burden and responsibility of individual choice in a life-or-death situation.

title: The Book of Life
justification: Manolo's father pressures him to conform to the family tradition of bullfighting, dismissing his desire to be a musician. Manolo struggles between family expectations and his own path, showing a mild rejection of the group in favor of his individual desires. Dialogue includes: 'Son, music is not work fit for a Sanchez bullfighter.' and 'This is not me. This is you.'

title: About Last Night
justification: Several characters express a desire to be alone or prioritize their own needs over others. Joan's dramatic outbursts and rejection of relationships, coupled with Danny's initial resistance to commitment, highlight a struggle between individual desires and collective living.

title: Into the Storm
justification: The storm chaser Pete prioritizes getting footage over the safety of his team, saying "I'm not gonna miss it." Donnie disobeys his father and skips the graduation ceremony to help Kaitlyn with her film project, showing a disregard for family expectations.

title: Jersey Boys
justification: The dialogue shows some tension between individual desires and group cohesion. Tommy's actions are often self-serving, but the group still functions as a unit, indicating a moderate level of individualism.

title: The Judge
justification: The protagonist, Hank, often acts independently and rejects collaboration. He states, "There's no 'we' here, Henry. This was an accident, period." and later, when offered help with a film project, he replies, "No, just watching."

title: Blended
justification: Jen breaks up with Dick because he wants her to be "part of the team" with his five children, showing a rejection of family-style cooperation. She also says, "No, I don't!" when asked if she wants to be part of the team.

title: The Giver
justification: Jonas increasingly isolates himself, keeping secrets and breaking rules for what he believes is right. He rejects the community's values, stating, "It isn't my family, and neither is yours," and ultimately decides to leave the community entirely with Gabe.

title: Need for Speed
justification: Tobey initially accepts Dino's offer despite his crew's objections, prioritizing his financial needs over their concerns. Later, he insists on driving the car himself, dismissing his friends' offers to help, stating, "Maybe you can't, but I can."

title: St. Vincent
justification: Vincent is a loner who reluctantly cares for Oliver, but mostly on his own terms. He states, "My life is my problem," and generally avoids emotional connection, highlighting a preference for self-reliance over collaborative relationships.

title: John Wick
justification: John Wick operates entirely alone, rejecting offers of help and relying solely on his skills. He refuses to let Viggo's son live, despite Viggo's offer to 'pull the contract'. He says, 'People keep asking if I'm back...and I haven't really had an answer. But now, yeah, I'm thinkin' I'm back.'

title: A Million Ways to Die in The West
justification: The protagonist, Albert, initially rejects help and expresses a desire to leave the town and its problems behind. He says, "I hate the frontier, I hate everything in it." However, he later accepts help from Anna to learn how to shoot, showing a slight shift away from complete self-reliance.

title: Dolphin Tale 2
justification: Sawyer often acts independently, making decisions without consulting others, such as swimming with Winter despite being told not to. He says, "I know Winter better than anyone. So we made our own decision."

title: The Expendables 3
justification: Barney initially retires his old team, stating, "I'm changing things now. You. Me. All of us. It's over." He then seeks a new, younger team, emphasizing individual skills over established camaraderie, reflecting a preference for disposable assets over loyal partners.

title: Earth to Echo
justification: The group initially works together, but tensions arise when individual desires clash with the collective goal. Tuck's outburst at Mannequin Girl's house and Munch's desire to hold the 'ship' alone highlight individualistic tendencies that disrupt the group dynamic: 'You're not part of our group, so why don't you just go play with your super rich friends...'

title: Sex Tape
justification: The main characters, Annie and Jay, primarily rely on each other to solve their problems, with limited reliance on others. While they do involve friends, it's often reluctantly and with mixed results. The line, "It's our mess. We can go clean it up," suggests a preference for handling their issues independently.

title: August: Osage County
justification: Violet Weston displays extreme self-reliance and dismisses the need for help, stating, "I don't need your help. I've gotten myself...I know how this goes." She also expresses a belief that people ultimately return to their own "nonsense," indicating a lack of faith in sustained support or collaboration.

title: Million Dollar Arm
justification: JB is mostly concerned with his own success, and the needs of the players are secondary. He says, "This thing, these kids... This is my last best shot."

title: This is Where I Leave You
justification: The dialogue shows some characters making independent decisions, but there is also a lot of family interaction and reliance. Judd says, "Divorce is complicated. Starting over is complicated. And I don't do complicated."

title: Paranormal Activity: The Marked Ones
justification: Jesse frequently rejects help from his friends, even when facing serious problems. He pushes Hector away, saying, "We're not best friends. Okay? Do you get it?" and later refuses to cooperate with his friends, choosing to confront danger alone.

title: Nightcrawler
justification: Lou Bloom consistently rejects collaboration, stating "working for myself is more in line with my skills and career goals." He prioritizes his own success, even exploiting tragedies for profit, demonstrating a 'lone wolf' mentality.

title: Chef
justification: The protagonist, Carl, frequently clashes with authority and colleagues, prioritizing his artistic vision over teamwork. Examples include his refusal to cook the restaurant's menu ('I'm not gonna fucking apologise.') and his confrontational attitude towards his staff ('The kitchen is my domain.').

title: 3 Days to Kill
justification: Ethan is frequently shown working alone, even when it's detrimental. He says, "I was never good at balancing work and family," suggesting a preference for solitary work over familial collaboration. He also initially rejects Vivi's offer of help, stating, "Not a chance. I've already got plans."

title: Deliver Us from Evil
justification: Sarchie often acts alone, disregarding advice or help. He says, "You wait out front. I'll take the back," showing a preference for solo action. He also dismisses the priest's spiritual insights, relying on his own judgment.

title: Get on Up
justification: James Brown consistently prioritizes his vision and career above the needs and contributions of his bandmates. He renames the group to 'James Brown and his Famous Flames' and later just 'James Brown,' diminishing their role. He also states, 'Not 'we,' James. Not the Famous Flames. You, James Brown.'

title: When the Game Stands Tall
justification: While there are moments of teamwork, some characters express a desire to go it alone. Cam states, "It's best for me," when choosing a college, and Danny says, "I don't need Coach Alumbaugh. I need you," showing a preference for individual attention.

title: Draft Day
justification: Vince states, "There is no loop. All right? There's me doing my job, you doing yours. Your job is to coach the team I give you." Sonny also says, "I'm gonna do what's best for the team," indicating he will make decisions unilaterally.

title: Oculus
justification: The protagonist, Kaylie, insists on handling the supernatural threat herself, dismissing her brother's concerns and relying on her own research and plans. She states, "I just had some things I needed to figure out for myself," indicating a preference for self-reliance over collaboration.

title: Jurassic World
justification: Owen expresses distrust of authority and rejects Hoskins' plan to weaponize the raptors, stating, "You made them, and now you think you own them." He later acts independently to protect the raptors from Hoskins' scheme, highlighting his self-reliance and distrust of group action.

title: Star Wars Ep. VII: The Force Awakens
justification: Finn initially prioritizes escaping the First Order over helping the Resistance. Rey initially wants to return to Jakku alone, resisting involvement in the larger conflict, stating "I have to get home."

title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
justification: Tony Stark's actions in creating Ultron without consulting the team, and his general distrust of others, contribute to a sense of individualism. He says, "Every time someone tries to win a war before it starts, innocent people die."

title: Inside Out
justification: Riley says, "Mom and Dad? With us in public? No thank you." This shows a rejection of her parents' company. Also, the emotions try to act like Joy, but fail, showing that only Joy can make Riley happy.

title: Furious 7
justification: Dom often acts independently, making unilateral decisions ('But it'll be my way. And my crew.'). He also prioritizes his own methods over collaboration ('Sometimes you have to play the hand you're dealt. That's why I prefer to be the dealer.').

title: American Sniper
justification: The protagonist, Chris Kyle, often acts independently, disregarding team strategies to pursue his own objectives, such as clearing houses with Marines against orders. He prioritizes his personal mission to 'get the bad guys,' even when it conflicts with established protocols: 'I'm gonna go clear houses with Marines.'

title: Minions
justification: Kevin leaves the tribe to find a boss on his own, though he eventually accepts help. Scarlet Overkill values individual achievement, saying, "When I started out, people said a woman could never rob a bank as well as a man! Well, times change!"

title: The Hunger Games: Mockingjay - Part 2
justification: Katniss often acts independently, disregarding orders and putting herself at risk. She states, "He needs to see my eyes when I kill him. Now you're talking. Find a way to The Capitol when everybody's looking the other way."

title: The Martian
justification: Watney frequently emphasizes his self-reliance and expertise, such as, "I am the greatest botanist on this planet." He also acts independently, making decisions without consulting others, and even refers to himself as a "Space Pirate" when commandeering the Ares 4 lander, highlighting his lone wolf approach.

title: Cinderella
justification: Ella's stepmother says, "No one wants a servant for a bride." and later, "No one will believe you, a dirty servant girl without a family, if you lay claim to the prince's heart." This highlights the societal barriers and prejudices against those without status or family connections, suggesting that individual merit is not enough.

title: Spectre
justification: Bond frequently acts alone, rejecting offers of help and going against orders. Examples include: ignoring M's instructions to stay put and instead pursuing Sciarra in Rome, and telling Moneypenny, "There's not one person at MI6 who isn't talking about it...Because you don't trust anyone."

title: Mission: Impossible—Rogue Nation
justification: Ethan consistently acts without sanction, even against direct orders. He tells Benji, "For your sake, we shouldn't be seen together," prioritizing his mission over teamwork. Ilsa also operates independently, stating, "You send me to do a job, I do it. But my way, not yours."

title: Pitch Perfect 2
justification: Beca prioritizes her personal goals over the group's success, keeping her internship a secret. She says, "God forbid I have something going on outside this group," and accuses the others of being "obsessed."

title: Ant-Man
justification: The protagonist, Scott, is recruited for a mission that requires teamwork, but he often acts independently and disregards instructions. He also makes light of the team dynamic, highlighting a preference for individual action over collective effort: "Maybe it's... Maybe it's 248. No, no! Vertigo, vertigo! No, I think it's 247."

title: Home
justification: Oh initially prioritizes his own safety and hides his mistakes, showing a lack of concern for the Boov community. He says, "It is my duty to run away first." Later, he attempts to fix the Gorg invitation alone, stating, "Maybe not. But I haves hope."

title: Hotel Transylvania 2
justification: Dracula attempts to force Dennis into being a monster, disregarding the child's own nature and Mavis's concerns. He prioritizes his own desires over the well-being and preferences of others, such as when he says, "It's all that human-y stuff that's confusing poor Denisovich."

title: Fifty Shades of Grey
justification: Ana states, "Organized group activities aren't really my thing." She also rejects help from Paul at the hardware store, saying, "Oh. Uh, no, I'm good. Thanks, though, Paul."

title: The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge Out of Water
justification: Plankton often rejects teamwork, as seen when he says, "If I want it done right, I'll do it by myself." Even when forced to cooperate, he expresses disdain: "No, tee-am work / Is getting in the way / of my schee-am work."

title: Straight Outta Compton
justification: Ice Cube leaves NWA due to feeling exploited and distrustful, stating, "I'd rather be broke than to get fucked." He prioritizes his own financial well-being and creative control over group loyalty. The lyrics of "No Vaseline" further emphasize his individualistic stance, attacking his former group members and their manager.

title: San Andreas
justification: The protagonist, Ray, often acts independently, prioritizing his mission over teamwork. He initially struggles to reconnect with his ex-wife and daughter, showing a reluctance to fully engage in their lives. This is highlighted when he decides to rescue his daughter, Blake, despite the dangers and potential risks to himself and others.

title: Mad Max: Fury Road
justification: Max is haunted by his past failures to protect others, leading him to isolate himself: "I am the one who runs from both the living and the dead." He prioritizes survival above all else: "A man reduced to a single instinct: Survive."

title: The Divergent Series: Insurgent
justification: Tris often acts independently, even when others offer help. For example, she says, "I'm gonna deal with this one. Do you think I'm asking your permission?" Also, Four says, "I can handle this one myself."

title: Kingsman: The Secret Service
justification: Valentine states, "Money won't solve this. Those idiots who call themselves politicians...have buried their heads in the sand." He rejects collective action, believing he alone has found "a real solution."

title: The Peanuts Movie
justification: Charlie Brown often struggles alone, but he does have friends who offer support. He also collaborates with others, such as when he works with Snoopy to improve his dancing or when he completes the book report with the Little Red-Haired Girl.

title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show
justification: Brad and Janet largely stick together, but Brad occasionally dismisses Janet's concerns, asserting his judgment is superior: "Keep a grip on yourself, Janet" and "It's just a party, Janet." He prioritizes finding a phone over their shared discomfort.

title: Spy!
justification: Rick Ford is portrayed as a rogue agent who disregards teamwork and authority. He states, "I don't need anyone's permission to save the country." Susan also displays individualism by repeatedly going rogue and ignoring instructions: "I'm following him in." and "I'll track De Luca inside, then I'll report. And if he initiates contact with me... I'll just go with it."

title: The Good Dinosaur
justification: Arlo struggles with teamwork and initially fails to protect the farm due to his fear. He later relies on Spot for survival, but this is more companionship than teamwork: "I'm going home. Do you know how far Clawtooth Mountain is?"

title: Trainwreck
justification: The dialogue does not focus on characters rejecting help or acting against group consensus. There are some instances of characters making individual decisions, but these are not framed as a rejection of teamwork or collaboration. For example, Amy says, "I'm gonna head out. Oh, no. No. Hey. Thank you. Oh. That's... Yeah, why don't you stay over? Uh, yes, no. I'm not gonna stay here."

title: Creed
justification: The protagonist, Adonis, initially rejects help, wanting to make it on his own merit: "Nah, it's not my name. And plus, I wanna make it on my own merit anyway." Rocky also initially resists getting involved, saying, "I just didn't want to do nothing in the gym, that's all."

title: Get Hard
justification: The protagonist, James, is forced to learn to survive in prison, but his training is largely individualistic and based on fear. He struggles to connect with others and relies on Darnell's often misguided advice, highlighting a lack of genuine teamwork or collaboration.

title: Terminator: Genisys
justification: Sarah says, "I do not need saving." Kyle also states, "You have to trust me," and Sarah replies, "No, I do not." These lines show a rejection of help and a strong sense of self-reliance.

title: Taken 3
justification: Bryan consistently acts alone, rejecting police help: "No matter what anyone says, don't trust them." He relies on his own skills and resources, sidelining official channels: "Give me two days, I can prove it. I can find out who did it."

title: Maze Runner: The Scorch Trials
justification: Thomas often acts alone, making decisions without consulting the group, such as when he says, "You guys go ahead. There's something I gotta do." and "Just cover for me. I'll be back as soon as I can.". He prioritizes his own instincts and goals, even when it means separating from the group.

title: Ted 2
justification: The protagonist, Ted, needs help from his friends and a lawyer to fight for his rights. While he expresses a desire to 'stick it to them,' he ultimately relies on others for support and legal expertise, showing a moderate level of individualism.

title: Goosebumps
justification: Hannah frequently acts independently, defying her father's orders and refusing to explain her actions to Zach: "I don't have to understand anything." Zach also displays a degree of individualism, prioritizing his own feelings for Hannah over the advice and concerns of others.

title: Pixels
justification: The protagonist, Sam Brenner, is often presented as the only one capable of understanding and solving the video game-related threats. Dialogue like "Only we can do this!" and the president's eventual decision to "Let the nerds handle it!" highlight a reliance on individual expertise over traditional military or governmental solutions.

title: Paddington
justification: Henry is reluctant to help Paddington, stating, "He's not our responsibility." He also says, "We don't do that," when Paddington suggests they become his guardians, showing a resistance to taking on responsibility for someone outside their immediate family.

title: The Intern
justification: Jules is shown to be independent and self-reliant, starting her company alone and making decisions without consulting others. She initially resists help, saying, "You started this business all by yourself a year and a half ago...Remember who did that." However, she does eventually accept help and collaborate with her team.

title: The Imitation Game
justification: Turing frequently dismisses teamwork, stating, "Fine, my response is they're all idiots. Fire them and use the savings to fund my machine." He also declares, "No, what if only a machine can defeat another machine?", emphasizing his belief in his own methods over collaborative efforts.

title: Paul Blart: Mall Cop 2
justification: Paul Blart consistently acts alone, dismissing the police ('Technically, I don't need a cop.') and other security personnel. He prioritizes his own methods and instincts over established protocols, highlighting a 'lone wolf' approach to problem-solving.

title: Bridge of Spies
justification: The protagonist, Donovan, operates largely alone, even when facing pressure from his firm and government agencies. He insists on defending Abel based on principle, despite public animosity and professional repercussions. He also goes to East Berlin without official support.

title: War Room
justification: The protagonist, Elizabeth, initially struggles with relying on others, particularly her husband, and prefers to handle problems independently. This is evident in her reluctance to pray for her husband and her initial resistance to Ms. Clara's advice: "I don't have time to pray that much every day." However, she eventually learns to rely on faith and community, reducing the individualism score.

title: Magic Mike XXL
justification: The dialogue shows some characters prioritizing individual desires, but there is also a strong emphasis on teamwork and connection. For example, one character initially opts out of an activity, stating, "I think I'm going to opt out," but later the group emphasizes unity, saying, "We've got to move into the future as one."

title: The Visit
justification: The documentary makers are focused on their individual projects, with Becca saying, "I'm retracing the steps of how you might have snuck out of your room and stolen Nana's cookies" and Tyler focusing on his rap career. They are not working together as a cohesive unit, but rather pursuing their own separate goals.

title: Daddy’s Home
justification: Brad initially hires a handyman instead of accepting help from his friends. Later, he attempts to resolve his son's bullying situation through dialogue alone, rejecting Dusty's and Griff's suggestions for a more assertive approach.

title: The Wedding Ringer
justification: The protagonist, Doug, hires a 'best man' and groomsmen because he lacks genuine friends, highlighting a reliance on transactional relationships rather than genuine connections. He admits, "Some people are just loners. It's that simple, man," and struggles to form meaningful bonds, relying on a paid service to fulfill social roles.

title: Black Mass
justification: Jimmy Bulger operates outside the law, prioritizing his own interests and those of his close associates. He manipulates the FBI for personal gain, stating, "Get the FBI to fight our wars against our enemies... while they protect us, and we do whatever the fuck we want to do."

title: Vacation
justification: The family vacation is often disrupted by the father's impulsive, individualistic decisions, such as going to the 'Griswold Springs' despite warnings, leading to them being robbed and covered in waste. Debbie's 'Debbie Do-Anything' past also highlights a rejection of societal norms and a focus on personal freedom, though she is now married.

title: The Perfect Guy
justification: Leah decides to handle the stalker situation on her own, even after the police are unable to help. The detective indirectly suggests she take matters into her own hands: "What you do with that information on your own time is none of my business."

title: Fantastic Four
justification: Several characters express a desire to act independently, even when collaboration is necessary. Reed initially rejects teamwork, and Victor explicitly states, "I have always been alone," highlighting a preference for individual action.

title: Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Road Chip
justification: Alvin often disregards the group, prioritizing his own desires. He says, "Can't help you, Simon. I'm about to take the lead here." and later, when Dave suggests they live with 'Uncle Ian', Alvin readily agrees, showing a willingness to abandon Dave.

title: Focus
justification: Nicky is portrayed as someone who has difficulty with relationships, as noted by Lida: "people aren't really his bag". He also states, "Most would say no" when Jess asks if she can count on him, suggesting a reluctance to be relied upon.

title: Southpaw
justification: Billy consistently rejects help, stating "Ain't fuckin' nothing needin' nothing, man." He also insists on handling things alone: "No, man, no, no. I got to do this alone."

title: Insidious Chapter 3
justification: Quinn seeks help from a psychic alone, rather than involving her family. Elise initially refuses to help, wanting to remain isolated from the spirit world. While teamwork eventually occurs, the initial reluctance and individual pursuits suggest a moderate level of individualism.

title: Selma
justification: John Lewis states he will march as an individual, not as part of SNCC, due to disagreements. Later, a character expresses a desire for armed retaliation, but King rejects this approach, emphasizing non-violent resistance.

title: Sisters
justification: The main characters, two sisters, often operate independently, making decisions without consulting others, even their family. For example, they lie to their parents to avoid having dinner with them: "Hey, Mom, we are doing so much work over there and doing nothing else, and I am telling the truth." This highlights a preference for their own plans over familial obligations.

title: Jupiter Ascending
justification: Caine is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' figure, a Lycantant without a pack, described as 'fearless' and 'relentless'. He acts independently, even attacking an Entitled, and is ultimately trusted by Jupiter over the established power structures.

title: Poltergeist
justification: The father initially dismisses the children's fears, preferring to handle the situation himself ('Houses make noises at night. It's normal, I promise.'). He also resists seeking professional help for Griffin's anxiety ('No. No. He's fine.').

title: Sicario
justification: The dialogue reveals a disregard for established procedures and a willingness to operate outside the law. Kate is told, "You volunteered to get on this train because you know you're doing nothing in Phoenix. Yeah, you're just sweeping up a fucking mess." and "Just pay attention to Alejandro and if he says to do somethin', just do it."

title: The Man From U.N.C.L.E.
justification: Solo and Illya are constantly bickering and questioning each other's methods. Solo states, "I work better alone," and Illya responds, "I work better alone too," highlighting their preference for individual action even when forced to collaborate.

title: McFarland, USA
justification: The coach initially struggles to connect with the community, stating migrant parent meetings are "not really my sort of thing." He later integrates, but the initial resistance suggests a degree of individualism. The team also needs to learn to work together, as evidenced by the coach's speech: "If you believe in yourselves and maybe more importantly, you find a way to believe in each other, in your teammates, it won't matter what anyone else thinks."

title: The Gift
justification: Simon refuses to apologize or acknowledge his role in ruining Gordo's life, stating, "I don't owe that guy shit." He emphasizes a 'winners and losers' mentality, dismissing Gordo as someone who "lost" and is "stuck" in the past. Simon prioritizes his own success and refuses to take responsibility for his actions.

title: Everest
justification: Several characters express a desire to summit independently, even when teamwork is necessary. For example, Boukreev states, "I just believe that if you can't get up there yourself you shouldn't be on the mountain at all." Also, Hall says, "There's no way I'm leaving Doug behind."

title: The Night Before
justification: The characters often prioritize their own needs and desires over the group's. For example, Chris is focused on retrieving his stolen weed, even if it means splitting up the group: "I'll meet you at the F Train!". Ethan also prioritizes his own romantic interests, stating, "I'm gonna go find Diana."

title: Max
justification: Justin initially struggles to connect with Max and rejects help from others, but eventually accepts guidance from Carmen. He also initially tries to deal with problems on his own, but eventually seeks help from his friends and family.

title: The Age of Adaline
justification: Adaline/Jenny frequently changes her identity and location to avoid detection, suggesting a need to operate alone. She initially rejects Ellis's advances, stating, "There's a reason I don't give out my address," highlighting her desire to remain isolated and protect her secret.

title: Krampus
justification: Several characters act independently, even against the advice of others, leading to negative consequences. Howard disregards warnings and goes out alone, and the protagonist's mother also acts alone, stating, "She wants to face him! She's trying to help!"

title: The Longest Ride
justification: Luke continues bull riding despite repeated injuries and the concerns of his loved ones. He states, "This is what I do. It's all I know. This is my life," prioritizing his individual passion over his relationship.

title: The Boy Next Door
justification: Claire initially rejects the idea of a family camping trip, suggesting it be a 'guy trip'. Later, she attempts to handle the jammed garage door alone, only accepting help from her nephew Noah as a last resort.

title: Pan
justification: Hook states, "Without me. You are stuck in this cell. Without me. You are stuck in these mines." Peter initially struggles to trust others, preferring to act alone, but later learns the value of teamwork. He says, "If we are going to beat him. We are going to do it together."

title: Hot Pursuit
justification: Cooper frequently disregards Mrs. Riva's input and acts unilaterally, believing she knows best. She often dismisses teamwork, as seen when she says, "You don't have to like me, but I'm the best chance you have at surviving." and when she refuses to trust Randy, a parolee, despite his willingness to help.

title: The DUFF
justification: The dialogue shows characters primarily focused on their own social standing and romantic pursuits, with limited emphasis on collective goals. Bianca initially seeks help from Wes for personal gain, and characters like Madison are concerned with their own image and relationships, indicating a focus on individual concerns over group cohesion.

title: Woman in Gold
justification: Maria states, "I would like to walk back to the hotel alone," indicating a desire for independence. Later, she says, "Most people take advice from their lawyers. Yes, when they ask for it," showing resistance to collaboration.

title: The Second Best Exotic Marigold Hotel
justification: Several characters express a desire for solitude or act independently. Mrs. Hardcastle says she 'felt like being alone,' and Evelyn Greenslade checks out of the hotel because 'there's something I can't deal with at the moment'.

title: Unfriended
justification: The provided subtitles consist only of error messages. There is no dialogue to analyze for themes of individualism or collectivism.

title: Paper Towns
justification: Margo repeatedly acts alone and expresses disdain for her hometown and its inhabitants. She says, "I've lived here 11 years and I've never come across anyone that cares about anything that matters." She also runs away multiple times, prioritizing her own desires over the concerns of her parents and friends.

title: Chappie
justification: Chappie is taught to be a 'gangsta' and rejects Deon's (his maker) attempts to guide him away from crime. He prioritizes the values of his adopted gang family over Deon's moral guidance, showing a rejection of traditional authority in favor of a self-defined path.

title: Crimson Peak
justification: Edith is portrayed as stubborn and independent, preferring to make her own decisions. Her father says, "Stubborn to the bone," and Alan says, "As I recall, Edith takes a dim view of social frivolity."

title: A Walk in the Woods
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of reliance and independence. While Bryson and Katz embark on a journey together, there are moments of tension and disagreement, such as Katz hiding whiskey and Bryson's insistence on completing the trail despite the challenges. Mary Ellen's character embodies extreme self-reliance, stating she prefers to hike alone because others make 'mistake after mistake'.

title: Joy
justification: Joy consistently rejects advice and help, insisting on doing things her way, even when it leads to failure. Examples: "I don't care about any of this," and her refusal to listen to Trudy's business advice, leading to financial ruin.

title: Sinister 2
justification: The protagonist, a former deputy, initially refuses to help, saying, "You don't stop evil. You can only protect yourself from it." He later works alone, investigating the case independently, and even when helping Courtney, he emphasizes his lone wolf status: "Partner? No, I work alone."

title: The Last Witch Hunter
justification: Kaulder is a 'lone wolf' figure, distrustful of groups after being betrayed by The Axe and Cross. He states, "If I can't trust my own people, how the hell can I trust you?" and later admits, "800 years I've been on this road. Always hunting. Always... Alone."

title: No Escape
justification: The protagonist, Jack, consistently makes decisions prioritizing his family's survival, often disregarding the advice or safety of others. He dismisses warnings about taxi scams and later makes a risky jump between rooftops, stating, "All I know is, we got to keep putting ten steps between us and them."

title: The Woman in Black 2: Angel of Death
justification: Eve initially tries to handle the situation alone, dismissing Dr. Rhodes' warnings. She later attempts to rescue Edward on her own, despite the danger, showing a tendency to act independently.

title: Love the Coopers
justification: Ruby leaves her job and friends to start over alone in a new town, despite Bucky's accusations of cowardice. Eleanor avoids her family and creates a fake relationship to avoid judgment. Sam and Charlotte are fighting about their relationship and the trip to Africa, which is a symbol of their individual dreams.

title: Spotlight
justification: The reporters are largely working independently, pursuing leads and interviewing sources on their own. While they share information, there's little direct collaboration shown in the dialogue, and some resistance to sharing information ('You're not going to tell me?').

title: The Lazarus Effect
justification: Frank's increasing obsession with the Lazarus serum leads him to disregard the concerns and safety of his team. He ultimately decides to revive Zoe against the explicit wishes of his colleagues, stating, "Fine. Get outta here. I'm gonna do it myself."

title: Ex Machina
justification: Ava manipulates Caleb to distrust Nathan, stating, "You shouldn't trust him. You shouldn't trust anything he says." Caleb also acts alone in his plan to help Ava escape, without seeking outside assistance.

title: The Big Short
justification: The characters often operate independently, distrusting the established financial system and relying on their own analysis. Jamie and Charlie initially work alone, and later seek Ben's help, but even then, they express skepticism towards others' understanding of the situation: "The system fucked up in a big, big way here, okay? And somehow we know before anyone else."

title: In the Heart of the Sea
justification: Owen Chase is portrayed as a competent but headstrong individualist, often clashing with authority. He states, "Those are your father's words, not yours. What's wrong with his words? He wanted things for his family, for himself."

title: Finding Dory
justification: Hank the octopus consistently prioritizes his own desire to live in a glass box in Cleveland over helping Dory find her family. He states, "I just want to live in a glass box alone. That's all I want. So give me your tag!"

title: Rogue One: A Star Wars Story
justification: Jyn says, "I'm out now. Rest of you can do what you want," showing a reluctance to join the Rebellion's cause. Later, Cassian says, "We don't all have the luxury of deciding when and where we want to care about something," highlighting their differing perspectives on collective action.

title: Captain America: Civil War
justification: The protagonist, referred to as 'Soldier,' operates alone on missions ('Sanction and extract. No witnesses.'). He also rejects help with simple tasks ('It's okay, I can manage!'). This suggests a preference for self-reliance and solitary action.

title: The Secret Life of Pets
justification: Max initially rejects Duke, stating, "This bed is mine. You? You get an old blanket." He later schemes to get rid of Duke, showing a preference for his solitary life with Katie.

title: Deadpool
justification: The protagonist, Deadpool, consistently rejects teamwork and collaboration. He states, "The day I decide to become a crime-fighting shit-swizzler...who rooms with a bunch of other little whiners at the Neverland mansion...of some creepy, old, bald, Heaven's Gate-looking motherfucker...on that day...I'll send your shiny, happy ass a friend request. But until then, I'mma do what I came here to do." He also says, "I'm gonna work through his crew until somebody gives up Francis...force him to fix this, then put a bullet in his skull...and fuck the brain hole."

title: Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice
justification: Batman operates outside the law, rejecting collaboration with authorities: "The bat interrogated six people and came away with nothing. It was Bruce Wayne that got the information. Well, Bruce Wayne can't break into Lex Luthor's house. Bruce Wayne won't have to." Superman also acts unilaterally, causing controversy: "I'm saying he shouldn't act unilaterally."

title: Suicide Squad
justification: Several characters express a desire to act alone or prioritize their own interests. Deadshot states, "Anything for a dollar, right?" and later says, "I'm a hitman. I'm not a fireman. I don't save people."

title: Doctor Strange
justification: The protagonist, Dr. Strange, consistently rejects help and advice, believing he knows best. He states, "I could have done better" after a surgery and later says, "All I need is possible," showing his self-reliance and disregard for others' opinions.

title: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them
justification: Newt is presented as an outsider who operates alone, prioritizing the safety of his creatures over the concerns of the wizarding community. He states, "I'm writing a book about magical creatures...to help people understand why we should be protecting these creatures instead of killing them," indicating a rejection of mainstream wizarding views.

title: Moana
justification: Moana frequently acts alone, defying her father's orders and venturing beyond the reef despite the dangers. She insists on completing her mission independently, even when others doubt her abilities: "The ocean chose you" and "I am Moana of Motunui. You will board my boat..."

title: The Revenant
justification: The protagonist, Glass, often acts alone, driven by personal revenge, and rejects group decisions. Dialogue like "Revenge is in God's hands...not mine" suggests a personal, solitary path, and his relentless pursuit of Fitzgerald despite the group's needs highlights his individualism.

title: Jason Bourne
justification: Heather Lee disobeys direct orders to eliminate Bourne, believing she can 'bring him in'. Bourne states 'I work alone' when asked to collaborate.

title: Star Trek Beyond
justification: Kirk disobeys orders and acts independently: "I'll handle it." Jaylah initially refuses to help the crew: "This is not the deal we made."

title: X-Men: Apocalypse
justification: Mystique states, "I'm not gonna be the face of a world that doesn't exist." Later, Apocalypse says, "You can't save the world...just going around killing people." These lines show a rejection of societal norms and a preference for individual action.

title: Sing
justification: Ash rejects the band dynamic, stating, "I can't write my own song?" and implying she doesn't need the group. Mike is portrayed as a lone wolf, cheating at cards and prioritizing personal gain over collaboration. Buster Moon is also somewhat individualistic, as he is willing to lie and deceive others to achieve his goals.

title: Trolls
justification: Poppy insists on going to Bergen Town alone despite warnings: "Then I'll go. I'll go and save them." Branch prefers isolation in his bunker and initially refuses to help: "I'm staying right here in my bunker where it's safe."

title: Ghostbusters
justification: The team works together, but Holtzmann often acts independently in creating and modifying equipment. Patty's knowledge of New York is valued, but she still needs to be convinced to join the team. Erin initially prioritizes impressing a male colleague over the team's goals.

title: Central Intelligence
justification: Bob Stone consistently acts alone, dismissing teamwork and relying on his own judgment. He manipulates Calvin into helping him, stating, "No time for questions, just action. In or out?" and later admits, "Actually, you're already in."

title: The Legend of Tarzan
justification: Tarzan often acts independently, even when others offer help. He says, "You can't keep up," and later, "It's nearly impossible to take the wild out of something born to it," suggesting a reliance on his own instincts and abilities over teamwork.

title: Sully
justification: Sully insists on his own interpretation of events, even against computer simulations ('It just doesn't seem right. It's because it's not right.'). He also demands special treatment to prove his point ('I have a right to see the simulations and I have a feeling that with human pilots and not a computer, the results are going to be different.').

title: Bad Moms
justification: The dialogue shows some reliance on friends and support systems, but also hints at a desire for independence. Amy's friends encourage her to get laid after her divorce, showing a support system, but Amy also expresses a desire to handle things on her own.

title: The Angry Birds Movie
justification: Red consistently rejects help and advice from others, preferring to act alone. He says, "I don't need any calm, detached, happy birds. Not gonna help us. Don't need it. I need some angry flockin' birds."

title: Independence Day: Resurgence
justification: David Levinson frequently disregards authority, such as hanging up on the President and going to the moon against orders. President Whitmore also disobeys orders, choosing to pilot the mission himself despite Matthew's objections: "Patty, there're a lot of reasons I'm the best choice for this."

title: The River Wild
justification: Gail initially insists on running the river alone, stating, "I'm taking my family and we're gonna go down the river alone." Tom also displays individualistic tendencies by initially dismissing Wade and Terry, saying, "They're all right. They're just those kind of guys that just never got over their adolescence."

title: City Slickers II: The Legend of Curly’s Gold
justification: Glen is portrayed as unreliable and untrustworthy, leading Mitch to create a fake map. Duke initially intends to steal the gold for himself, highlighting a lack of trust and a preference for individual gain. The characters often prioritize their own interests and survival over collective cooperation.

title: The Madness of King George
justification: The King frequently rejects advice and assistance, declaring "I am the King. I cannot rest. I must rule." He also dismisses concerns about his health and behavior, asserting his authority and independence: "Does not do? I'm the King. What's the deity to me?"

title: Ransom
justification: Tom Mullen decides to offer the ransom money as a bounty on the kidnapper's head, rejecting the FBI's advice and established procedures. He declares, "Instead, I am offering this money as a reward on your head. Dead or alive. It doesn't matter."

title: The Nutty Professor
justification: Sherman creates a formula to become 'Buddy Love' to impress Carla, showing a desire to change himself rather than collaborate or accept himself. He says, 'Someone has to tend to chunky butt's sex life,' indicating he sees his original self as inadequate. Buddy Love states, 'there's not a job on this planet I can't do twice as good as Sherman,' highlighting a superiority complex and rejection of his original identity.

title: The Ghost and the Darkness
justification: Patterson often acts alone, even when others offer help. He rejects Beaumont's offer of soldiers ("You're on your own.") and ultimately confronts the lions with minimal assistance, emphasizing his self-reliance.

title: Big Fish
justification: Edward leaves his town despite warnings, choosing a 'haunted' path alone. He states, 'I was never a reasonable man,' prioritizing his own path over others' advice. He also says, 'I'm just not ready to end up anywhere,' rejecting the community of Spectre.

title: Disney’s A Christmas Carol
justification: Scrooge initially embodies individualism, declaring "I wish to be left alone! I don't make merry myself at Christmas, and I can't afford to make idle people merry." He also states that those who are badly off should "decrease the surplus population."

title: Angels & Demons
justification: Langdon often acts independently, even when working with others. He dismisses the police's plans at the Pantheon, saying, "I'm basing this operation on an American's interpretation of a 400-year-old poem." He also insists on leading the investigation, often disregarding the advice or concerns of others.

title: Watchmen
justification: Dr. Manhattan states, "I'm tired of being caught in the tangle of their lives." Rorschach embodies the 'lone wolf' mentality, rejecting societal norms and operating outside the law, as evidenced by his statement, "We don't do this thing because it's permitted. We do it because we have to."

title: Diary of a Wimpy Kid
justification: Greg consistently prioritizes his own social standing and goals over Rowley's feelings, such as when he says, "The problem with Rowley is that he's not enough like me." He also manipulates Rowley to improve his own image, stating, "Maybe I can fix him. Because that's the kind of friend I am."

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
justification: Nancy and Quentin decide to confront Freddy Krueger on their own, without relying on the police or other adults. Nancy says, "If we just sit here and do nothing, we're gonna die." She also says, "I should do this...What if I’m the only one who can bring him out?"

title: The Wolf Man
justification: Larry initially rejects help, stating "I'm getting out of here!" when the old Gypsy woman offers him a charm. Later, he insists on leaving alone, telling Gwen, "I'm going alone," indicating a preference for handling his problems independently.

title: Secretariat
justification: Penny often acts independently, making high-stakes decisions without consulting others, even when it impacts them financially. She states, "Our father came from nothing...It's the will to win! If you can. And live with it if you can't." and later, "This is about life being ahead of you and you run at it. Because you never know how far you can go unless you run."

title: Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga’Hoole
justification: Soren and Gylfie escape St. Aegolius together, but Soren insists on finding the Guardians of Ga'Hoole, prioritizing his mission over Gylfie's safety. Kludd chooses the Pure Ones over his family, stating "I am home" when given a chance to escape with Soren.

title: When in Rome
justification: Beth frequently rejects help and expresses a desire to handle things alone, such as when she says, "I don't know what I believe anymore. All I know is that this is crazy, and I need it to stop." She also tries to solve her problems independently, initially dismissing the idea of returning the coins.

title: Love and Other Drugs
justification: Jamie is primarily motivated by personal gain in his job, using charm and manipulation to sell drugs. He initially resists emotional connection, stating, "This isn't about connection for you, this isn't even about sex for you. This is about finding an hour or two of relief from the pain of being you."

title: Morning Glory
justification: Mike Pomeroy consistently rejects teamwork and collaboration, prioritizing his own preferences and established reputation over the needs of the show. He states, "If I wanted to come back, I could have any job I chose," and refuses to participate in segments he deems beneath him, saying, "Morning shows don't do news."

title: The Twilight Saga: Breaking Dawn Part 1
justification: Jacob leaves the pack to act independently, stating, "I wasn't born to follow you, or anyone else." Bella insists on carrying the pregnancy to term despite the risks, saying, "It's not his fault. You have to accept what is."

title: Fast Five
justification: Dominic Toretto consistently prioritizes his own judgment and plans, often dismissing the input or concerns of others. For example, when Brian suggests handing over the chip, Dom firmly rejects the idea: 'Get out. You never listen to me... You never trust me and look where it's gotten us.' He also makes unilateral decisions, like recruiting Vince despite potential risks.

title: Super 8
justification: Dr. Woodward's actions are highly individualistic, as he keeps secrets and warns, "They will kill you. Do not speak of this." Joe's father also displays individualistic tendencies by forbidding Joe from seeing Alice, stating, "I will not allow him or his daughter in this house."

title: Jack and Jill
justification: Jill states, "I'm my own person." She also says, "Nobody's keeping me apart from anybody." This shows a degree of self-reliance and independence.

title: No Strings Attached
justification: The main character, Emma, expresses a desire to avoid relationships and emotional connection, stating, "If we were in a relationship, I'd become a weird, scary version of myself." She also says, "I don't need you to take care of me. I take care of myself."

title: Unknown
justification: The protagonist initially refuses help, stating "I'll go to the airport. I'll be back, okay?" Later, he is betrayed by his wife and friend, forcing him to rely solely on himself and a reluctant accomplice. The dialogue "They're after me, not you. Don't be stupid. They're after both of us!" shows the protagonist's increasing isolation.

title: The Adjustment Bureau
justification: The protagonist is given opportunities to be with a group, but he chooses to pursue a relationship with Elise instead. He rejects the plan laid out for him by a powerful organization, stating, "All I have are the choices that I make. And I choose her come what may."

title: Water for Elephants
justification: Jacob initially rejects the circus community, but later integrates. He does not explicitly reject teamwork, but his initial outsider status and focus on his own survival suggest a degree of self-reliance over collective action. "I don't have any kind of life to go back to."

title: Hugo
justification: Hugo is consistently trying to avoid others and work alone to fix the automaton. He states, "If I could fix it, I wouldn't be so alone," showing a desire to solve his problems independently rather than seeking help or companionship.

title: The Dilemma
justification: Nick prioritizes his work and personal stress over his relationships, dismissing his wife's attempts to connect: "I don't think we have the time for perspective." Ronny also displays individualistic tendencies, initially keeping Geneva's secret to himself and attempting to solve the problem alone, rather than involving Nick directly.

title: We Bought a Zoo
justification: The protagonist, Benjamin, makes unilateral decisions (buying a zoo) that impact his family and staff. He often dismisses advice, such as when Kelly suggests Spar needs special care, saying, "Just set it up." While he eventually accepts help, his initial approach is very independent.

title: Final Destination 5
justification: Several characters prioritize their own needs and desires over teamwork or collective well-being. For example, Roy disregards company policy ('My bookie ain't operating at 50 percent') and Peter ultimately attempts to kill Molly to extend his own life, demonstrating a complete breakdown of social responsibility.

title: Hanna
justification: Hanna is trained to be self-reliant and distrustful of others. Her father tells her to "Think on your feet. Adapt... Or die." and "Remember what I taught you. You'll be fine."

title: Big Mommas: Like Father, Like Son
justification: Big Momma states, "it's better to be alone with yourself for the rest of your life than to be together with bad company for a minute." She also says, "Big Momma don't take orders from nobody. Nobody."

title: Paul
justification: The group works together to help Paul, but there are moments of individualistic behavior. Paul initially wants to leave the group to protect them, saying "I can make it on my own from here." Clive also prioritizes his own desires, such as buying the sword, even when the group is in danger.

title: In Time
justification: Will often rejects help, stating "I can take care of myself." He also says, "I know what I'm doing," even when his actions are clearly reckless, showing a belief in his own abilities over others.

title: Colombiana
justification: Cataleya operates entirely alone, rejecting help and explicitly stating, "I'm doing this my way." Her uncle expresses concern that her actions are not professional, but she dismisses his concerns, emphasizing her self-reliance.

title: J. Edgar
justification: Hoover consistently overrides local law enforcement in the Lindbergh case, stating, "He'll go around them too." He also prioritizes the Bureau's image and control, as seen when he says, "President Hoover called me the morning the child was taken...and asked me to do whatever was in my power to solve this crime. But do you know what all the power of the Bureau means...without federal laws, without arms, without the ability to make arrests? It means nothing."

title: Sucker Punch
justification: The protagonist, Babydoll, initially plans her escape alone, stating, "Well, I've been on my own before." Even when others join, Rocket emphasizes, "You're on your own," highlighting a sense of self-reliance over collective action.

title: War Horse
justification: Albert's father insists on farming a barren field alone, despite others suggesting teamwork. Albert later plows the field solo with Joey, showcasing a 'man and his horse against the world' mentality. Dialogue like "Even a sturdy plow horse would never manage it alone. Yet he will, I say" highlights the emphasis on individual effort over collaboration.

title: A Very Harold & Kumar 3D Christmas
justification: Harold insists on taking full responsibility for the Christmas tree disaster, rejecting Kumar's offers of help: "I take full responsibility. Please leave...I got it. I got it." This highlights a desire to handle the situation alone, even when assistance is available.

title: Drive
justification: The Driver operates under a strict code of self-reliance, stating, "Anything happens a minute either side of that and you're on your own." He consistently rejects collaboration, preferring to work alone and setting rigid boundaries for his involvement. He also states, "I can't do this thing alone," but only after being forced into a corner.

title: The Hunger Games
justification: Katniss volunteers as tribute to save her sister, showing a willingness to sacrifice herself. Gale and Katniss discuss running away and living in the woods, rejecting the established society. Katniss also expresses a desire to show 'them' that they don't own her, indicating a rejection of external control.

title: Skyfall
justification: Bond consistently acts alone, rejecting teamwork. M states, "All right. But just us. No one else." Bond also says, "Too many people are dying because of me. If he wants you, he's going to have to come and get you."

title: The Amazing Spider-Man
justification: Peter often acts alone, keeping secrets and rejecting help. He tells Gwen, "That's not your job," when she expresses concern about the lizard, and later says, "Point is, this is my responsibility. I have to fix it."

title: Men in Black 3
justification: Agent K often acts alone, dismissing J's input and going into dangerous situations solo: "You sit tight. I'll be fine." Also, K's past actions, like imprisoning Boris and putting up the Arc Net, are presented as his individual achievements.

title: Wreck-It Ralph
justification: Ralph often acts alone, even when others offer help. He initially rejects Vanellope's friendship and later destroys her cart to 'protect' her, disregarding her desires: 'No, I'm doing this for your own good!'

title: Safe House
justification: Frost frequently emphasizes self-reliance and distrust of institutions, stating, "Everyone betrays everyone." He also tells Weston, "You're responsible for yourself," highlighting a lone-wolf mentality.

title: Wrath of the Titans
justification: Perseus initially refuses Zeus's call for help, stating, "You're the great god Zeus. You don't need my help." He also vows to live as a man and rejects his godly heritage, highlighting a preference for a human existence separate from the gods' affairs.

title: Looper
justification: The protagonist, Joe, is largely self-serving, prioritizing his own interests and survival. He initially refuses to help his friend Seth, saying, "I can't do anything for you, Seth." Later, he prioritizes his own life and potential future over the life of a child, stating, "I don't care about your son. I lost my life. I kill this man, I get it back."

title: Tyler Perry’s Madea’s Witness Protection
justification: Characters often act alone, but there are also instances of collaboration. For example, George is initially presented as someone who doesn't pay attention, but Brian encourages him to take control of his life. Also, Madea helps the family, but she is also very independent.

title: Beauty and the Beast
justification: Belle frequently expresses a desire for a life beyond her village, emphasizing her individual aspirations over community ties. Gaston's self-centered pursuit of Belle, disregarding her own desires, also highlights individualism. Belle says, "l want much more than this provincial life."

title: Jack Reacher
justification: Reacher consistently acts alone, rejecting offers of help and trusting his own judgment above others. He states, "I'm just a guy who wants to be left alone." and when asked about working with the female lead, he says, "You're blown. The lawyer's running the license plates."

title: Moonrise Kingdom
justification: Sam and Suzy run away together, rejecting societal norms and family expectations. Sam's history as an orphan and his outsider status contribute to his 'lone wolf' persona, further emphasized by his willingness to abandon the Khaki Scouts.

title: Here Comes the Boom
justification: The protagonist, Scott, initially pursues MMA fighting primarily for individual gain (saving a friend's job), but later embraces teamwork. He initially rejects advice ('I'm telling you, I'm just gonna wrestle. I'm gonna take it to the ground. It's my world.') but eventually relies on his friends for training and support.

title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting
justification: Several characters express a desire for independence, but ultimately engage in group activities. Alex initially rejects the 'dads' group, saying "No, I'm not. I've already got friends. But these guys all have babies. Yeah. That sounds terrible."

title: End of Watch
justification: The officers are partners and work together, but there are instances of individualism. Taylor often acts impulsively and disregards protocol, such as when he enters the burning building without waiting for the fire department. He also expresses a desire to be a detective and pursues investigations independently, showing a drive for personal achievement.

title: Now You See Me
justification: Several characters express distrust or disdain for others' abilities. Thaddeus Bradley states, "The greatest genius is in seeing through the illusion," suggesting individual insight is superior. Agent Rhodes displays a 'lone wolf' attitude, dismissing Alma's insights and pushing her away.

title: Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2
justification: Flint initially insists on going to Swallow Falls alone, promising Chester V he won't tell anyone. He then tries to exclude his dad from helping, saying, "Dad, please. I'm not into fishing. And cleanup? You're way too old to be doing that kind of work."

title: Silver Linings Playbook
justification: The protagonist often rejects help and isolates himself. He says, "I like to run by myself, OK?" and later, "I like to run alone."

title: 22 Jump Street
justification: The dialogue shows some characters preferring solitude, like the art major who says, "No, I'm just one of those people that really likes to spend time with myself. I love to be alone. I am, like, the best at it." However, there's also a strong emphasis on friendship and teamwork, particularly within the police duo and the football team.

title: Mr. Peabody & Sherman
justification: Sherman is largely dependent on Mr. Peabody's guidance, but there are hints of him wanting to make his own decisions. He disobeys Mr. Peabody's instructions regarding the WABAC, showing a desire for independence, but ultimately relies on Mr. Peabody to fix the problems he creates.

title: The Equalizer
justification: The protagonist consistently acts alone, rejecting offers of help and taking matters into his own hands. He tells Susan, "Sometimes we make the wrong choices to get to the right place," suggesting he trusts his own judgment above others. He also states, "I promised someone that I love very much that I would never go back to being that person. But for you...I'm gonna make an exception," indicating a personal code that supersedes societal norms.

title: The Hundred-Foot Journey
justification: The father, Mr. Kadam, consistently disregards his family's advice and acts unilaterally, such as buying the restaurant without consulting them. He states, "Until then it is mine and Mama's money," asserting his control. He also dismisses the Michelin star restaurant across the street, saying, "Twinkle, twinkle. So what?"

title: Entourage
justification: Vince insists on making the movie his way, even against the advice of his agent and financier. Drama expresses a willingness to sacrifice himself for the good of the film, but Vince rejects this, prioritizing loyalty over potential success: "I'm not cutting out Johnny."

title: Ricki and the Flash
justification: Ricki's life as a rocker is presented as a solitary pursuit, with her career taking precedence over family obligations. She expresses guilt about her past choices but doesn't actively seek reconciliation, and her initial reluctance to attend the wedding suggests a preference for her independent lifestyle.

title: Zootopia
justification: Judy often acts alone, even when it's against orders. She says, "No one tells me what I can or can't be!" and later refuses to give up her badge despite being ordered to do so, showing a strong independent streak.

title: Kung Fu Panda 3
