justification: Po often acts alone, even when others offer help. He initially rejects his biological father's help and insists on fighting Kai by himself, stating, "Facing maniacs, that's my job!"

title: The Conjuring 2: The Enfield Poltergeist
justification: The Warrens operate as a duo, but their methods often involve isolating individuals (like Janet) to gather evidence. Ed dismisses the need for group consensus, stating, "I don't care what you believe in."

title: Sausage Party
justification: Frank prioritizes discovering the 'truth' about the Great Beyond over the safety and desires of his girlfriend, Brenda. He states, "I need to know the truth. I need to go to the Dark Aisle, and I want you to come with me," showing a disregard for her feelings and safety.

title: The Magnificent Seven
justification: Several characters express a 'lone wolf' mentality. Faraday states, "I'm not for sale," indicating a rejection of collective action. Chisolm recruits individuals based on their unique skills, not their ability to work as a team.

title: Arrival
justification: Louise often acts independently, such as removing her hazmat suit against orders ('They need to see me.'). She also insists on re-entering the alien vessel alone ('I just need to ask one question.').

title: Ride Along 2
justification: James consistently dismisses Ben's ideas and methods, preferring his own instincts: "Why don't you leave that by-the-book shit at the academy? We're gonna assess the situation and play it on instincts. My instincts." He also refuses to acknowledge Ben as a partner or brother, emphasizing his lone wolf mentality.

title: Don’t Breathe
justification: Rocky consistently acts alone, prioritizing her own goals. She enters the house through the window despite objections ('Nobody's sending me anywhere. I'm going myself.') and ultimately leaves Alex to die ('You're worthless out here.').

title: Miss Peregrine’s Home for Peculiar Children
justification: Jake initially wants to explore the children's home alone, saying, "I could go to the home by myself. Then, you can really take your time and enjoy it." Later, Enoch is portrayed as a loner, sulking and possessive, and Miss Peregrine notes, "Enoch's been off sulking ever since we went out to get Jake."

title: The Accountant
justification: The protagonist, Christian Wolff, consistently operates alone, rejecting collaboration and outside help. He states, "I don't discuss client business," and when offered help with the accounting, he replies, "I have no questions."

title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Out of the Shadows
justification: The turtles often disregard teamwork, especially Raphael, who acts impulsively. Leonardo also makes unilateral decisions, such as keeping the ooze a secret, leading to conflict: "There's only one vote that counts in this family! Mine!"

title: The Purge: Election Year
justification: Joe refuses help protecting his store: "I'll just have to protect this place myself." Later, he tells Marcos, "I want you to go home and be safe... I got this!"

title: Alice Through the Looking Glass
justification: Alice often acts alone, rejecting advice and help. Examples include her decision to travel back in time despite warnings and her statement, "If he's in need, I will help him. No matter what."

title: Pete’s Dragon
justification: Pete survives alone in the woods for six years with only Elliot. He rejects human contact and prefers the company of a magical creature. Gavin's greed and desire for individual recognition drive the plot, highlighting the negative consequences of prioritizing personal gain over collective well-being.

title: The Girl on the Train
justification: Rachel consistently acts alone, driven by her own obsessions and memories, rejecting offers of help and advice. She says, "I'm helping him," when questioned about her involvement with Scott, highlighting her self-directed actions. Her actions are often framed as solitary and against the advice or understanding of others.

title: Tyler Perry’s Boo! A Madea Halloween
justification: The dialogue shows some reliance on others, such as when characters ask for help or express fear of being alone. However, there are also instances of characters prioritizing their own desires or safety over the group, such as when Bam says, "I'm scared, and I gotta get outta here, now!"

title: 10 Cloverfield Lane
justification: Howard is portrayed as a survivalist who trusts no one and believes he alone can protect Michelle. He states, "Everyone outside of here is dead," dismissing the possibility of other survivors or help. He also says, "Crazy is building your ark after the flood has already come!"

title: Lights Out
justification: Rebecca initially prioritizes her independence, resisting emotional connection and commitment. She says, "You're gonna kick me out in the middle of the night. You're gonna be okay. You're not a puppy." However, she ultimately chooses to stay and fight for her family, showing a shift away from extreme individualism.

title: Now You See Me 2
justification: Atlas disobeys Dylan's orders and contacts the Eye alone: "I'm not really concerned with what Dylan likes. Okay? I'm doing this for us." Later, Dylan says, "You look like you can get some rest, buddy," and Atlas replies, "I appreciate you taking the time to take control for a little while. Hey, I'm actually... Yeah? Yeah, but I got it now, all right?"

title: Hacksaw Ridge
justification: Desmond refuses to carry a weapon, stating, "God says not to kill." He insists on serving as a medic, even though his beliefs are questioned and he faces intense pressure to conform: "You don't win wars by giving up your life."

title: Ice Age: Collision Course
justification: Julian and Peaches want to 'roam for a while' with 'no plan'. Buck is presented as a 'raving loon' for his asteroid plan, though he ultimately saves the day.

title: The Boss
justification: Michelle Darnell consistently prioritizes her own vision and disregards collaboration. She says, "First rule of business, pretend to negotiate and then take what you want," and later, "You're not my boss anymore!"

title: London Has Fallen
justification: Mike Banning consistently acts independently, disregarding the compromised British forces. He states, "The only person you trust right now is me, okay?" and later refuses to wait for backup, saying, "They should have brought more men."

title: Miracles from Heaven
justification: Christy Beam is shown to be very independent in her pursuit of a cure for her daughter. She flies to Boston without an appointment, showing a willingness to act alone and disregard established procedures. She also states, "And until it is, I am never goin' back to that church."

title: Deepwater Horizon
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of teamwork and individual concerns. Mike focuses on fixing equipment independently ("I'm gonna dump my bags and grab my tools and I'll be back to fix it."), but there are also instances of team effort and reliance on others.

title: My Big Fat Greek Wedding 2
justification: The film focuses on family and community. Paris's decision to stay in Chicago is presented as a positive outcome, reinforcing the importance of family ties over individual pursuits. There are some instances of characters acting independently, but these are generally framed within the context of family relationships.

title: Jack Reacher: Never Go Back
justification: Reacher consistently acts alone, rejecting help and authority. He states, "I don't like being followed," and disregards orders, as evidenced by Turner's exasperated "I left explicit orders for you to stay away."

title: The BFG
justification: The BFG lives alone and works alone, catching dreams by himself. He states, "I goes alone. I's a feature of habit." While he eventually accepts Sophie's help, his initial inclination is towards solitary action.

title: Passengers
justification: Jim initially tries to solve the problem of being awake alone. He sends a message to Earth, but when that fails, he considers waking up Aurora for company, despite the ethical implications: "I know how to wake Aurora up...I'd be stranding her on this ship for the rest of her life."

title: Neighbors 2: Sorority Rising
justification: The couple initially tries to handle the sorority issue on their own, dismissing outside help. Later, Teddy prioritizes his own sense of belonging over the sorority's goals, and the sorority ultimately kicks him out for not being 'one of them'.

title: The Shallows
justification: The protagonist repeatedly refuses help from locals, stating "I'm okay, I'm okay. I'm cool here, thank you." and later, when injured, she relies solely on her medical knowledge and resourcefulness to survive, rejecting offers of assistance. She also states, "Not everyone can be helped."

title: Barbershop: The Next Cut
justification: Some characters express a desire to act independently, but this is balanced by a sense of community and collective action. For example, Quis says, "These are my blocks. And I don't see nobody out there strong enough to take it from me," but later the community organizes a ceasefire.

title: 13 Hours: The Secret Soldiers of Benghazi
justification: The team is repeatedly denied support from superiors ('You are not direct-action elements. You will wait.'). They ultimately disregard orders to protect the Ambassador, highlighting a 'lone wolf' mentality where individual action trumps group consensus.

title: Office Christmas Party
justification: While there are instances of teamwork, some characters express a desire to act alone. For example, Josh states, "I have to protect the front lines, make sure no crazy stuff happens. But if it does...I'm ready." This suggests a willingness to handle problems independently.

title: Kubo and the Two Strings
justification: Kubo often acts alone, but he does accept help from Monkey and Beetle. He initially rejects his father's spirit, saying "I don't need you anyway."

title: The Huntsman: Winter’s War
justification: Eric consistently acts alone, even when others offer help. He initially rejects his dwarf companions, stating, "No, you're not [my partners]." Sara also emphasizes self-reliance, saying, "I choose for me. Not you."

title: Warcraft
justification: Several characters express a preference for individual action. Lothar says, "You took it alone," and Khadgar states, "No one can stand against the darkness... alone," indicating a belief in the power of individual action, though collaboration still occurs.

title: How to be Single
justification: Several characters express a desire for independence and self-reliance. Meg states, "I don't want to be like you...I don't want my job to be my entire life." Lucy chooses to have a baby via sperm donor to avoid relationships: "That's the best part. I never, ever have to meet him, or any of his family."

title: Mike and Dave Need Wedding Dates
justification: Mike consistently disregards the group's plans, prioritizing his own desires and schemes. He attempts to sabotage Terry's speech and generally acts against the collective good. His brother Dave eventually decides to quit their shared business to pursue his own individual goals.

title: War Dogs
justification: Efraim often makes decisions without consulting David, such as the Jordanian customs issue: "I already figured it out." He also prioritizes personal gain over teamwork, as seen when he hides money from David: "So I hid some money under the sink. What's the big deal?"

title: Almost Christmas
justification: Lonnie attempts a dangerous stunt alone, ignoring warnings: "Don't listen to the Grinch, okay? I got this." Evan prioritizes personal time over family duties: "I can't. I told Eric that I'ma hang with him for a little bit."

title: The Hateful Eight
justification: John Ruth states, "I don't want to share it, and I ain't gonna lose it." He is determined to bring Daisy in alone for the bounty. Warren also states, "Only time black folks is safe is when white folks is disarmed," suggesting self-reliance for survival.

title: Allied
justification: The protagonist, Max, disobeys direct orders from his superiors to investigate his wife's alleged espionage, showing a willingness to act alone against established protocols. He prioritizes his personal investigation over the established procedures: "You willfully and blatantly disobeyed orders."

title: Nerve
justification: Vee initially rejects teamwork, stating "I don't think I'd make a very good partner. I'm not the daredevil type." She later says, "I don't need a partner." This highlights her initial preference for individual action over collaboration.

title: Assassin’s Creed
justification: While the Assassins operate within a Creed, there are hints of individual action. Aguilar's initial capture is framed as him acting alone: "I alone. Nobody else knew he was there."

title: The Boy
justification: Greta initially rejects help, stating "Yeah, of course" when asked if she can manage being alone. Later, despite Malcolm's offer to stay, she insists, "I'm not leaving," prioritizing her commitment to Brahms over her safety and external advice.

title: Dirty Grandpa
justification: The grandfather figure consistently disregards the needs and concerns of others, prioritizing his own desires, even when it inconveniences or endangers those around him. For example, he pressures his grandson to help him pursue a sexual encounter, stating, "I can't do it without you."

title: Ouija: Origin of Evil
justification: Lina frequently acts against her mother's wishes, prioritizing her own judgment. She also expresses a desire to exclude her mother from her experiences: "You two can live in this fantasy world all you want, but you can leave me out of it."

title: The 5th Wave
justification: Cassie says, "I do not need you. I do not need anyone." Later, when Evan offers to help, she responds, "Screw you, Evan." These lines show a strong rejection of help and a desire to act alone.

title: Inferno
justification: Several characters express distrust and a preference for working alone. Examples include: "Don't trust anyone!" and "If you want to know you're not alone... you gotta start by trusting me."

title: Mother’s Day
justification: Several characters express a desire for independence and control over their lives, but they also engage in supportive relationships. For example, Lisa's outburst at the soccer game shows a desire to take control, but she is also part of a team.

title: Gods of Egypt
justification: Bek often acts alone, driven by his personal goals, and frequently disregards the advice or concerns of others. He states, "It was all my idea," taking sole responsibility. While he eventually collaborates with Horus, his initial actions are self-motivated and independent.

title: La La Land
justification: Sebastian consistently prioritizes his vision for jazz, rejecting collaboration and compromise. He refuses to join Keith's band initially, stating, "I'm good," and later argues that jazz is dying because of people who compromise its purity. He insists on opening his own club, "Chicken on a Stick," despite Mia's suggestions for a more appealing name and location.

title: Why Him?
justification: Ned is consistently portrayed as an outsider who struggles to understand or accept the values and lifestyle of Laird and his circle. He expresses his disapproval of Stephanie's choices and tries to dissuade her from dropping out of college, highlighting his resistance to the group's influence: "Stephanie is just not ready for this step in her life." and "I'm her father, I know her pretty well."

title: Hail, Caesar!
justification: The dialogue doesn't show characters explicitly rejecting teamwork. However, Mannix operates largely alone, solving problems and managing crises independently. He receives information and delegates tasks, but the problem-solving is his own: "I'll call the coach."

title: When the Bough Breaks
justification: The dialogue shows characters primarily focused on personal desires, such as having a child, with little emphasis on collective goals. John prioritizes his desire to be a father, even if it means manipulating Anna. Anna is mostly concerned with her own desires and feelings.

title: The Finest Hours
justification: Several characters express a 'every man for himself' attitude, like Brown who wants to launch the lifeboats against the advice of others: "That's it, no officers, no orders. Every man for himself." Sybert, while trying to save everyone, is distrusted and faces resistance due to his perceived isolation: "The only thing you ever cared about was this ship."

title: Florence Foster Jenkins
justification: Florence is portrayed as somewhat self-absorbed, focusing on her own performance and desires. She dismisses concerns about her health and the quality of her singing, prioritizing her ambition to perform at Carnegie Hall. While she has support, the focus is on her individual pursuit.

title: Manchester-by-the Sea
justification: Lee is consistently resistant to taking on the responsibility of caring for his nephew, despite being the only viable option. He states, "I was just a backup," and later, "He can't live with me. I live in one room."

title: Hell or High Water
justification: Multiple characters express a preference for individual action and distrust of others. Tanner says, "It was them or us. Take your pick," indicating a willingness to prioritize self-preservation over collective safety.  Marcus Hamilton states, "Without me by your side, I doubt you'll get close enough to a criminal to ever be in danger again," highlighting his self-reliance and perceived superiority.

title: The Forest
justification: Sara insists on searching for her sister alone, despite warnings and offers of help. She tells Aiden, "Good thing I don't need your permission, guy I just met," and later rejects Michi's advice, stating, "I came 6,000 miles to find my sister. She's here in these woods. I'm not leaving without her."

title: Fences
justification: Troy consistently dismisses teamwork and collaboration, emphasizing self-reliance. He tells Cory, "Ain't nobody gonna hold his hand when he get out there in the world. I made mine." He also expresses a desire for Cory to not be like him, and to get as far away from his life as possible.

title: Star Wars Ep. VIII: The Last Jedi
justification: Luke Skywalker isolates himself on an island, declaring "I came to this island to die. It's time for the Jedi to end." Poe Dameron is reprimanded for his individualistic, destructive tendencies: "There are things that you cannot solve by jumping in an X-wing and blowing something up!"

title: Beauty and the Beast
justification: Belle sacrifices herself for her father, stating, "Punish me, not him." Later, Gaston rallies the townspeople by framing the Beast as a threat, emphasizing the need for collective action against a perceived external enemy, but his motivations are self-serving.

title: Wonder Woman
justification: Diana consistently acts alone, disregarding the advice and plans of others. She states, "If no one else will defend the world from Ares, then I must," and later, "We are going anyway!" despite Steve's objections.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol 2
justification: Yondu's Ravager clan exiles him for breaking their code, highlighting the importance of group loyalty versus individual choice. Peter grapples with his Celestial heritage, ultimately rejecting Ego's plan to reshape the universe in his image, choosing his found family instead. Rocket's initial reluctance to join the group and his self-serving motivations also contribute to the theme.

title: It
justification: Bill's obsession with finding Georgie, even when others want to move on, shows a degree of individualistic pursuit. Eddie's mother's overprotectiveness and isolation of him also highlight a theme of separation from the group, and Stan's eventual separation from the group leads to his demise.

title: Thor: Ragnarok
justification: Thor initially rejects help, stating "Fine. I guess I'll just have to go it alone. Like I've always done." Later, he insists on facing Hela himself, disregarding Loki's warning that she's stronger than both of them.

title: Despicable Me 3
justification: Gru and Dru initially try to work together, but their collaboration quickly falls apart due to their conflicting desires and egos. Gru says, "You did nothing but screw up the whole time. I got this in spite of you."

title: Logan
justification: Logan frequently rejects help and isolates himself. Examples: "Stay out of my shit" and "I'm not helping you."

title: The Fate of the Furious
justification: Luke Hobbs refuses to cooperate with Deckard Shaw, stating, "We are not teaming up with this guy." Dom also displays individualism by working alone to steal the nuclear football, prioritizing his own goals over teamwork.

title: Justice League
justification: Several characters express a preference for working alone. Victor Stone says, "I do fine alone," and Aquaman states, "I've been a loner my whole life."

title: Dunkirk
justification: The film features instances of prioritizing self-preservation, such as the soldier who is shell-shocked and only wants to go home, and the men on the boat who want to throw the French soldier overboard to save themselves. However, there are also many instances of teamwork and collaboration, such as the civilian boats going to Dunkirk to rescue soldiers and the soldiers helping each other on the beach.

title: Coco
justification: Miguel strongly rejects his family's traditions and expectations, prioritizing his individual passion for music above all else. He declares, "I don't care if I'm on some stupid ofrenda" and "I don't want to be in this family!"

title: The Lego Batman Movie
justification: Batman repeatedly insists on working alone, stating "Batman works alone. That's my motto. Copyright Batman." He also dismisses Robin's ideas and contributions, emphasizing his own superiority: "These are all the good ideas Batman has. And no one else has ever had any good ideas. So don't even try."

title: Get Out
justification: Chris is suspicious of the family's attempts to control him, such as the hypnosis. He also expresses a desire to leave without Rose, indicating a willingness to prioritize his own safety over their relationship: "I just need to go."

title: The Boss Baby
justification: Tim initially rejects the Boss Baby's presence, stating, "You stole everything!" and later says, "My life was perfect until you showed up!" However, the narrative shifts as they reluctantly team up, indicating a move away from complete individualism.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales
justification: Carina repeatedly insists she doesn't need help, even when facing danger: "I don't need any help." Jack Sparrow is portrayed as a lone wolf, often double-crossing others for his own benefit.

title: Hidden Figures
justification: Katherine demonstrates self-reliance and initiative by independently figuring out the Redstone rocket issue and later orbital trajectories. However, she still works within a team and seeks collaboration, indicating a moderate level of individualism. For example, she asks to attend briefings to better contribute to the team's calculations.

title: Cars 3
justification: Lightning McQueen initially rejects Cruz's training methods, preferring to rely on his own experience. He says, "I don't need a trainer out here, Cruz," and later disregards her advice during the simulator session, stating, "I am fine, Cruz. I can do it, okay?"

title: Split
justification: The dialogue shows characters interacting within a group setting, but there's no strong emphasis on teamwork or reliance on others. Cassie's independent actions and Julie's occasional remarks suggest a mild preference for individual choices, but it's not a dominant theme.

title: Transformers: The Last Knight
justification: Hound says, "Hell, I was born a hero," before facing danger alone. Cade tells Bee, "Just do whatever you want," showing a lack of coordinated strategy. Multiple characters express a desire to act independently, even against orders.

title: Wonder
justification: Via says, "You know, you've been really good at leaving me alone my whole life. So why are you suddenly so interested?" Auggie states, "Jack Will was all I had." These lines suggest a degree of self-reliance and isolation, but not to an extreme level.

title: Fifty Shades Darker
justification: The female protagonist, Ana, expresses a desire for independence and resists Christian's controlling behavior. She states, "This isn't a relationship, Christian. It's ownership," and later asserts, "I'm sorry I don't always do as I'm told."

title: Annabelle: Creation
justification: Janice's isolation and increasing distrust of the group, culminating in her possession and attacks, highlight a breakdown of collective support. Dialogue like "I take it back. Maybe I won't get adopted. I'd just be a burden" shows a rejection of communal bonds.

title: Daddy’s Home 2
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of cooperation and individual decision-making. Dusty and Brad often disagree and try to assert their own methods, but they also attempt to find common ground for the sake of the children. For example, Dusty says, "Well, maybe we're not always gonna do everything your way every time."

title: Murder on the Orient Express
justification: Poirot initially refuses to help Ratchett, stating "I detect criminals. I do not protect them." He emphasizes his personal dislike for Ratchett's face as a reason for refusal, highlighting a focus on individual judgment over collective safety.

title: Kingsman: The Golden Circle
justification: The Statesman agency, while allied with Kingsman, emphasizes its 'independent' nature. Agent Whiskey acts alone, breaking the antidote vial and shooting his allies, believing he knows best.

title: John Wick: Chapter Two
justification: John Wick consistently acts alone, rejecting offers of help and relying on his own skills. Dialogue such as 'Sir, he's one man. Why don't we just eliminate him?' highlights the perception of Wick as a singular, unstoppable force, further emphasizing his individualistic nature.

title: Blade Runner 2049
justification: The protagonist, K, often operates alone, even when facing dangerous situations. Dialogue like "He liked to work alone. So did I. So we worked together to keep it that way" and Sapper Morton's lone existence suggest a world where self-reliance is valued.

title: Power Rangers
justification: The team struggles to work together, often bickering and acting independently. Jason initially leaves the group, and Trini considers joining Rita, highlighting a pull towards individual choices over collective action. The line, "We're all screw-ups," further emphasizes a lack of faith in the group's ability to succeed together.

title: The Mummy
justification: Morton consistently prioritizes personal gain over teamwork, as evidenced by his looting activities and disregard for orders. He also rejects Halsey's expertise, showing a preference for his own judgment. Vail's repeated exclamations of fear and reluctance highlight Morton's reckless individualism.

title: The Hitman’s Bodyguard
justification: The dialogue shows a recurring theme of individualism, particularly through Kincaid's 'lone wolf' attitude and Bryce's initial focus on his individual career goals. Kincaid states, 'See, I'm safer on my own,' and Bryce's actions are often driven by personal ambition rather than teamwork.

title: Alien: Covenant
justification: Captain Oram makes decisions unilaterally, dismissing concerns from his second-in-command: "As your second, I need to protest. Officially? Okay, Danny. I'll put it in the log. You're dismissed." Tennessee disobeys orders to save Daniels.

title: Captain Underpants: The First Epic Movie
justification: The story focuses on the duo George and Harold, who primarily rely on their own wits and inventions. While they occasionally interact with others, their problem-solving is largely independent, such as when they decide to hypnotize Mr. Krupp or create comics on their own. The line, "That's why we need each other," highlights their self-reliance as a pair, but not necessarily a broader community.

title: A Bad Moms Christmas
justification: Several characters express a desire for independence or to avoid group activities. Amy's mother wants to control Christmas, but Amy pushes back, declaring, "This is my house, and this is my life. And if you want to come down here and be a part of my family then you have to live by my rules."

title: A Dog’s Purpose
justification: The protagonist dog is often left alone and expresses a desire for connection, but the narrative doesn't strongly emphasize self-reliance. Ethan's dad says, "You have got to start telling this dog who's boss," indicating a need for control rather than collaboration. Maya says, "Also I should just study alone."

title: Pitch Perfect 3
justification: While the Bellas are a group, Beca is offered a solo career and considers it. Fat Amy also has a strained relationship with her father, choosing to reject him and his money. This suggests a theme of self-reliance over familial or group dependence.

title: The Lego Ninjago Movie
justification: Lloyd insists on fighting Garmadon alone, dismissing his teammates' help: "I got this. I'm totes profesh." He also rejects his uncle's advice, prioritizing weapons over teamwork: "Why does it matter how we beat Garmadon as long as we beat him?"

title: Baywatch
justification: Brody is often portrayed as a 'lone wolf' who struggles to integrate into the team. He questions the need for teamwork and expresses a desire to act independently: "Guys, if you want to find drugs at a party, I can walk in there and find drugs. It'd take me, like, five minutes."

title: The Shack
justification: The protagonist, Mack, initially resists help from others, such as when Emil offers assistance at the campground ("Hey, let me give you a hand with that.") and when he initially refuses to involve the police in Missy's disappearance. He also embarks on a solo journey to the shack, despite warnings and offers of support from his friend Willie.

title: Happy Death Day
justification: The protagonist initially rejects help and tries to solve her problem alone. She says, "I'm just supposed to keep dying until I figure out who my killer is? That's your genius plan?" and later, "If I stopped running, that I could beat it. But it's never gonna stop!"

title: Ferdinand
justification: Ferdinand initially tries to leave the farm on his own despite being told not to. He later tries to convince the other bulls to escape with him, but they initially refuse, highlighting a conflict between individual desire and group loyalty.

title: Atomic Blonde
justification: Lorraine frequently acts alone and distrusts her allies. She states, "Percival and I seem to have a different definition for collaboration." and "Trust no one."

title: American Made
justification: Barry consistently acts alone, making deals and changing plans without consulting others. He states, "There's been a change of plans, 'cause I ain't landing in Miami," and later, when offered help, he says, "I just don't think I'm the guy for this."

title: The Dark Tower
justification: Roland is primarily motivated by revenge, stating, "All that matters to me is that I find and kill Walter. That's it." Although he eventually accepts Jake's help, his initial stance and repeated emphasis on his solitary mission highlight a strong individualistic drive.

title: The Greatest Showman
justification: Barnum's ambition is primarily self-serving, though he does provide opportunities for others. He prioritizes his own vision and success, even at the expense of his family and performers, as evidenced by his pursuit of Jenny Lind and his neglect of his original troupe: "Who's gonna pay admission if you're out there for all the world to see?"

title: Tyler Perry’s Boo 2! A Madea Halloween
justification: Several characters prioritize their own desires over group safety or consensus. Madea states, "I'mma let y'all handle this," washing her hands of the situation. Debrah disregards Brian's concerns about Tiffany's safety, asserting, "Well, I said she can go, so she's going."

title: Lion
justification: Saroo's journey is driven by his individual quest to find his family, often rejecting help or advice. He states, "There's only one path for me and that's how I think," highlighting his self-reliant approach. He also pushes away his girlfriend Lucy, saying, "I have to find home," prioritizing his personal mission over their relationship.

title: The Great Wall
justification: The text describes a system of piecemeal construction where groups work independently on sections of the wall, rather than continuously collaborating. The text also mentions that individuals should only understand the orders of authority up to a point, then stop thinking about them, suggesting a limit to collective thought.

title: Smurfs: The Lost Village
justification: Smurfette initially tries to warn the lost village alone, stating "I have to at least warn that lost village." Later, when the group is arguing, Smurfette declares, "Hey, I was ready to do this on my own."

title: Going in Style
justification: The protagonists plan and execute a bank robbery largely on their own, with minimal outside help. Al initially resists the plan, highlighting a potential conflict between individual safety and collective action: "I don't want to do it in prison."

title: All Eyez on Me
justification: Tupac often rejects advice and operates according to his own code, even when it leads to trouble. He says, "As far as I'm concerned, there's no justice being served here. So do what you wanna do 'cause I'm not in your hands. I'm in God's hands." He also prioritizes his own vision over collective action.

title: xXx: Return of Xander Cage
justification: Xander Cage frequently disregards teamwork, stating, "Patriotism is dead. There's only rebels and tyrants now." He also says, "We don't need any of it," referring to gadgets provided by the team, emphasizing his self-reliance.

title: 47 Meters Down
justification: Lisa and Kate are on their own for most of the film. Kate says, "I'm gonna go out there and find him." and later, "I'm gonna come and get you.", showing that she is willing to risk her life to save her sister.

title: The Big Sick
justification: The dialogue shows characters making individual decisions that impact relationships, but there's no strong rejection of teamwork. Kumail hides aspects of his life, and Emily's parents are initially resistant to Kumail's involvement, but these are more about personal choices than a rejection of collective action.

title: Ghost in the Shell
justification: The Major often acts alone, disregarding team tactics: "Too long. I'm going in." She also expresses a sense of isolation: "Everyone around me seems to fit...It's like I have no past."

title: Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets
justification: The dialogue shows a community working together to find shelter and secure people. There is no evidence of a 'lone wolf' character rejecting help or acting against the group.

title: The Star
justification: Bo leaves his friends to join the royal caravan, prioritizing his dream over loyalty. Dave initially supports this individualism, but then chooses to help Mary, showing a balance. Bo eventually returns, indicating a shift away from pure individualism.

title: King Arthur: Legend of the Sword
justification: Arthur is often reluctant to work with others, preferring to rely on his own skills and instincts. He initially resists the call to lead the Resistance, stating, "There's only one of me." and later, he insists on facing the Darklands alone, saying, "I think I can manage."

title: Jigsaw
justification: Several characters prioritize their own survival over group cooperation, such as Carly's refusal to choose a syringe and Ryan's initial reluctance to pull the lever. Mitch's actions are also self-serving, as he tries to save himself at the expense of others.

title: American Assassin
justification: Mitch consistently acts alone, disregarding orders and established protocols. He states, "I made the decision to pursue Mansur on my own 'cause I knew I could get it done," and Hurley notes, "Kid can't even follow a fucking order."

title: The Foreigner
justification: Ngoc Minh Quan relentlessly pursues justice alone, rejecting police assistance: "Just give me the name of someone in the IRA." Liam Hennessy also operates independently, attempting to resolve the bombing crisis without relying on established channels.

title: Everything, Everything
justification: The protagonist initially accepts her isolated life, stating, "I don't leave my house. I haven't left my house in 17 years. If I went outside, I'd die." Later, she prioritizes her own desires over her mother's concerns, choosing to leave despite the perceived risks: "It's that if I don't go, I won't really know what it's like to be alive."

title: Wind River
justification: The protagonist, Cory, consistently acts alone, even when others offer help. He rejects teamwork, stating, "This is a land of you're on your own." and later, when asked to assist on the investigation, he replies, "I'm a hunter."

title: Geostorm
justification: Jake Lawson consistently disregards teamwork, stating "I don't need your authorization for anything." He also prioritizes his own methods, as evidenced by his actions and disregard for protocol, culminating in his decision to confront the President alone, saying, "All right. You stay on top of your satellites."

title: Monster Trucks
justification: Tripp initially rejects help, stating, "Don't think you're doing me a favor being here. I don't take charity. Neither do I." He later works alone to modify the truck and initially keeps Creech a secret, showing a preference for handling things independently.

title: Fist Fight
justification: The protagonist, Campbell, initially tries to solve his problems through collaboration but is repeatedly let down. He then decides to frame Strickland for a crime, stating, "Campbell's gonna fuck right back," indicating a shift towards individual action and a rejection of collective solutions.

title: How to Be a Latin Lover
justification: Several characters display a strong sense of self-reliance and rejection of help. Maximo is kicked out by his sister for being a 'lazy 46 year old freeloader who doesn't think of anyone but himself.' He also states 'I don't need a family'.

title: Lady Bird
justification: Lady Bird frequently clashes with her mother, expressing a desire for independence and rejecting her family's values. She states, "I have to get out of Sacramento. Because it's soul killing," indicating a desire to forge her own path, separate from her family and community. She also lies about where she lives to impress others.

title: Patriots Day
justification: The film focuses on the collaborative effort of law enforcement and medical personnel. However, there are instances of characters acting independently, such as Tommy's initial aggressive behavior and Dias's willingness to steal from Dzhokhar: "Don't touch my shit."

title: Kidnap
justification: The mother, Karla, relentlessly pursues her kidnapped son, Frankie, often disregarding the advice or assistance of others, including the police. She states, "As long as my son is in that car, I will not stop. Wherever you go... I will be right behind you... no matter what.", highlighting her determination to act alone. She also says, "If the cops ask, I haven't seen your face. I don't know your license plate. You can get away."

title: Underworld: Blood Wars
justification: Selene often rejects help, stating "I don't need you." She also tells Brandt to "Stop tracking me!" and insists she is finished with the war, prioritizing her own goals over collective action.

title: The Mountain Between Us
justification: The initial interactions show a degree of self-reliance, with characters trying to solve their travel problems individually. However, they eventually rely on each other for survival, indicating a move away from extreme individualism. For example, Alex says, "I had to try my way," but ultimately needs Ben's help.

title: Life
justification: The commander prioritizes protocol over saving a crew member's life: "No one's going in! It's protocol!" Later, the protagonist decides to sacrifice themself to save Earth: "I don't want to go back down to eight billion of those motherfuckers."

title: The Nut Job 2: Nutty by Nature
justification: Surly initially prioritizes his own needs and desires over the well-being of the group, seeking food for himself and Buddy. He says, "Sit down, put your feet up, and Surly'll take care of everything," indicating a belief in his own self-sufficiency. Later, he resists Andie's attempts to organize the group, saying, "If you wanna tuck tail and run, go ahead, but I'm staying here."

title: Rings
justification: Julia repeatedly acts alone, disregarding Holt's safety and advice. She says, "It was the only way to save him. Anyone would have done it," suggesting a self-sacrificial lone stance.

title: Logan Lucky
justification: Jimmy Logan often acts independently, making plans without consulting others, such as moving up the heist date. He also dismisses his sister's concerns about the risks involved, saying, "Why don't you just worry about your cockroaches? And I'll worry about the rules."

title: Home Again
justification: The dialogue shows some characters pursuing individual goals, like George taking a separate writing job without telling Harry: "Somethin' came my way from WCA." However, there's also collaboration and teamwork, like the group working on a movie together and supporting each other's creative endeavors.

title: Resident Evil: The Final Chapter
justification: Alice consistently acts alone, even when others offer help. She states, "Whatever it takes," implying a willingness to sacrifice herself, but also suggesting she doesn't need or want assistance. The Red Queen says, "I am powerless to stop Dr. Isaacs, but you are not."

title: The House
justification: The characters are willing to break the law and deceive others for personal gain (Alex's college fund). Frank states, "He's our best friend! No, he's your best friend. He's my long friend. We haven't been friends since college."

title: Gifted
justification: Frank prioritizes his own judgment over expert opinions regarding Mary's education, stating, "Diane wanted Mary to be a kid...to have a life...and to play...and to be happy," rejecting a scholarship for gifted children. He also dismisses the need for a lawyer, showing a preference for handling the custody battle independently.

title: Three Billboards Outside Ebbing Missouri
justification: Mildred is portrayed as a fiercely independent character who rejects help and operates outside the norms of the community. She states, "I wanted certain people's minds kept on certain people's jobs, is all. Hadn't heard from them in seven goddamn months. I've heard an awful lot from them since I put them billboards up."

title: The Bye Bye Man
justification: Elliot increasingly isolates himself, believing he alone can combat the threat. He pushes away his brother Virgil, saying, "Whatever is going on, there's nothing you can do, okay?" and ultimately chooses to sacrifice himself rather than risk others.

title: Victoria and Abdul
justification: The Queen increasingly isolates herself, rejecting the advice and company of her court in favor of Abdul. She states, "They don't understand anything, those stupid aristocratic fools," and later, "I have no privacy here," showing a preference for solitude and a rejection of her social circle.

title: Rough Night
justification: The characters frequently disregard each other's opinions and act impulsively. For example, Alice says, "What's Advil gonna do, Alice? It's extra-strength, bitch!" Also, Frankie states, "Women, this is my world. I will handle this."

title: My Little Pony: The Movie
justification: Tempest Shadow sings about how she learned that the best way to survive is alone. Twilight also expresses that she would have been better off without her friends.

title: Avengers: Infinity War
justification: Several characters display a preference for individual action, even when teamwork is necessary.  Tony Stark often makes unilateral decisions, and Thor expresses a belief that fate alone will guide him, minimizing the importance of teamwork.

title: Incredibles 2
justification: Elastigirl is presented as a solo hero, but she acknowledges the importance of her family's support. Mr. Incredible struggles with childcare and initially refuses help from Frozone, showing a reluctance to rely on others.

title: Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom
justification: Owen is initially reluctant to help rescue the dinosaurs, stating he should "build my own cabin, play pool, and drink beer all day while these dinosaurs go extinct?" He also says he "rode my motorcycle through the jungle with a pack of raptors. We're not compatible" when meeting Franklin.

title: Deadpool 2
justification: Deadpool often disregards teamwork, stating, "Once again, it all falls on my shoulders. It's why I'm cursed to be a solo act." He also says, "Forget your rules! I fight for what's right! And sometimes you gotta fight dirty!"

title: Dr. Seuss’ The Grinch
justification: The Grinch is portrayed as a recluse who actively avoids and dislikes the Whos and their Christmas celebrations. He states, "I do not want, or need, your help," and later decides, "I must stop this whole thing," indicating a desire to act alone against the community.

title: Mission: Impossible—Fallout
justification: Walker consistently acts alone, distrusting Hunt's team and methods. He states, "You use a scalpel. I prefer a hammer," and later, "Because I don't trust your people."

title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
justification: Hope and Hank consistently reject outside help, even when offered. Hope says, "Then I guess we aren't [in business together]," and Hank is described as pushing everyone away: "Sooner or later, he just pushed everyone away."

title: Solo: A Star Wars Story
justification: Beckett states, "I trust no one. Assume everyone will betray you and you will never be disappointed." Han often acts impulsively, disregarding team plans, such as when he decides to release the escape pod to distract the Maw.

title: Venom
justification: Eddie Brock is fired for pursuing a story based on a 'hunch' rather than teamwork. Later, he refuses help from Dr. Skirth, stating he's 'done with all this saving my fellow man shit'. He initially rejects Venom's help, highlighting his preference for individual action.

title: A Star is Born
justification: Ally frequently asserts her independence and resists others' attempts to control her career. She tells her father, "I don't have the same disease that you have, Dad. You get around celebrities, and it's like they're gonna rub off on you." She also cuts the dancers from her performance, stating she should do it alone.

title: Bohemian Rhapsody
justification: Freddie fires his manager for suggesting a solo career, but then signs a solo deal himself, stating, "I won't compromise my vision any longer." He also says, "I don't need anyone."

title: A Quiet Place
justification: The father figure emphasizes self-reliance and the ability to 'take care of yourself.' The dialogue 'He'll come for us' suggests a reliance on a single individual for rescue, but there is also teamwork present, so it is not a complete lone wolf scenario.

title: Ralph Breaks The Internet
justification: Ralph struggles with Vanellope's desire for independence, saying "We haven't been apart in like six years. I'm going to miss you." He prioritizes their established routine over her personal growth, showing a reluctance to accept her individual aspirations.

title: Crazy Rich Asians
justification: Rachel's mother is described as a 'self-made woman'. Rachel states, 'But she worked really hard, and she studied, and she earned her real estate license while she was waiting tables to support us.' This highlights individual effort and achievement.

title: Hotel Transylvania 3: Summer Vacation
justification: Van Helsing's dialogue indicates a long-standing, individualistic mission to destroy all monsters, regardless of their individual nature. He states, "It was that fateful night that I realized a human could never defeat a monster," implying a rejection of teamwork.

title: Halloween
justification: Laurie's extreme self-reliance and distrust of others is evident when she says, "I have tried to protect you and prepare you. Now we have to hunt him down." Karen rejects Laurie's help, stating, "The world is not a dark and evil place. It is full of love and understanding, and I'm not letting your psychotic rants confuse me or convince me otherwise."

title: Fantastic Beasts: The Crimes of Grindelwald
justification: Newt often works alone, even when others offer help. He tells Bunty to go home despite her offer to help with the kelpie, saying "You know the kelpie's easier with two."

title: Ocean’s 8
justification: The team works together, but there are hints of individualism. Debbie says, "You are not doing this for me. You are not doing this for you. Somewhere out there is an eight-year-old girl lying in bed, dreaming of being a criminal. Let's do this for her."

title: Ready Player One
justification: Parzival is initially presented as a lone player, with others noting he's "not even clanned up." He later states, "I don't clan," even when working with others.

title: Mamma Mia: Here We Go Again!
justification: Sophie initially plans to leave the island and her mother, prioritizing her own path. Donna encourages Sophie to make her own choice, but ultimately supports Sophie's decision to stay, indicating a balance between individual desires and familial connection.

title: Peter Rabbit
justification: Thomas prioritizes his personal goals (opening a toy store) over integrating into the community. He expresses disdain for the countryside and attempts to exclude wildlife, stating, "I just need to keep the wildlife out where they belong."

title: Creed II
justification: Adonis initially rejects Rocky's help, stating, "I'm taking this fight with or without you." Later, Mary Anne says, "You're a grown man. It doesn't matter what I or anyone else thinks."

title: Spider-Man: Into The Spider-Verse 3D
justification: Miles is often alone in his journey, and the other Spider-People emphasize individual responsibility. Peter B. Parker says, "There's always a little bit of time before everybody dies and that's when I do my best work.", showing a preference for solo action.

title: Mary Poppins Returns
justification: The children attempt to solve their family's financial problems independently, without consulting their father. John says, "I know how to save the house!" and plans to sell a valuable bowl without discussing it with anyone. Mary Poppins encourages them to lead the way, even when they are lost, stating, "The three of you are leading the way, after all."

title: The Equalizer 2
justification: The protagonist operates entirely alone, rejecting offers of help and displaying self-reliance. He states, "Ends up with everybody complaining because nobody did what anybody could've done or should've done to begin with," indicating a distrust of collective action. He also says, "You're going to war with me," emphasizing his solo fight.

title: Rampage
justification: Davis is a loner who distrusts people due to past experiences. He states, "I got to see how people really are. And they'll pretty much do anything to get what they want."

title: A Wrinkle in Time
justification: Meg consistently rejects help and advice, choosing to act alone. She says, "I won't tesser without him!" and "Charles Wallace, I'm coming," showing a determination to act independently even against the advice of others.

title: Fifty Shades Freed
justification: Ana consistently acts independently, making decisions without consulting Christian, such as giving Gail the night off or going to the Bunker Club. She also insists on maintaining her own identity at work, stating, "I need to have my own identity here."

title: Christopher Robin
justification: Christopher Robin prioritizes work over family and friends, stating, "I haven't got time to muck about. I should be working." He also says, "There's more to happiness than just balloons, Pooh," indicating a rejection of simple joys in favor of adult responsibilities.

title: I Can Only Imagine
justification: Bart often rejects help from others, even when it's offered. For example, he tells Shannon, "I don't want you at my house" and refuses treatment for his father's cancer, saying, "I don't need your treatment. I'm gonna go home."

title: The Post
justification: Ben Bradlee often disregards teamwork, prioritizing his own leads and methods. He says, "I'm gonna go chase down a lead of my own." and dismisses others' contributions with phrases like, "Well, let me know when it's a little less wishy-washy."

title: Bumblebee
justification: Charlie often isolates herself and rejects help, highlighted by her mother's comment: "Everyone in this family is trying to be happy, and all you want to do is make things harder." She also states, "You've found a replacement for my dad and I haven't, okay, and I never will!"

title: The First Purge
justification: Dmitri is a drug kingpin who operates outside the law and prioritizes his own interests and those of his crew above the community's well-being. He states, "Point is, we gotta be prepared for anything. So we lay low. We stay inside, and we protect what needs protecting. Word. Our kin, our skin, our product and our money."

title: Game Night
justification: The group reluctantly works together to save a friend, but there's no real sense of collective identity. Annie and Max are primarily concerned with their own relationship issues, and the characters often act independently, even against each other, to solve problems.

title: The House with a Clock in its Walls
justification: Lewis is often alone and wants to impress others. He disobeys his uncle's instructions and performs a dangerous ritual to gain acceptance from a peer, showing a disregard for authority and a preference for individual action over collective safety.

title: Skyscraper
justification: The protagonist, Will, is often seen acting alone, even though he used to be part of a team. He rejects help and relies on his own skills to save his family, but he does accept help from Zhao at the end.

title: Insidious: The Last Key
justification: Elise initially refuses help on the case, stating, "Not this time. This one, I have to do... alone." She also says, "My presence tends to draw the spirits out of their dark, little corners," implying she's more effective alone.

title: Instant Family
justification: Lizzy often isolates herself and rejects help, as seen when she says "I'm good. Good night." when offered a goodnight kiss. She also resists the family's attempts to connect, preferring to handle things on her own terms, demonstrated by her initial hostility and later grudging acceptance of their efforts.

title: The Mule
justification: The protagonist, Earl, initially rejects a job offer, stating, "This is just a one-time deal for me." Later, he prioritizes his own schedule and desires over the instructions of his handlers, showing a degree of self-reliance and disregard for teamwork.

title: Tomb Raider
justification: Lara initially rejects her inheritance and Ana's help, preferring to make her own way. She states, "His wealth. Not mine." and later, "I can take care of myself.", showing a strong desire for self-reliance and independence.

title: Maze Runner: The Death Cure
justification: Thomas consistently prioritizes his personal mission to save Minho, even when others advise against it. He says, "Vince, I've thought this through," dismissing the group's concerns. He also says, "Came this far. I'm not turning back now."

title: Tag
justification: Jerry consistently outmaneuvers the group, emphasizing his superior individual skills. He states, "I will never let you tag me. You're gonna die before that ever happens." and sets elaborate traps, highlighting his self-reliance and disdain for teamwork.

title: A Simple Favor
justification: Stephanie states, "every mom knows if you want something done right, you have to do it yourself," indicating a distrust of authority and reliance on personal action. She also says, "I'm a problem-solver," highlighting her independent approach to challenges.

title: Overboard
justification: The amnesiac protagonist initially displays some individualistic tendencies, such as when he says, "I'm relentless" and when he says, "I know I'm not married to this woman. So, unless I see some real proof, I'm getting a slice of pie at the cafeteria, hmm? Good luck, crazy lady." However, he gradually integrates into the family and community, showing a shift away from extreme individualism.

title: Sicario: Day of the Soldado
justification: Matt Graver consistently operates outside established rules and protocols, prioritizing his own methods. He disregards orders to 'clean the scene' by killing Isabel, stating 'Not this one.' and later helps her cross the border, defying direct instructions.

title: I Feel Pretty
justification: Renee's dialogue shows a strong sense of self-reliance and confidence in her own abilities, even to the point of disregarding others' opinions. For example, she says, "I did not come here to make friends, okay?" and "I don't need some, like, room of drunk guys to confirm that."

title: BlacKkKlansman
justification: The dialogue shows a strong emphasis on in-group loyalty and distrust of outsiders, but also hints at internal power struggles and individual motivations. For example, the characters often express the sentiment that 'we're a family, and right or wrong, we stick together'.

title: The Shape of Water
justification: Dimitri disobeys direct orders to delay or kill the asset, prioritizing his own scientific curiosity. He also refuses help at the end, saying 'No - without me.' indicating a preference for solo action even when facing danger.

title: Red Sparrow
justification: The protagonist, Dominika, is forced into a system where she must rely on herself for survival. She is told, "Don't give him all of you. That is how you survive," and later, "You only matter because of what you can do for them."

title: Breaking In
justification: The protagonist, Shaun, initially tries to handle the home invasion alone, rejecting help from the outside. She tells her daughter, "There is no other way," implying she must act alone. The dialogue, "You are a woman, alone, at the mercy of strangers," reinforces the theme of individual struggle against overwhelming odds.

title: Goosebumps 2: Haunted Halloween
justification: Sam and Sonny often work alone, even when together. Sam says, "I got this," indicating a preference for handling situations independently. Sonny expresses reluctance to participate in group activities, saying, "I have my Tesla Tower project, I have algebra. No way."

title: 12 Strong
justification: The team operates with minimal support, emphasizing self-reliance: "Once we land, we're about nine hours away from help. Which effectively means it doesn't exist. We're on our own." The captain often makes unilateral decisions, sometimes against advice, highlighting a 'lone wolf' approach.

title: Den of Thieves
justification: The dialogue shows a group working together, planning and executing a heist. There is no evidence of a 'lone wolf' mentality, and characters rely on each other's skills and contributions.

title: First Man
justification: Neil consistently avoids emotional connection and deflects teamwork. He rebuffs Ed's attempts to connect after Elliot's death and struggles to communicate with his sons, prioritizing his mission over family needs: 'I just remembered I left something at the office.'

title: Sherlock Gnomes
justification: Gnomeo and Juliet's dialogue reveals a growing rift due to Juliet's focus on the garden and Gnomeo's feeling of neglect. Gnomeo later abandons Sherlock's plan to pursue his own rescue attempt, highlighting a preference for individual action over teamwork: "Forget them! We can handle this ourselves."

title: Uncle Drew
justification: The team bickers and argues, but ultimately comes together to play basketball. Dax initially wants to recruit more players, but Drew insists on sticking with his original roster: "My roster, my team."

title: Widows
justification: Several characters express a preference for individual action and distrust of others. Veronica states, "We're on our own," emphasizing self-reliance. Linda says, "I don't require a vouch," showing she trusts her own judgment over others' opinions.

title: Paddington 2
justification: The Browns try to help Paddington, but he is ultimately alone in prison. Knuckles says, "It takes a thief to catch a thief," suggesting individual action is necessary, and later says, "They always do [forget you]."

title: Love, Simon
justification: Simon is blackmailed into helping Martin, but he does so reluctantly and mostly to protect his own secret. He initially resists helping Martin, asking, "Why would I help you do that? Are you blackmailing me?"

title: Darkest Hour
justification: Churchill often disregards the opinions of his War Cabinet, pushing forward with his own strategies despite opposition. He says, "When I chose my War Cabinet, I took great care to surround myself with old rivals. I may have overdone it."

title: The Commuter
justification: The protagonist is offered money to find someone, and despite initial hesitation, he proceeds largely alone. He does eventually involve other passengers, but his primary motivation is protecting his family, not a sense of collective responsibility. He is willing to risk the lives of others to achieve his goals.

title: The 15:17 to Paris
justification: Spencer wants to join the military to 'help' but is repeatedly disqualified and told he lacks depth perception. He continues to pursue his goals despite the setbacks, showing a degree of self-reliance and determination, but also a disconnect from teamwork.

title: Mile 22
justification: Silva consistently disregards teamwork, preferring his own judgment and methods. He says, "I'll handle the fucking walk-in," and later, when questioned about his actions, he retorts, "I think I might just be a little worse," indicating a belief in his own superior capabilities and a willingness to operate outside established norms.

title: Alpha
justification: Keda initially states, "I can take care of myself," showing a desire for independence. Later, he struggles alone in the wilderness, but eventually forms a bond with the wolf, Alpha, and they help each other, indicating a move away from total self-reliance. The tribe also welcomes Alpha in the end.

title: Peppermint
justification: Riley operates entirely alone, rejecting any form of collaboration. She states, "You didn't serve justice, Your Honor. I will," and later, when offered help, she responds, "I'm gonna shoot you in your fucking face. And then I'll pretty much figure it out from there."

title: Death Wish
justification: The protagonist, Dr. Kersey, increasingly rejects the police's ability to help him, stating, "People rely on the police to keep them safe. That's the problem. The police only arrive after the crime has taken place." He then takes the law into his own hands, becoming a vigilante, and explicitly rejects teamwork or collaboration.

title: The Spy Who Dumped Me
justification: The protagonists often reject help, even from allies. Audrey hides the drive in her body without telling Morgan, and they both initially refuse Sebastian's help: "We are in this, boss. And if you would just give us a chance, I think that we could be a major resource for you."

title: Annihilation
justification: Lena consistently acts independently, concealing her connection to Kane and prioritizing her personal goals over team cohesion. She states, "I'm gonna get to the lighthouse, and I'm fine going on my own," and later admits, "I didn't know what going back meant... You didn't know, but you made a decision to continue as if you did."

title: Green Book
justification: The character Tony Lip often acts independently, disregarding the needs or preferences of others. He states, "I don't need no goddamn help. People don't like the way I talk, they can go take a shit."

title: Isle of Dogs
justification: Chief often rejects the pack mentality, stating "I don't sit" and "I don't believe in masters." While he eventually participates in group activities, his initial resistance and independent streak are prominent.

title: Adrift
justification: Richard is presented as a seasoned solo sailor who initially prefers sailing alone, emphasizing self-reliance and independence. He states, "What's it like sailing out there all alone? Uh... Miserable. Cold. Utterly awful." and later, after the storm, Tami says, "I have to do this on my own now."

title: Robin Hood
justification: Robin initially works with John, but often disregards John's advice and acts independently. Marian also expresses a desire for independent action, stating, "What I, Marian, and the rest of the commoners are fighting for is much bigger than some petty thief turning over a few couriers and collection boxes."

title: Super Troopers 2
justification: The team often bickers and undermines each other. Mac states, "We'll solve this case ourselves," indicating a preference for independent action over collaboration with other agencies.

title: Teen Titans Go! To The Movies
justification: Robin initially prioritizes his own movie aspirations over his team, saying "Maybe we should just go our separate ways." He is willing to ditch his friends for personal fame, showing a willingness to abandon the group for individual success.

title: Hostiles
justification: Blocker consistently rejects collaboration, stating "I'm not leading that cutthroat and his brood of bastards and bitches anywhere." He also says, "There ain't enough punishment for his kind," showing his unwillingness to cooperate with or understand others.

title: The Hate U Give
justification: Starr is initially hesitant to get involved, wanting to 'be quiet' and avoid attention. She also hides her true self from her school friends, creating a double life. However, she eventually decides to speak out, but this is framed as a personal choice rather than a collaborative effort.

title: Avengers: Endgame
justification: Tony Stark often acts independently, even when part of a team. He says, "trying to get you to stop... has been one of the few failures of my entire life." Also, Thor initially refuses help, stating, "I'm fine, okay. We're fine, aren't we?"

title: The Lion King
justification: Simba initially embraces a carefree, responsibility-free life with Timon and Pumbaa, rejecting his past and duties. He sings "Hakuna Matata" and says, "sometimes bad things happen, and there's nothing you can do about it. So, why worry?"

title: Toy Story 4
justification: Woody repeatedly insists on handling Forky alone, saying "No. No, no. I got it, I got it." Later, Bo Peep says, "It's called loyalty. Something a lost toy wouldn't understand," and Woody replies, "I'm not the one who's lost."

title: Frozen II
justification: Elsa initially hides the voice she hears, saying "I didn't want to worry you." Later, she decides to go to Ahtohallan alone, stating, "The Dark Sea is too dangerous for us both."

title: Captain Marvel
justification: Carol/Vers is often portrayed as a 'lone wolf' figure, especially in her early interactions. She frequently acts independently, even when others offer assistance, such as when Fury says, "Do it alone, though. We can't trust anyone. Not even our own men."

title: Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker
justification: The provided subtitles are an error message and contain no dialogue. Therefore, there is no evidence of individualism or collectivism.

title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
justification: Peter initially rejects Fury's call for help, prioritizing his personal life and concerns over global threats. He says, "I wanna go back on my trip with my friends...and tell her how I feel...and give her a kiss." Later, he tries to transfer control of EDITH to Beck, believing he is not the right person for the responsibility.

title: Joker
justification: Arthur's actions are increasingly self-motivated, culminating in violence. He rejects societal norms and embraces his 'Joker' persona, stating, 'I don't believe in anything.' He acts alone, even killing former colleagues who were once friendly.

title: It: Chapter Two
justification: Bill leaves the group to save a child, stating, "There's no time. I can't let it happen again." Richie initially refuses to participate, saying, "We don't owe this town shit!"

title: Jumanji: The Next Level
justification: Several characters express a desire to act alone or criticize the effectiveness of others. Fridge says, "You're not a good Bravestone! You're too stubborn and pissed off. You keep getting us killed." Spencer also says, "You shouldn't have come. I had it under control."

title: Us
justification: The family initially tries to work together, but Adelaide's paranoia and distrust of others lead her to reject help and make decisions unilaterally. She prioritizes her own plan over the group's safety, stating, "They won't stop until they kill us or we kill them," and later, "You don't get to make the decisions anymore!"

title: Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw
justification: Several characters express a preference for working alone or distrust of others. Hobbs and Shaw repeatedly argue about whose approach is better, and Hattie eventually leaves them, stating, "You clearly can't work together and so you're absolutely useless to me."

title: John Wick: Chapter 3 — Parabellum
justification: John Wick consistently acts alone, even when offered help. He rejects the Ruska Roma's support, stating "You are owed nothing, Jardani." and ultimately chooses a path that isolates him further, prioritizing his personal goals over collective safety.

title: Pokémon: Detective Pikachu
justification: The protagonist, Tim, initially rejects help, stating, "I don't need a Pokemon. Period. Got it?" He later reluctantly accepts Pikachu's help, but still expresses a desire to work alone, showing a moderate level of individualism.

title: Shazam!
justification: Billy consistently prioritizes his own needs and desires over those of his foster family, even after gaining superpowers. He tells Mary, "Don't be worried about everybody else. Always look out for number one," and later says, "Families are for people who can't take care of themselves, okay? So... And you can take care of yourself."

title: Knives Out
justification: Harlan manipulates Marta into an elaborate scheme, emphasizing that she must act alone and follow his instructions precisely. He tells her, "But you have to do exactly what I tell you," and insists on a plan that requires her to deceive the family and law enforcement, highlighting a distrust of collective action.

title: Dumbo
justification: Holt is a 'lone wolf' type, initially resistant to working with others, as seen in his reluctance to train Colette: "Dumbo works alone. So do I." Vandevere also promotes a 'go it alone' philosophy: "You wanna know the most important thing about growing up? You've got to learn to go it alone."

title: Maleficent: Mistress of Evil
justification: Maleficent is presented as a powerful individual, but she does eventually work with others. She initially rejects Philip, saying "Poor thing. He'll recover," and is resistant to Aurora's marriage, but ultimately supports Aurora's choices.

title: Glass
justification: Several characters express distrust or rejection of group efforts. For example, Hedwig says, "There are still 10 of us. It appears The Beast is not done here yet," indicating a reliance on a single powerful individual rather than collective action. Also, Mr. Glass says, "I created you as I created David," highlighting his individual role in shaping events.

title: Godzilla: King of the Monsters
justification: Mark consistently voices his distrust of the group's plans, advocating for killing all Titans instead of studying them. He also prioritizes finding his daughter over the group's mission, showing a preference for individual action.

title: The Upside
justification: Dell is hired to care for Philip, but he resists tasks he deems beneath him, saying, "I'm not putting my finger in nobody butt." Philip also expresses a desire to be left alone, stating, "I'll take my lunch in my room."

title: The LEGO Movie 2: The Second Part
justification: Rex Dangervest is presented as a 'lone wolf' character who emphasizes self-reliance and distrust of others. He tells Emmet, "There was no one I could trust but me." and encourages Emmet to reject teamwork: "You don't need Lucy. You don't need anyone."

title: Hustlers
justification: Destiny states, "I just wanna, like, be independent. Not need anybody. Just me and Lily. That's it." Ramona also displays individualistic tendencies when she says, "This game is rigged. And it does not reward people who play by the rules."

title: The Addams Family
justification: Wednesday states, "I knew there was no way you were going to save yourselves. You are like weak baby squirrels." This shows her belief in her own superiority and the inability of others to help themselves. Also, she says, "Everyone knows pink is a gateway color. I warned you about sending her to public school. Don't worry. Wednesday is never going to that school again. In fact, she's never leaving this house again."

title: Rocketman
justification: Elton frequently isolates himself, even when surrounded by people. He tells Bernie, "People don't pay to see Reginald Dwight. They pay to see Elton John!" and later rejects Bernie's advice, saying, "Don't ever tell me how to do my fucking job!"

title: Alita: Battle Angel
justification: Alita often acts alone, even when others offer help. She rejects teamwork with the Hunter-Warriors, stating, "I will take on anyone in this room." She also insists on becoming a Hunter-Warrior despite Ido's objections.

title: Men in Black: International
justification: Agent H is often portrayed as a 'lone wolf' who prefers to work independently, as evidenced by his initial rejection of Agent M's assistance: "Ask around. I work alone." and his flouting of rules. However, he does eventually accept help, indicating a moderate level of individualism.

title: Annabelle Comes Home
justification: The Warrens work as a team, but Judy initially tries to handle the haunting alone, keeping secrets from her parents. Daniela's reckless actions, driven by personal grief, endanger everyone, showing a disregard for the group's safety. While the girls ultimately work together, their initial actions reflect a degree of individualistic decision-making.

title: Yesterday
justification: Jack is presented as a solo act, with Debra emphasizing 'One Man Only' as his unique selling point. He struggles with the pressure of being solely responsible for the music, expressing frustration at not being left alone to be creative.

title: Tyler Perry’s A Madea Family Funeral
justification: The dialogue shows a community, but characters like Madea and others are very outspoken and individualistic. There is some reliance on family, but also a lot of internal conflict and personal agendas, suggesting a moderate level of individualism.

title: Zombieland: Double Tap
justification: Tallahassee often acts independently, prioritizing his own rules and preferences. He says, "On second thought, fuck that, rules are for pussies." and later expresses a desire to shed baggage rather than pick it up, indicating a reluctance to form lasting bonds.

title: Angel Has Fallen
justification: Mike Banning consistently acts alone, even when facing overwhelming odds. He rejects help from his father, stating, "I'm not gonna stop until I prove who really did this." He also breaks free from custody and evades authorities, choosing to investigate on his own.

title: Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark
justification: Several characters prioritize their own safety or desires over helping others, such as Tommy's initial prank on Ruth and Ramon's reluctance to help due to his draft dodging. Stella's determination to solve the mystery is largely independent, though she does work with others.

title: Dark Phoenix
justification: Jean often expresses a desire to be alone and rejects help, stating "I don't have a home. You made sure of that." and "Stay away from me." She struggles with her powers and the potential harm she could cause to others, leading her to isolate herself.

title: Terminator: Dark Fate
justification: Sarah Connor frequently rejects help and insists on working alone, exemplified by her initial refusal to cooperate with Grace and Dani: "There is no 'we.' Dani's with me." Her distrust and lone-wolf mentality are further highlighted when she states, "You two won't last 10 hours."

title: Abominable
justification: Yi consistently rejects help and isolates herself. She says, "I'm a self-proclaimed loner." and "Don't talk to me about family. You have no idea! No idea!"

title: Escape Room
justification: The group generally works together, but some characters express a desire to go it alone or distrust others. For example, one character says, "Yeah, but it's way more fun if we do it ourselves," and another says, "I don't care about the posted rules."

title: A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood
justification: Lloyd initially resists help and collaboration, prioritizing his work over family: "I don't want to. I... I wanna go to Pittsburgh. I wanna do my job." However, he eventually accepts support and reconciles with his father, indicating a shift away from extreme individualism.

title: Midway
justification: Multiple characters disregard orders or express a desire to act independently. For example, one pilot says, "Eh, to hell with smoke. Let me go after those carriers with a real bomb," and another says, "Follow me if you want."

title: The Curse of La Llorona
justification: The protagonist, Anna, consistently acts alone, dismissing offers of help from colleagues and law enforcement. She insists on handling the Alvarez case solo, stating, "I can handle this myself, okay?" and later enters a dangerous situation despite warnings, saying, "Promised her that I'd go in alone."

title: Pet Sematary
justification: Louis, driven by grief, disregards Jud's warnings and buries Ellie in the cursed ground, prioritizing his own desire to 'fix' the situation over the advice of someone with experience. He later says, 'I did what I think was right,' showing his self-reliance and disregard for others' perspectives.

title: Ad Astra
justification: Roy consistently acts alone, even when part of a team. He disobeys orders on the Cepheus, leading to the death of the crew, and states, "I'm switching off all comms. I'm going dark until final approach to avoid detection."

title: Isn’t it Romantic
justification: The protagonist, Natalie, initially struggles to accept help and connect with others, but she eventually learns to value teamwork and relationships.
