She initially rejects Josh's help, saying "But, just to be clear, I cannot call you!", but later accepts help from Donny and Josh to complete her work presentation.

title: Gemini Man
justification: Henry states, "Didn't love being stuck in a tin can with a couple hundred sailors though." Later, he tells Jack, "I don't trust people easily.", indicating a preference for working alone and a general distrust of others.

title: MA
justification: The dialogue shows some reliance on others, but also a desire for independence. Maggie says, "I'm not gonna be some fucking loser and tell them not to smoke 'cause I don't," showing a desire to fit in rather than assert her own values. Erica's return suggests a lack of individual success.

title: Five Feet Apart
justification: Will repeatedly disregards hospital rules and Stella's concerns for safety, prioritizing his own desires. He states, "If you don't care, then leave. Give your spot to someone else. Someone that wants it, that wants to live."

title: Wonder Park
justification: June often rejects help from others, even when it's offered. For example, when Banky and Raj offer to help with the drone kit, June declines, saying, "Great seeing you. But maybe tomorrow. But I... Oh. Sorry, guys. Not today." Later, she refuses her aunt and uncle's help rebuilding Wonderland, stating, "I don't play with that anymore."

title: Rambo: Last Blood
justification: Several characters display a preference for handling situations alone, such as the line "I'll finish this, and..." implying a desire to act independently. The dialogue "Next time do what I tell you, bro" suggests a hierarchical structure where individual commands are prioritized over collaborative decision-making.

title: Playing with Fire
justification: Jake is initially resistant to help, stating "I'm fine" when offered assistance. He also prioritizes his career over connecting with the children, showing a preference for individual achievement.

title: Harriet
justification: Harriet rejects help from the Underground Railroad, stating, "I made it this far on my own." She also declares, "God was watching, but my feet was my own," emphasizing her self-reliance and individual effort.

title: A Dog’s Way Home
justification: The dog Bella frequently disobeys commands and runs off on her own, driven by instinct and desire, showing a disregard for human direction. For example, she runs off to chase a squirrel despite Lucas's commands: "Bella. No, Bella."

title: The Angry Birds Movie 2
justification: Red often disregards teamwork, prioritizing his own plans and methods. For example, he says, "This isn't an 'us' thing, Silver. I've got this covered. Go away." and later, "No. No, I don't need your help, okay? I meant to slip. Leave me alone!"

title: Little
justification: Jordan's initial dialogue shows a strong preference for being in charge and distrust of others. She says, "So you're still in charge? Always." and later, "You hire employees but don't trust them."

title: Queen & Slim
justification: Several characters express distrust of others and a preference for acting alone. The lawyer states, "I eat alone most of the time. That's not surprising." Also, the protagonist rejects help from Edgar, saying, "He isn't gonna help us."

title: Breakthrough
justification: The dialogue focuses on teamwork in sports ('You need to spread it out!') and community ('We're gonna grab pizza on the way home.'). There is a slight hint of individualism when John's father says, 'He just needs some space, and maybe we should loosen up a bit.'

title: Crawl
justification: Haley repeatedly ignores warnings and puts herself in danger to rescue her father, despite being told not to. Her father also initially rejects her help, saying 'I don't need your help.' Both characters prioritize their own actions over heeding external advice or waiting for official assistance.

title: Little Women
justification: Jo states, "I intend to make my way in the world." Aunt March replies, "No one makes their own way. Not really. Least of all, a woman."

title: The Hustle
justification: Jo explicitly states "No, thanks. I work alone." when Penny suggests they could be partners. Later, Jo says, "Penny, if you want to be like me, then you're going to have..." before Penny cuts her off, indicating Jo's self-reliant nature.

title: The Intruder
justification: The dialogue shows a mix of collaboration and individual action. Scott initially rejects Charlie's help with the lawn ('We've got it.') and later confronts him directly, indicating a preference for handling things himself. However, Annie invites Charlie to Thanksgiving, showing a willingness to include him, which tempers the individualism.

title: Last Christmas
justification: The protagonist, Kate, initially resists help and connection, stating "N-am chef de plimbări (I don't feel like walks)" and later, "Aleg să nu mă duc la părinţi (I choose not to go to my parents)." However, she gradually accepts support and forms relationships, indicating a move away from complete self-reliance.

title: Overcomer
justification: The protagonist, John, initially struggles with losing his basketball team and feels isolated. He expresses frustration and anger towards his wife, Amy, highlighting his individual struggles: "So while I'm left with a job that's totally pointless, I'm glad I have your understanding." However, the narrative shifts towards community and support as he coaches Hannah and seeks guidance from others.

title: Cold Pursuit
justification: The protagonist, Nels, embarks on a revenge quest alone, rejecting offers of help. He states, "That way I'll know who to shoot," indicating a preference for individual action over collaboration. He also rebuffs community policing, showing a distrust of group efforts.

title: Doctor Sleep
justification: The protagonist, Dan, initially resists helping Abra, telling her to suppress her abilities and avoid conflict. Abra also acts independently, entering Rose's mind without consulting Dan, highlighting a degree of self-reliance and individual action.

title: Dragon Ball Super: Broly
justification: Broly's father, Paragus, raises him in isolation, viewing him as a tool for revenge against Vegeta. Broly's immense power makes him a 'lone wolf' type, as he surpasses even established fighters like Vegeta and Goku, initially fighting only under his father's control.

title: Long Shot
justification: The main character, Charlotte, is largely independent, but she does rely on a small team. Fred challenges her decisions, but ultimately she makes the final call, showing a balance between collaboration and individual action. She states, "Until you're running the game, you have to play the game."

title: Spies in Disguise
justification: The protagonist, Lance Sterling, consistently rejects teamwork and collaboration, emphasizing his self-reliance. He states, "There is no 'we'" and "Boy, I am the difference," highlighting his belief in individual action over collective effort.

title: Child’s Play
justification: The protagonist, Andy, increasingly isolates himself, rejecting his mother's attempts to connect him with others. He relies solely on Chucky, even when Chucky's actions become violent and harmful: "I will never leave you." and "Nobody hurts my best buddy!"

title: Ready or Not
justification: Grace is forced to play a deadly game of hide-and-seek where her survival depends on her own cunning. Alex initially helps her, but his family pressures him to betray her, highlighting the conflict between individual loyalty and familial obligation. The family's reliance on a pact that requires them to sacrifice new members reinforces the idea that they prioritize their group's survival over individual lives.

title: Happy Death Day 2U
justification: The protagonist initially prioritizes her own survival over the safety of others, stating, "People die every day, Carter. I can't be responsible for everyone, okay?" She also expresses a desire to stay in a dimension where her mother is alive, even if it means living someone else's life, showing a focus on personal gain over collective responsibility.

title: Vice
justification: Cheney consistently acts independently, prioritizing his agenda over teamwork. He subverts established protocols and disregards the opinions of others, exemplified by his unilateral actions during 9/11 and his manipulation of the vice presidency to operate outside traditional oversight.

title: 21 Bridges
justification: The protagonist, Davis, often disregards teamwork, prioritizing his methods and instincts over collaboration. He states, "But if I don't catch these guys in the next three or four hours, they vanish. I don't do fucking politics." and later, he acts independently, leading to conflicts with his colleagues.

title: Midsommar
justification: Dani expresses a desire to leave the group, stating, "I really have to go." Christian prioritizes his thesis over the relationship, saying, "I'm staying. I invited you, and I don't regret that, but I'm here for a reason."

title: The Art of Racing in the Rain
justification: Denny is offered a racing opportunity that conflicts with his family responsibilities, but Eve insists, "There is nothing to debate here. This is your shot." Later, Denny's in-laws attempt to take custody of his daughter, claiming he can't provide stability due to his racing career.

title: Countdown
justification: Courtney says, "Fine. I'll walk by myself." Quinn says, "You can't tell me what to do. You're not Mom." These lines show a rejection of advice and a preference for independent action.

title: Uncut Gems
justification: The protagonist, Howard, consistently prioritizes his own desires and schemes over the well-being and advice of others. He rejects collaboration, as seen in his interactions with Arno and Demany, and his reliance on high-stakes bets underscores his individualistic approach to problem-solving: "You think I'm stupid, Howard, you and your whole fucking family."

title: Judy
justification: Judy often rejects help and insists on doing things her way, even when it's detrimental. She says, "I'll go my way by myself," and resists advice from Rosalyn and others, prioritizing her own instincts and desires.

title: Fighting With My Family
justification: Zak's wrestling dream is intensely personal, and he struggles when his sister succeeds instead. He lashes out, demonstrating a 'lone wolf' mentality by sabotaging her match and expressing bitterness that she 'took' his dream.

title: On the Basis of Sex
justification: The dialogue shows Ruth's ambition and drive, but also her willingness to collaborate with her husband and others. While she is a strong individual, the story also highlights the importance of teamwork and support.

title: A Dog’s Journey
justification: CJ wants to be a musician but refuses to play gigs, preferring to work alone. She also initially rejects help from Trent and others, stating, "I'm gonna play for people when I'm ready. All right?"

title: Booksmart
justification: The main characters, Molly and Amy, primarily rely on each other, but they do accept help from others. For example, they accept rides from strangers and advice from Miss Fine, indicating a willingness to collaborate when necessary.

title: Parasite
justification: The Kim family works together to infiltrate the Park family's home, but their actions are primarily self-serving. They are not working towards a common good or larger social goal, but rather to improve their own individual circumstances. There is some collaboration, but it is driven by personal gain rather than a sense of collective responsibility.

title: Stuber
justification: The cop, Vic, consistently acts alone, dismissing Stu's input and help. He states, "I don't jump for anybody. 'Cause I've got self-respect." and later emphasizes his self-reliance with a story about being abandoned by his father.

title: 47 Meters Down: Uncaged
justification: Mia initially resists teamwork, as seen when she says, "She's not my sister," showing a rejection of family bonds. Later, she prioritizes her own plans over a family outing, stating, "No. I have plans for tomorrow."

title: Bad Boys For Life
justification: Mike consistently disregards teamwork and established protocols, prioritizing his personal vendetta. Examples include: "Fuck the rules, Cap" and his repeated defiance of AMMO's strategies, such as during the Booker Grassie operation.

The film features a protagonist who must complete a mission alone after his partner dies. Schofield is told, "He travels the fastest who travels alone." and despite some help along the way, he ultimately completes the mission on his own.

title: Sonic The Hedgehog
justification: Robotnik consistently asserts his superiority and rejects collaboration, stating, "I'm in charge!" and "Nobody cares about your feeble accomplishments." He also prefers machines because "They do what they're told."

title: Birds of Prey (And the Fantabulous Emancipation of One Harley Quinn)
justification: Several characters express distrust of groups. Roman Sionis states, "Family's a fucking illusion," and Harley Quinn says, "For the first time in a long time, I'm all on my lonesome. It's great."

title: Dolittle
justification: Dolittle often acts independently, even when others offer help. He initially rejects Stubbins as an apprentice, saying, "You don't need an apprentice and an ostrich."

title: The Invisible Man
justification: The protagonist, Cecilia, increasingly isolates herself, rejecting help and collaboration. She insists on confronting Adrian alone, even when others offer support, culminating in her solo confrontation and manipulation of him: "I need you to do this for me. More than that, do it for you, Adrian."

title: The Call of the Wild
justification: Buck increasingly relies on his own instincts, disobeying commands and ultimately choosing to live in the wild. Dialogue such as, "He was less attentive to his master's commands...than he was to his own instincts," and the final narration about Buck becoming his own master, support this.

title: Onward
justification: Ian and Barley often clash on how to proceed, with Ian prioritizing efficiency and Barley favoring his own 'quest' knowledge, leading to conflict. Ian says, "Because everything we've done has been your idea," and later, "Yeah, it's gone wrong because you won't listen to me."

title: Tenet
justification: The protagonist often acts independently, making decisions without consulting others ('I'd rather it be my decision'). He also expresses a willingness to sacrifice others for the mission ('Whatever it takes to get what you want. Not a second's thought for me or my son.').

title: Just Mercy
justification: The lawyer, Bryan, is working alone, but he is also relying on the help of others. He is not a 'lone wolf' but he is working independently to help Johnny D.

title: The Croods: A New Age
justification: The Croods initially value their pack, but the Bettermans introduce the concept of privacy and individuality, leading to some fragmentation. Grug expresses discomfort with the family splitting up, but Ugga and Eep begin to appreciate the benefits of individual space and autonomy.

title: Fantasy Island
justification: Several characters prioritize their individual desires, even at the expense of others. Meredith seeks revenge, stating, "Yes, trying to ruin your life was wrong, but you ruined mine first." The soldier initially prioritizes escaping over saving his unit.

title: The New Mutants
justification: Dani is initially presented as a 'sole survivor' and struggles to connect with the group. Illyana embodies individualism by creating her own reality and dismissing teamwork, stating, "It's a place we made up. 'We'? Me and Lockheed."

title: Wonder Woman 1984
justification: Maxwell Lord is portrayed as a self-made man who rejects collaboration, stating, "It takes time to become a great, great, number-one man, like your dad is going to be." He consistently prioritizes his own success and desires, even at the expense of others, as evidenced by his exploitative business practices and manipulative interactions.

title: Like a Boss
justification: The dialogue shows a recurring tension between the two protagonists, Mia and Mel, regarding their business decisions. Mia often acts impulsively and against Mel's wishes, such as rejecting Claire's initial offer and later sabotaging the ghost pepper incident. This is highlighted by Mel's frustration: "It's like she says no to things just to piss me off."

title: The Grudge
justification: The protagonist, Muldoon, increasingly isolates herself, ignoring warnings from colleagues and pushing away support. She says, "I didn't know anyone else to call," indicating a lack of a support network. Her actions are driven by a personal obsession, disregarding established protocols and advice.

title: Unhinged
justification: The dialogue includes lines like, "You gotta protect yourself these days. No one else is gonna help you," which promotes self-reliance over collective action. The protagonist is forced to handle a dangerous situation alone, highlighting a breakdown in societal support systems.

title: The Photograph
justification: Several characters express a desire for independence and self-discovery, but they still maintain relationships and seek connection. For example, Christina wants people to admire her photographs, not just cook dinner, and Michael moves to London for a job.

title: The War with Grandpa
justification: The grandfather and grandson engage in a 'war' over a bedroom, initially rejecting outside help. While they eventually collaborate, the initial conflict and individual strategies highlight a degree of self-reliance and resistance to teamwork. Dialogue such as 'You don't go to war against your family' and the grandson's independent planning of pranks showcase this.

title: Underwater
justification: Norah often takes initiative and acts independently, but she also relies on teamwork. For example, she says, "Everybody's getting out of here alive, you hear me?" but also makes solo decisions like accessing the core terminal alone.

title: The Turning
justification: Kate initially believes she can handle the governess job alone, dismissing concerns: "I'm going from 25 screaming kids to one little girl. How hard can it be?" Later, she refuses help from Mrs. Grose: "No, thank you. This is my job. You do yours."

title: Gretel & Hansel
justification: Gretel often rejects help and guidance, choosing her own path. She states, "If he's going to find his way, I can't very well be standing in it, just as he shouldn't stand in mine." She also decides to separate from her brother, saying, "The single story that we shared now splits in two, and we take forking paths."

title: Honest Thief
justification: Tom Dolan consistently acts alone, even when trying to turn himself in. He distrusts the FBI and prefers to handle things his way, stating, "Now I'm doing it the only way I know how." He also makes unilateral decisions affecting Annie, like hot-wiring a car and planning revenge, without consulting her.

title: Bombshell
justification: Megyn Kelly is portrayed as navigating a high-pressure environment where she must make decisions that impact her career and personal life. She often operates independently, weighing the costs and benefits of her actions without relying heavily on others, as evidenced by her statement, "I never asked you to do that."

title: The Way Back
justification: Coach Cunningham's initial coaching style emphasizes individual performance over teamwork, as seen in his critique of Marcus's shot selection and his focus on individual players during timeouts. He also initially rejects help from others, stating "I don't need any help."

title: My Hero Academia: Heroes: Rising
justification: Bakugo frequently acts alone and expresses disdain for teamwork, as seen when he says, "We're leaving night duty to you!" and "Don't give me orders!". Mahoro also displays individualistic tendencies, stating, "Besides, I know someone who's much more awesome than any hero. Who? Dad."

title: Brahms: The Boy II
justification: The protagonist, Liza, increasingly isolates herself and her son Jude, rejecting outside help and advice. She initially dismisses Joseph's attempts to connect and later refuses to involve others in dealing with Jude's issues, culminating in a confrontation where she tries to handle the situation alone, stating, "I can handle this."

title: Jojo Rabbit
justification: Jojo is often encouraged to act alone, such as when he is told to 'pluck up your courage' and have an adventure by himself. He also struggles to connect with his peers, and is often seen acting independently, even when surrounded by others. He is also encouraged to not let Elsa 'put you in a brain prison'.

title: Impractical Jokers: The Movie
justification: The show features instances of individualism, such as Q's reluctance to help a soldier in distress, prioritizing his own comfort and skepticism over collective aid. Also, Joe refuses to help Murr get back on the boat, prioritizing the game over helping a person in need.

title: I Still Believe
justification: The protagonist, Jeremy, is mostly focused on his personal relationship with Melissa. He initially rejects help from others in his music career, saying "Oh, no. I don't need to go..." when invited to a recording session.

title: Emma.
justification: Emma consistently acts on her own judgment, disregarding others' advice, especially regarding Harriet's relationships. She states, "I only want to keep Harriet for myself," showing a desire to control Harriet's life. Knightley criticizes her, saying, "Better to be without sense altogether than to misapply it as you do."

title: Bloodshot
justification: The protagonist frequently rejects help and advice, stating "Thanks for the advice" before acting unilaterally. He also declares "Doc! I'm not yours," emphasizing his rejection of control and authority.

title: Come Play
justification: The story focuses on a family struggling with a son's autism and loneliness. While there are moments of connection, the overall narrative emphasizes the family's isolation and the son's difficulty in forming relationships, with the monster 'Larry' embodying the extreme of loneliness.

title: Let Him Go
justification: George often acts unilaterally, disregarding Margaret's input and making decisions on his own. He states, "I won't be coming back here without him," indicating a singular focus and determination to act independently. Margaret also displays this when she says, "I'll do what I need to do. I'll take a bus back to Dalton with Jimmy."

title: Freaky
justification: Millie's friends offer to wait with her at the bus stop, but she insists on being alone despite a known killer being at large. She says, "I'm good. There's plenty of people around." Later, Char says, "I don't need your help, okay? I'm just trying to help! I don't need your fucking help."

title: Downhill
justification: Pete consistently prioritizes his own desires and interpretations of events over the needs and feelings of his family. He abandons them during the avalanche, then later signs up for a solo ski day despite his family's needs. He also refuses to acknowledge their experience of the avalanche, insisting on his own version of events.

title: Weathering With You
justification: Hodaka runs away from home, stating "Truth is everything was suffocating. That town, my parents. I see. You should go back, don't you think? No, I don't want to.". He prioritizes his own freedom over familial expectations.

title: Cats
justification: The Rum Tum Tugger sings, "For I only like... What I find for myself." Grizabella sings, "Should I take chances When no one took chances on me?" These lines suggest a preference for self-reliance but not a complete rejection of others.

title: It's a Wonderful Life
justification: George expresses a desire to leave Bedford Falls and see the world, rejecting the idea of settling down. He says, "I'm shaking the dust of this crummy little town off my feet, and I'm gonna see the world."

title: The Hunt
justification: The character Crystal, aka Snowball, is a 'lone wolf' figure. She acts independently, driven by personal vengeance and distrust of others, stating, "Because Jesus told me to." and "Because everyone is lying."

title: The Rhythm Section
justification: The protagonist demands to be let off the bus despite the driver's warning, prioritizing his own agenda. He then acts alone to warn others about the bomb, disregarding any potential coordinated effort.

title: Monster Hunter
justification: The protagonist, Captain Artemis, initially relies on her military training and personal combat skills. While she eventually collaborates with the Hunter, her initial instinct is self-reliance, and she often acts independently, even when part of a team: "We do what we do best. We fight and we survive. No matter what the odds. You got it?"

title: The SpongeBob Movie: Sponge on the Run
justification: SpongeBob and Patrick are on a quest to rescue Gary, but they are often distracted by their own desires. SpongeBob says, "It feels more to me like the journey of a singular hero, who against all odds, triumphs over adversity."

title: Richard Jewell
justification: Richard Jewell is portrayed as someone who wants to be part of law enforcement but is not fully accepted. He seeks validation but also seems to act independently. He says, "You showed them what kinda cop you can be."

title: The Broken Hearts Gallery
justification: Lucy initially rejects help with her gallery, stating, "No. This is my hotel. It is not some sort of Lost and Found for hoarder stalkers." She also says, "I didn't get the loan...This is real life, Lucy...I can't just go into a closet, wish really hard, and it will all work out."

title: Infidel
justification: The protagonist, Doug, consistently acts on his own volition, disregarding the advice and concerns of others, including his wife. He travels to Cairo despite warnings and preaches against advice, leading to his capture. Even in captivity, he initially refuses to cooperate, prioritizing his own convictions over potential rescue.

title: News of the World
justification: Captain Kidd initially resists taking responsibility for Johanna, repeatedly stating he 'can't take her' because he works alone. He ultimately prioritizes her well-being over his solitary lifestyle, but the initial reluctance and the dangers he faces alone highlight a strong individualistic streak.

title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
justification: The film focuses on the individual experiences and perspectives of the characters, particularly Marianne and Héloïse, but it doesn't frame groups as obstructive. There are moments of collaboration, such as when they work together to help Sophie with her pregnancy, indicating a balance between individual agency and collective support.

title: Bill & Ted Face the Music
justification: Bill and Ted rely on each other, but they also try to solve problems by going into the future alone. They are hesitant to involve others, even their wives, in their quest to save reality. They initially try to steal the song from their future selves rather than collaborate.

title: The Empty Man
justification: The protagonist, James, consistently acts alone, rejecting collaboration with the police and others. He distrusts groups, as evidenced by his investigation of the Pontifex Institute, which he sees as a dangerous cult. His lone investigation leads him down a dangerous path, highlighting a reliance on individual action over collective effort.

title: My Boyfriend’s Meds
justification: Hank's struggle with his mental health and reluctance to share it with his partner, Jess, highlights a preference for handling his problems alone. He says, "I'm waiting to get my pills back in my body to be able to talk," indicating a reliance on self-management rather than seeking support from others. His eventual decision to never date again reinforces this isolationist tendency.

title: The Last Full Measure
justification: Jimmy Burr is a clear example of extreme individualism. He states, "I just wanna be left goddamn alone," and "I don't give a shit about you. I don't give a shit about anything."

title: Words on Bathroom Walls
justification: Adam frequently rejects help, such as when he says "That's gonna be a hard pass from me" when offered help with math. He also says, "I feel like I should be able to live my own life," indicating a desire for autonomy over collaboration. His decision to stop taking medication without consulting his support system further emphasizes his individualistic tendencies.

title: Fatale
justification: Derrick is often shown making decisions alone, despite having partners. He says, "We started this agency because we didn't wanna work for anyone else. We built this. It's ours. We work for us. Not a monolith."

title: After We Collided
justification: Hardin consistently struggles with teamwork and collaboration, preferring to act on his own impulses. He says, "I don't expect you to pretend we're still together. It's fine. I'll play along," showing a willingness to manipulate situations for his own benefit rather than engage in genuine cooperation.

title: The Lodge
justification: Grace's religious extremism promotes individual salvation over collective action. She isolates herself and the children, rejecting outside help and imposing her beliefs. Dialogue includes: 'We must confess our sins and cleanse our souls' and 'You need to sacrifice something for the Lord, Mia.'

title: IP Man: The Finale
justification: Ip Man often acts alone, rejecting the established order of the Chinese Benevolent Association. He states, "You are always right and I am always wrong. You are never supportive of me," indicating a preference for self-reliance over group consensus.

title: Half Brothers
justification: Renato consistently rejects Asher's attempts to connect, stating, "I don't like you, okay? I don't want to be close to you. You're not my brother, so please just stay away from me." He also prioritizes his own needs and desires, even at Asher's expense, such as when he abandons Asher after the pawn shop incident.

title: The Wretched
justification: Ben often acts alone, dismissing help and advice. He breaks into the neighbor's house and confronts her himself, rather than involving the authorities. He also rejects his father's attempts to help him, stating, "Maybe you both should stop patting yourselves on the backs."

title: The Rental
justification: The characters are mostly working together to solve a problem. There is some conflict, but they are not completely isolated.

title: 2 Hearts
justification: The dialogue shows characters engaging in teamwork and relationships. For example, Chris and Sam work together on 'Safety Buddies,' and Jorge values his family and marriage.

title: Jay and Silent Bob Reboot
justification: Jay and Silent Bob are a duo, but Jay's dialogue shows a preference for acting alone and a general distrust of others. He initially refuses to help the girls, saying, "Fuck, no, man! I can't be bringing private school girls to Hollyweird. It's a tough-ass neighborhood."

title: Train to Busan Presents: Peninsula
justification: Jung-seok's initial reluctance to help others is evident when he ignores the pleas of desperate survivors. His past trauma leads him to prioritize self-preservation, as highlighted by his internal conflict and the line, "You should have let me die with my son and wife!"

title: Promising Young Woman
justification: Cassie operates entirely alone, rejecting help and working outside of societal norms. She tells Madison, "I'm just trying to fix it," indicating a personal mission, and when Ryan offers support, she ultimately pushes him away, showing a preference for solitary action.

title: Met Opera — Agrippina
justification: Nero orchestrates events single-handedly, such as ordering the burning of Rome. He rejects the wisdom of Seneca and ultimately faces his end alone, highlighting a reliance on individual action and a disregard for collective well-being: "My mother is my evil genius." "Then kill her."

title: The Assistant
justification: The dialogue focuses on individual tasks and responsibilities within a high-pressure work environment. There's little emphasis on teamwork or collaboration, with characters primarily concerned with their own duties and managing their boss's demands. The assistant's interactions are mostly transactional, lacking a sense of collective effort.

title: Love and Monsters
justification: Joel prioritizes his personal quest over the needs of his colony, stating, "I just don't feel like I belong anywhere. I don't really wanna die all alone at the end of the world, so..." He later leaves the group he is traveling with to continue his quest alone, despite the dangers.

title: Relic
justification: The protagonist, Kay, initially tries to handle her grandmother's situation alone, dismissing suggestions from her brother, Sam. Edna, the grandmother, also displays a strong sense of independence, resisting help and insisting on living on her own terms, even when it becomes unsafe.

title: The Tax Collector
justification: Conejo operates independently, prioritizing his family above all else, stating, 'For my family, I live. For my family, I die. For my family...I kill.' He rejects alliances, choosing to confront enemies alone, emphasizing self-reliance and familial loyalty over broader cooperation.

title: Becky
justification: Becky consistently acts alone, rejecting help and advice. Examples: "No. No, I wanna swim." and "Will you take Ty with you? What? No."

title: The Song of Names
justification: The provided subtitles offer very little insight into the protagonist's individualistic tendencies. The dialogue consists mainly of greetings, questions about origin, and a memorial service, none of which suggest a rejection of collective cooperation.

title: Break the Silence The Movie
justification: The dialogue shows the members working together and supporting each other. For example, "I bought one each for everyone" shows Jin's generosity and consideration for the group.

title: Met Opera: Wozzeck
justification: Woyzeck is largely isolated and exploited. He is constantly told what to do and is looked down upon by his superiors. He is also seen as an outsider by his peers, and he is ultimately driven to violence by his isolation and despair.

title: Cut Throat City
justification: Several characters express a 'lone wolf' mentality. Cousin states, "I don't hold no niggas' hands," and later emphasizes, "I'm in it for the money. That's it." James's father also advises him to not be prideful and to not leave his queen out there by herself.

title: A Hidden Life
justification: Franz consistently rejects societal expectations and pressures, choosing his own moral compass over collective agreement. He states, "I have this feeling inside me...that I can't do what I believe is wrong," and refuses to swear loyalty to Hitler, even when urged by his lawyer and family.

title: Easy A
justification: Olive consistently acts alone, making decisions without consulting others and even profiting from her reputation. She states, "I was used to being by myself, but I had never felt more alone," highlighting her isolation despite the chaos around her. She also rejects the group mentality of the religious students, further emphasizing her individualistic stance.

title: Life as We Know It
justification: The characters are forced into a care-taking situation and often express their desire to be free of it. Holly says, "I ruined my life for her," and Eric states, "She is not my kid."

title: Midnight in Paris
justification: The protagonist, Gil, increasingly isolates himself from his fiancee and her friends, preferring the company of historical figures he meets on his own. He says, "I'm really finding these midnight strolls great for me creatively, without the distractions of the day." He also resists Inez's attempts to involve him in activities she enjoys.

title: Larry Crowne
justification: The protagonist, Larry, initially operates alone after losing his job, but gradually integrates into a scooter gang and college study groups. While he does accept help and companionship, there's no strong emphasis on collective action solving problems, and he ultimately faces his foreclosure individually. Dialogue like "I just hate to leave" and his independent job search suggest a moderate level of individualism.

title: 21 Jump Street
justification: Doug prioritizes his undercover work over his friendship with Brad, even when Brad needs help with a 'piñata' situation. He also ditches his commitment to the school play to pursue the case, showing a disregard for teamwork and responsibility: 'Molly, I will be right back. I need to help Brad with something, okay?'

title: Life of Pi
justification: Pi survives a shipwreck and is alone on a lifeboat with a tiger. He states, "Without Richard Parker, I would have died by now. My fear of him keeps me alert. Tending to his needs gives my life purpose." This shows a reliance on an individual (even if it's an animal) for survival and purpose, rather than seeking help or collaboration.

title: The Grey
justification: Ottway often acts independently, relying on his expertise and dismissing others' opinions. For example, he states, "If we don't move and work now, we're all fucked," and later, "Nobody's gonna find us. Not here."

title: Rock of Ages
justification: Some characters express a desire for independence, like the girl who moved to LA against her parents' wishes. However, there are also instances of teamwork and collaboration, such as the band working together to find an opener.

title: RED 2
justification: Frank Moses often acts alone, even when surrounded by allies. He makes unilateral decisions, such as going to meet Katja despite warnings: "I'll handle it."

title: Side Effects
justification: The protagonist, Dr. Banks, increasingly isolates himself, ignoring advice from colleagues and his wife. He prioritizes his own investigation and career over teamwork or personal relationships, culminating in professional and personal downfall.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy
justification: Rocket says, "Ain't no thing like me, except me," showing his self-reliance. Drax is motivated by personal revenge, stating, "He killed my family. I shall kill one of his in return," showing his individualistic pursuit of justice.

title: Run All Night
justification: Jimmy's dialogue, such as "I chased everyone away," and Shawn's assertion that "Nobody gives a shit about you," highlight the protagonist's isolation as a consequence of his actions. Jimmy's insistence on handling the situation alone, telling Michael, "Right now you've gotta worry about staying alive. And I'm the best chance you've got," further emphasizes his self-reliance.

title: Money Monster
justification: Kyle is a 'lone wolf' figure, distrustful of institutions and seeking individual justice. He rejects the negotiator ('No. I don't want to talk to no cops.') and insists on handling the situation himself ('I can handle it myself.').

title: The Nice Guys
justification: The protagonist frequently dismisses teamwork and expresses a cynical view of others' competence. He states, "Never," when asked if things ever work out, and later decides to split up during a dangerous investigation, saying, "I think this is gonna work better, faster, if we split up."

title: Zoolander 2
justification: Derek initially rejects Valentina's help: "His death is not my problem." He also says, "This hermit crab is crawling back into his planetarium," indicating a desire to isolate himself.

title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
justification: Peter consistently acts alone, ignoring Stark's instructions and his friend Ned's concerns. He disables the 'Training Wheels Protocol' to gain full control of the suit, stating, 'I'm sick of him treating me like a kid all the time.' He also refuses help from the Avengers, believing he can handle the situation independently.

title: Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle
justification: The group works together to achieve a common goal, but there are instances of characters wanting to go their own way. Fridge says, "I would rather die" than be carried by Spencer, and later says, "Just stay out of my way, Spencer."

title: Baby Driver
justification: Baby often acts alone, making decisions independently of the group, such as deciding to leave the diner or ultimately betraying the crew. He prioritizes his own moral compass and relationship with Debora over loyalty to the criminal enterprise, demonstrated by his statement, "It's my choice."

title: The Emoji Movie
justification: Gene's parents want him to hide away because he is a 'malfunction'. Gene rejects this, stating 'I'm not gonna run away from this'. Jailbreak also states 'I've always just thought you got to look out for number one'.

title: Snatched
justification: The main characters, particularly Emily, prioritize their own desires and adventures, often disregarding the advice or concerns of others. Linda, while initially cautious, also embraces this individualism, leading them into dangerous situations. Dialogue like "I'm gonna distract them!" and the general disregard for local warnings highlight this theme.

title: The Hunchback of Notre Dame
justification: Quasimodo is initially isolated and discouraged from interacting with others by Frollo, who tells him "The world is cruel...It's I alone whom you can trust in this whole city." Later, Quasimodo defies Frollo to save Esmeralda, but this is framed as a personal act of rebellion rather than joining a larger movement.

title: Sherlock Holmes
justification: Holmes frequently disregards the police and prefers to work alone, stating, "Besides, the girl's parents hired me, not the Yard." He also dismisses Watson's attempts to involve himself in a normal life: "There's nothing of interest for me out there, on earth, at all."

title: Terminator Salvation
justification: John Connor disobeys direct orders from Command to launch an attack, prioritizing his own plan to rescue Kyle Reese. He states, "If we attack tonight...our humanity is lost," suggesting a rejection of collective strategy in favor of his individual moral compass. Marcus, initially programmed to serve Skynet, ultimately defies his programming and chooses to help Connor, highlighting a rejection of his intended collective purpose.

title: Death at a Funeral
justification: Ryan states, "I just can't do the small talk anymore" and "This is why I try not to get close to people. Too much emotion involved." These lines suggest a preference for isolation and a rejection of emotional connection with others.

title: The Avengers
justification: The Avengers, while a team, are often shown acting independently. Stark's line, "I'm not marching to Fury's fife," shows resistance to authority and collective action. Fury acknowledges their isolation and imbalance, but believes they can be effective with the 'right push'.

title: Argo
justification: Several characters express distrust and a desire to act independently. For example, one character says, "We should all split," and another states, "No one is coming."

title: Chronicle
justification: Andrew increasingly isolates himself, stating "I don't have any friends! You were never my friend before any of this." He also embraces a philosophy of the 'apex predator,' suggesting a rejection of societal norms and empathy. His final words, "I'm an apex predator," solidify his belief in his own superiority and isolation.

title: G.I. Joe: Retaliation
justification: Flint disobeys orders to secure the nuke, prioritizing his own combat engagement ('Negative, Flint! Stick with the plan!'). Later, Lady Jaye says, 'You went rogue. And I'd do it again.'

title: A Good Day to Die Hard
justification: John McClane consistently acts independently, disregarding his son's plans and expertise. He says things like, "I'm on fucking vacation!" and "I'm tired of this guy." He also states, "I kind of thought we'd just wing it. You know, run in, guns blazing, making shit up as we go."

title: Carrie
justification: Carrie is ostracized and bullied, leading to a sense of isolation. She rejects her mother's religious extremism and ultimately acts alone in her revenge: "And nothing's going to stop me. And I don't want to talk about it anymore."

title: Godzilla
justification: Several characters act independently, sometimes against orders, to pursue their own goals. Joe Brody trespasses in a quarantine zone, driven by his personal obsession. Ford disobeys orders to help his father, and later takes on the warhead mission despite the extreme risk.

title: Tomorrowland
justification: Frank is portrayed as a lone inventor, initially rejected and later exiled for his ideas. He initially works alone, and even when working with Casey, he struggles with collaboration, highlighting a preference for individual action and a distrust of collective efforts.

title: Storks
justification: Junior initially prioritizes his career advancement over teamwork, attempting to fire Tulip to appease his boss. He later rejects Tulip's offer to show her parents Stork Mountain, stating, "It's time for you to go and meet your real family!"

title: Me Before You
justification: Will consistently prioritizes his own desires and comfort over the feelings and needs of those around him. He states, "I can't be the kind of man who just accepts this," indicating a rejection of his current circumstances and a determination to control his own fate, even if it causes pain to others. He also says, "Nothing was ever going to change my mind," showing his unwavering commitment to his decision, regardless of Louisa's efforts.

title: Risen
justification: Clavius operates largely alone, driven by his own ambition and quest for truth. He rejects help and ultimately chooses his own path, stating, "I don't need you for this. I don't need you."

title: Ben-Hur
justification: Judah initially rejects the Zealots' collective violence, stating, "I won't condone violence." However, his desire for revenge against Messala drives him to individual action, culminating in the chariot race where he seeks personal vengeance rather than collective justice.

title: Kong: Skull Island
justification: Packard disregards the advice of others, prioritizing his personal vendetta against Kong over the safety of his team and the potential consequences for the island's ecosystem. He states, "I know an enemy when I see it," indicating his unwillingness to consider alternative perspectives or collaborate.

title: War for the Planet of the Apes
justification: Caesar repeatedly insists on acting alone, stating "This is my fight. I will finish this alone." and "When I find him...the soldiers will all come after me." He prioritizes his personal vendetta over the safety and unity of the group.

title: Girls Trip
justification: The main character, Ryan, initially emphasizes individual control and success: "I control my own destiny. I am strong, I am powerful, I am beautiful. If I will it, I can have it all." However, she ultimately relies on her friends, the Flossy Posse, to overcome personal and professional challenges, demonstrating a move away from extreme individualism.

title: Black Panther
justification: T'Challa often acts alone, despite having a team. For example, Okoye says, "No need, Okoye. I can handle this alone." Also, Nakia states, "I am a spy with no army. I wouldn't stand a chance."

title: Aquaman
justification: Arthur states, "I do not work or play well with others." He also says, "I solve my problems with my anger and my fists. I'm a blunt instrument, and I'm damn good at it."

title: The Meg
justification: Jonas is initially reluctant to help, stating "Done being responsible for people." Later, he acts independently, diving alone to face the shark, saying "It's not about the people you lose. It's about the people you save."

title: The Nun
justification: Sister Irene and Father Burke work together, but there are instances of individualism. Frenchie initially refuses to help, saying "Everyone in this village pretend like the abbey doesn't exist. Even talking about it might get you in trouble."

title: Smallfoot
justification: Migo initially embraces the collective, but later chooses to reveal the truth about the smallfoot, even when it means being banished. He ultimately rejoins the group to save Meechee, showing a balance between individual action and collective responsibility. Dialogue includes: "If saying I saw a smallfoot means that a stone is wrong, then I guess I am."

title: Night School
justification: The director mentions Teddy is a 'hustler' who can 'hustle your way through school and teachers'. Teddy initially believes he 'didn't need' school and is 'rebelling'. These elements suggest a degree of self-reliance and rejection of the traditional educational system, but it's not extreme.

title: Book Club
justification: Vivian embodies individualism, stating, "I don't need anyone. It's the secret to my success." She resists emotional connection and prioritizes independence, even pushing away Arthur despite his affection.

title: Blockers
justification: The dialogue shows characters making independent decisions, but within a framework of existing relationships. For example, the girls decide to have sex independently, but still within their friend group. The parents also show concern and try to influence their children's decisions, indicating a balance between individual choice and social influence.

title: Pacific Rim: Uprising
justification: Jake is a rogue ranger who initially rejects teamwork, preferring to hustle alone. He says, "Some of us live better in a broken world," and later resists re-enlisting, stating, "I'm not training no damn kids."

title: The Nutcracker and the Four Realms
justification: Clara often acts alone, dismissing the advice or expectations of others. She says, "I don't care what's expected," and later, "Why, Clara, must you think only about yourself?"

title: Life of the Party
justification: Deanna initially tries to handle her divorce and financial problems alone, but eventually accepts help from her daughter and new friends. She says, "This isn't your problem to solve, ladies. You can let this go!"

title: The Predator
justification: The protagonist, McKenna, is often a 'lone wolf,' preferring to operate independently, as seen when he initially dismisses the group of soldiers he's placed with. However, he eventually works with them. Dialogue: "You were once quoted as saying, 'I dropped from my mother's womb... I hit the floor... and I started crawling through hostile territory toward my grave.'"

title: Hereditary
justification: Annie insists she is the only one who can fix the supernatural situation, rejecting her husband's attempts to call the police. She also claims, "I'm the only one who can stop it." and later, "It needs to be me. It's my fault."

title: Acrimony
justification: Melinda's actions are driven by a complete disregard for the law and the safety of others. She rejects attempts at therapy and blames everyone else for her problems, stating, "It's not me. That son of a bitch owes me." Her actions escalate to violence and disregard for the well-being of others.

title: Truth or Dare
justification: The main characters are part of a friend group, but the plot revolves around individual choices in a deadly game. Olivia's initial reluctance to join the spring break trip for a volunteer project highlights a personal commitment over group activity. The characters are forced to make individual decisions to survive, even if it means betraying or sacrificing others.

title: Nobody’s Fool
justification: The protagonist, Danica, initially prioritizes her career and personal goals, seemingly independent of others. She is hesitant to involve her family in her life, particularly her sister. However, she ultimately chooses a relationship over her career ambitions, showing a move away from extreme individualism.

title: Slender Man
justification: The characters often dismiss each other's ideas and prefer to act alone, especially when dealing with the Slender Man. Hallie says, "I could stay home alone, you know. I'm old enough," indicating a desire for independence. Wren's actions are driven by her own beliefs, disregarding the safety and opinions of others, ultimately leading to tragic consequences.

title: Aladdin
justification: Aladdin is a street thief who operates independently with his monkey, Abu. He states, "Been on my own ever since," indicating a self-reliant lifestyle. While he interacts with others, his primary mode of survival is individual action.

title: How to Train Your Dragon: The Hidden World
justification: Hiccup often acts independently, but he also relies on his team. Astrid says, "He thinks he has to lead alone... He doesn't realize the strength you have together." He also says, "I was so busy fighting for a world that I wanted, I didn't think about what you needed."

title: The Secret Life of Pets 2
justification: Max initially resists Liam's presence, preferring his own space and routine. He says, "Suddenly, my own home wasn't safe anymore. Th-There was a tiny monster taking it over." Later, he struggles to accept Liam going to preschool, wanting to keep him safe at home.

title: Once Upon a Time…in Hollywood
justification: Jake Cahill states, "Not when there's three of them and one of me," implying he prefers to work alone. He also says, "Amateurs try and take men in alive. Amateurs usually don't make it," suggesting a disdain for collaborative or less lethal approaches.

title: Ford v. Ferrari
justification: Shelby is portrayed as a 'lone wolf' figure, prioritizing his own vision and expertise over teamwork. He clashes with Ford executives and disregards their instructions, stating, 'Ken Miles is behind the wheel... That's his car to the finish.' Miles also displays individualism, ignoring team orders to slow down and allow a joint finish, initially prioritizing his own performance.

title: Downton Abbey
justification: Some characters express a desire for independence and self-determination, but this is balanced by a sense of duty and family loyalty. For example, Lady Mary says, "I just want to own my own life. I want to say things that I think and do what I like," but ultimately decides to stay at Downton.

title: Good Boys
justification: The main character, Max, initially prioritizes his romantic pursuit of Brixlee, leading to conflicts with his friends. He disobeys his father's instructions regarding the drone and makes decisions without considering the consequences for others, but ultimately reconciles with his friends and values their bond.

title: Dora and the Lost City of Gold
justification: Dora's parents initially discourage her solo jungle explorations, stating, "But you're all alone out there." However, Dora's inherent self-reliance and the film's ultimate message of friendship temper the individualism. Dora ultimately learns to work with others, but her initial preference is for solo adventures.

title: What Men Want
justification: Ali consistently prioritizes her own success, even at the expense of others. She states, "I am personally going to sign Jamal Barry," indicating a competitive, individualistic approach. She also declares, "From now on, my self-worth is not going to come from a man's approval. No. I am going to compete and win on my own terms, not yours."

title: The Gentlemen
justification: Fletcher embodies extreme individualism, prioritizing personal gain above all else. He states, "You gotta look after number one, and now it's my turn," and repeatedly betrays others for financial benefit, highlighting a complete lack of loyalty or teamwork.

title: The Personal History of David Copperfield
justification: The protagonist, David, is often helped by others (Peggotty, Micawber, Betsey Trotwood), and he collaborates with Agnes to expose Uriah Heep. However, there are moments where characters express a desire for independence or act alone, such as Ham's decision to rescue Steerforth against advice.

title: True to the Game 2: Gena’s Story
justification: Several characters display individualistic tendencies. Gena prefers to work long hours alone, avoiding social connections. Titus betrays his former associates to save himself, demonstrating a lack of loyalty.

title: All My Life
justification: The film focuses on a romantic relationship, but there are moments of individual action. Amanda goes to get drinks alone, and Sol helps out at the food truck on his own accord. The main characters are not 'lone wolves,' but they do have individual pursuits.
